title: Graded-Edge Rakotch Contractions in Generalized Metric Spaces with Weighted Graphs
abstract: We introduce the notion of graded-edge Rakotch contraction mappings on a generalized metric space with a weighted graph. We prove that the successive iterate of every starting point converge uniformly to a common limit, which is the unique fixed point. We derive an explicit iteration-complexity bound and, under a relaxed triangle inequality, a geometric rate whose constant is the graph invariant. Finally, we illustrate the theory on an explicit real graded contraction that realizes the interior optimum, on a quadratic integral equation, and on finite weighted digraphs.

title: Irreducible Representations as Local Maxima of a Matrix-Coefficient Functional
abstract: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional unitary representation of a finite group $G$ and, for unit vectors $v$, let $Φ(v)$ be the mean of $|\langle v,gv\rangle|^2$ over $g\in G$. We show that $v$ is a local maximum of $Φ$ if and only if the subrepresentation generated by $v$ is irreducible. Thus local maximization of $Φ$ extracts irreducible subrepresentations of $V$ directly, with no character or isotypic projection specified in advance. The proof is elementary: Schur averaging reduces it to a singular-value calculation. The values and dimensions of the connected components of the local-maximum set determine the degrees and multiplicities of the irreducible constituents, and for $H\leq G$ the intersections of the $G$- and $H$-local-maximal loci encode branching multiplicities. We also determine the critical landscape and give a normalized gradient iteration whose generic limit generates an irreducible subrepresentation.

title: Parabolic frequency and backward uniqueness on compact Finsler metric measure spaces
abstract: We establish monotonicity formulas for parabolic frequency functions on closed Finsler metric measure spaces with fixed or evolving metrics and measures. When the reference measure is fixed, an integral bound on the metric variation yields monotonicity for the Finsler heat equation. For coupled metric measure flows, we construct positive global supersolutions and subsolutions of a linearized conjugate heat equation from local radial barriers. These weights define a frequency function whose monotonicity follows from an integral bound involving the metric variation and the change in weighted Ricci curvature. For parabolic equations with a source controlled by the solution and its gradient, we obtain a differential inequality for the frequency and prove that a solution vanishing at the terminal time must vanish throughout the preceding interval. The proof controls the comparison of the two weights through an energy quotient computed with the subsolution measure.

title: A Positively Curved Seven-Manifold Without Effective Smooth Circle Actions
abstract: We construct a compact Riemannian manifold $M$ with strictly positive sectional curvature and prove that $M$ admits no effective smooth $S^{1}$-action, which yields to a counterexample of a longstanding conjecture attributed to Yau.

title: On the multivariate hypergeometric function $F_K^{(L)}$, I
abstract: In recent years, a new multivariate hypergeometric series, known as the comb function, has attracted attention in physics, particularly in the study of conformal blocks in conformal field theory. This function can be regarded as a further generalization of Appell's function $F_2$ and Saran's function $F_K$. However, except for a few known formulas, little is known about its properties. In this paper, we study its fundamental properties from a mathematical perspective, such as the region of convergence, reduction formulas, an Euler-type integral representation, and decomposition formulas. Some directions for future research and connections with other multivariate hypergeometric series originating from physics are also mentioned.

title: Strong unique continuation on Riemannian manifolds for degenerate elliptic operators with convexified weights
abstract: In this manuscript, we consider a degenerate elliptic equation on a Riemannian manifold whose weight vanishes at an interior point $p$, and prove the strong unique continuation property (SUCP) at $p$. The curved setting gives rise to intrinsic geometric error terms that obstruct the analytic estimates available in the Euclidean case. To overcome this, we introduce a convexified radial weight that restores coercivity in the Carleman commutator. Combining the resulting Carleman estimate with a Hardy-type inequality and a Caccioppoli inequality, we show that any weak solution vanishing to infinite order at the degeneracy point must be identically zero on the connected domain. This result is the first SUCP theorem for this class of degenerate operators on general Riemannian manifolds.

title: Sharp Logarithmic Bounds for Vilenkin-Fejér Kernels
abstract:
Let $G_m$ be a bounded Vilenkin group and put $R:=\sup_j m_j$. We prove the sharp uniform estimate
  $$\|K_n\|_1\leq \frac{17}{15\ln 2}\ln R,\qquad n\geq1,$$
  for the Fejér kernels associated with the Vilenkin system. The constant $17/(15\ln2)$ is best possible. In the Walsh--Paley case $R=2$, the result reduces exactly to Toledo's sharp estimate $\sup_n\|K_n\|_1=17/15$.

title: On the Seven-particle Clusters of Lennard-Jones and Thomson
abstract: In this Letter, we develop a graph-geometric framework and prove that the pentagonal bipyramid (PBP) is the unique global minimiser of both the seven-particle Lennard-Jones energy in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the seven-charge Thomson energy on $S^2$, up to rigid symmetries and particle relabelling. For the Thomson problem, this strengthens a recent deterministic global-optimality certificate to numerical tolerance into an exact global-optimality and uniqueness theorem. A weak-interaction graph, defined by thresholding pair geometry, organises configuration space without imposing symmetry or discarding any pair interaction. For Lennard-Jones, pair-energy counting, graph classification, subset bounds, and force balance reduce all possible minimisers to 29 bounded domains; exact geometric certificates exclude 28, localise the survivor near the PBP, and a uniform restoring-energy estimate proves uniqueness. The Thomson proof follows the same progression: graph reduction, geometric localisation, and rigidity, but finalises through whole-domain coercivity and a global localisation theorem. The same fivefold order therefore emerges in two very different physical settings: an unconstrained cluster with a preferred bond length and purely repelling charges confined to a sphere, showing a common geometric organising principle for seven particles that is not tied to either interaction.

title: Linear Convergence of Nesterov's Acceleration for All Momentum Parameter
abstract: We study the convergence rate of the Nesetrov's accelerated proximal gradient method for a smooth, strongly convex composite minimization objective across a range of value of the momentum extrapolation. The literature proves a convergence rate of the method for a specific momentum extrapolation parameter choice based on the knowledge of strong convexity and Lipschitz smoothness constants. For the heavy ball method it is established that every choice of the momentum parameter either fails to accelerate or fails to converge on the same function class. We prove in this paper that a range of Nesterov style constant momentum extrapolation parameters produces a linear convergence rate. We corroborate these results numerically via performance estimation which computes a method's exact worst case rate as a semidefinite program.

title: Statistical Geometry of Group Actions: Symmetry, Transport, Estimation
abstract: We study variational inference in the presence of distributional symmetry, focusing on the interaction between two distinct group actions on a sample space: a symmetry action that leaves a reference distribution invariant, and a transport action that generates a parametric variational family by pushforward. By analyzing the algebraic structure of the total transformation group generated by both actions and the induced adjoint representation of the symmetry group on the transport Lie algebra, we establish that the Riemannian gradient of the Kullback--Leibler divergence at the true transport parameter is constrained to lie in the trivial representation of the symmetry group. Consequently, symmetry forces the gradient to vanish along all non-trivial representations. Combining this representation-theoretic constraint with parameter identifiability yields an orthogonal decomposition of the transport Lie algebra into three interpretable subspaces: an identifiability kernel (along which the objective is locally constant), a bias subspace (where the gradient may be nonzero due to model misspecification), and a symmetry-breaking subspace (where the gradient is forced to vanish by symmetry alone). Finally, we characterize the residual bias directions in terms of distributional mismatch between the base model and the standardized target, and derive an explicit Stein-type moment-matching condition that eliminates this bias, extending the location-scale results of (Margossian and Saul, 2025) to general Lie group transformation families.

title: An elliptic deformation of continued fractions
abstract: We construct an elliptic deformation $\mathcal{Q}_{a,b;q,p}(x)$ of positive rational numbers $x$ by attaching Schlosser's small elliptic weights $w_{a,b;q,p}(s,t)$ to prefixes of Stern--Brocot words. On positive integers $n$ it gives Schlosser's elliptic numbers $[n]_{a,b;q,p}$. Parameter shifts realize $x \mapsto x+1$ and $x \mapsto x/(x+1)$, while a reciprocal parameter transformation gives an inversion formula. The Gaussian degeneration recovers the $q$-deformed rationals of Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko. The regular and negative elliptic continued fractions agree, since they evaluate the same word with the same ordered weights. The numerator and denominator satisfy weighted Farey recursions and, for rationals greater than $1$, are the closure polynomials, or quiver $F$-polynomials, of the associated oriented type-$A$ quivers. Finally, we express the vertex weights as normalized elliptic Euler expressions of balanced virtual torus representations.

title: A singular homeomorphism between Pierce expansions and continued fraction expansions
abstract: In this paper, we study the map $Θ$ which sends each $x\in[0,1]$ to the number whose continued fraction digits are the first Pierce expansion digit of $x$ and the gaps between two consecutive Pierce expansion digits of $x$. We investigate the regularity of $Θ$ and $Θ^{-1}$, including the optimal Hölder exponent of $Θ^{-1}$, and the local and Hausdorff dimensions of the push-forwards of the Lebesgue measure under $Θ$ and $Θ^{-1}$. We also study the differentiability of $Θ$ at rational and irrational points, and calculate the Hausdorff dimension of the set of points at which $Θ$ has an infinite derivative.

title: Positivity Improving Quantum Markov Operators
abstract: A Markov operator on a matrix algebra, that is, a unital completely positive map, is called positivity improving if it maps every nonzero positive element to an invertible one. This is the noncommutative counterpart of a stochastic matrix with strictly positive entries. We show that positivity improvement is self-dual and equivalent to a faithful quantum Markov--Dobrushin--Doeblin minorization. We also compare the scalar trace minorization with the optimal common-lower-bound construction of the quantum Markov--Dobrushin coefficient. We then characterize positivity improvement through the Kraus space of the map: a Markov operator is positivity improving if and only if the Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal complement of its Kraus space contains no operator of rank one. As a consequence the Kraus rank of a positivity improving Markov operator on the algebra of $d\times d$ matrices is at least $2d-1$, and an explicit Hankel-type channel shows that this bound is attained in every dimension. Although deciding positivity improvement is NP-hard in general, we obtain complete and effectively checkable classifications for qubits and qutrits, together with families of examples (Pauli, Weyl and Werner--Holevo channels) showing that all our estimates are optimal. Finally we show that, in infinite dimensions, positivity improvement no longer implies any contraction of the Markov operator.

title: Multivariate Pellarin $L$-values on algebraic curves
abstract: We establish a generating trace formula for multicharacter ideal-type $L$-values associated with rank-one Drinfeld modules. For a sign-normalized Hayes module with free period lattice, the formula realizes the $L$-values at weights $n\equiv s\pmod{q^{°_\infty}-1}$ as a trace over the ordinary Hilbert class field. We further characterize the polynomials in the exponential variable $X$ arising in multicharacter lattice generating identities over arbitrary function rings. Their coefficients are given explicitly via the shtuka basis, which gives concrete control over their supports and degrees. This completely settles an open problem of Pellarin and Perkins: these polynomials are all constant if and only if $s<2q$. The results on coefficients apply to curves of arbitrary genus, infinite places of arbitrary degree, and nonprincipal period lattices.

title: Geometric Stochastic Dynamics and Fokker-Planck Equation on $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$
abstract: This paper develops a geometric (coordinate-free) stochastic model of a controlled point mass evolving on the unit two-sphere $\mathbb S^2$, together with the Fokker-Planck equation governing the probability density of the resulting stochastic process. The state manifold is the tangent bundle $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$. The Levi-Civita connection of the round metric is used to construct the horizontal-vertical splitting of $\mathsf{T}(\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2)$ and to convert the intrinsic second-order dynamics of the system into a first-order controlled vector field on $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$. Endowing the tangent bundle with the Sasaki metric then permits stochastic perturbations to be introduced intrinsically and independently in horizontal, i.e., position, and vertical, i.e., velocity, directions. The corresponding infinitesimal generator is obtained in horizontal-vertical Hessian form. The probability density is defined with respect to the Sasaki Riemannian volume measure. The Fokker-Planck equation is derived intrinsically in both Stratonovich and Itô forms. In the Itô representation, a globally defined horizontal-vertical diffusion tensor yields a compact double-divergence Fokker-Planck PDE. No coordinates or embedded Euclidean representation of the sphere dynamics are used in the development. Numerical simulations illustrate the stochastic motion of a controlled particle ensemble on $\mathbb S^2$ toward an antipodal target configuration.

title: A Zero-Free Sum of Cauchy Kernels with Positive Coefficients
abstract:
We construct a zero-free meromorphic function \[
  f(z)=\sum_n\frac{c_n}{z-a_n},\qquad
  c_n>0,\qquad |a_n|\to\infty,\qquad
  \sum_{a_n\ne0}\frac{c_n}{|a_n|}<\infty, \] thereby disproving the Clunie--Eremenko--Rossi conjecture. The construction starts from a product of two rotated Airy functions. The zeros of this product are shifted simultaneously so that all residues of $f$ are positive. The poles lie on the rays $e^{\pm iπ/3}[0,\infty)$. The resulting function has order and lower order $3/2$, and the sum of its residues in the disc $|z|\le r$ is asymptotic to $\frac{4}{3π}r^{3/4}$.

title: Zeroth-Order Langevin Dynamics for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization: Curvature Regularization and Non-Asymptotic Guarantees
abstract: Zeroth-order methods provide a way to optimize stochastic nonconvex objectives using only noisy function evaluations. However, the smoothing inherent in their gradient estimators effectively modifies the objective being optimized. In particular, Gaussian smoothing with smoothing parameter $η>0$ induces, to leading order, an implicit Hessian-trace regularization, which motivates the study of the curvature-regularized objective of the form $f(x)+(η^2/2) tr(\nabla^2 f(x))$. We develop a non-asymptotic theory in the nonconvex setting for a class of algorithms called stochastic zeroth-order Langevin dynamics (ZOLD), which use only noisy function evaluations and do not have access to first- or higher-order derivative information, and derive excess-risk guarantees for the curvature-regularized objective. We first control the finite-time distribution of the ZOLD iterates in Wasserstein distance with respect to the Gibbs measure associated with the Gaussian-smoothed objective. An explicit coupling between the smoothing and inverse temperature parameters then quantifies the proximity of this measure to the Gibbs measure associated with the corresponding Hessian-trace-regularized objective. These distributional estimates in Wasserstein distance lead to excess-risk bounds for the curvature-regularized objective. Our analysis accommodates assumptions under which the stochastic function evaluations are allowed to have non-uniform dependence on the data stream. In addition, the constants in the non-asymptotic bounds do not rely on log-Sobolev or Poincaré inequalities as in prior zeroth-order Langevin analyses. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first non-asymptotic analysis of a zeroth-order Langevin method that simultaneously establishes excess-risk guarantees for a curvature-regularized objective and Wasserstein guarantees for the associated Gibbs measure in the nonconvex setting.

title: Bulgarian solitaire with distinguishable cells
abstract: Classical Bulgarian solitaire tracks only the sizes of the stacks. We ask how the lengths of its periodic orbits change when individual cards are distinguished. To study this question, we introduce four actions $T_1,T_2,T_3,T_4$ on partitions with labeled cells. The actions differ in whether the top or bottom cell is removed from each column and in the order in which the removed cells are arranged to form a new column. We determine the exact sizes of the periodic orbits for all four actions. The main work lies in the analysis of $T_2$, for which we develop a coloring algorithm on Ferrers diagrams. The coloring encodes the cycle structure of the permutation of the labels induced by one full period of the underlying partition.

title: Basis selection, universal sampling discretization, and sampling recovery
abstract: For every real $N$-dimensional subspace of $L_2$, we construct one orthonormal basis such that, for every $1\le v\le N$, at most $Cv\log(eN/v)$ positively weighted samples discretize the squared $L_2$ norm of all $v$-term combinations. Random rotations also give simultaneous weighted $L_p$ estimates and a sharp $C\log(eN)$ bound for the squared $L_2$ norm of the pointwise maximum. For prescribed coefficient classes, a change of measure yields sampling recovery estimates from $Cv\log^3(2v)$ samples under a lower Riesz inequality and a common square-integrable pointwise bound.

title: Metric nefness of direct image sheaves under weakly semi-stable Kähler morphisms
abstract: We investigate the nefness of the direct image sheaves of relative adjoint bundles under weakly semi-stable Kähler morphisms between complex spaces. We show that the direct image sheaves are locally free and that their tautological line bundles are metrically nef, strengthening the previously known results on torsion-freeness and certain weak positivity.

title: Generalized near-group tensor categories
abstract:
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a finite tensor category with exactly one isomorphism class of simple objects which are non-invertible.
  Semisimple tensor categories $\mathcal{D}$ with this property are called near-group categories, and have been studied by Evans, Gannon, Siehler and others. In this paper, we study such categories in the non-semisimple setting, with the additional assumption that the non-invertible simple object is projective. Specifically, we consider the case when $\mathcal{D}$ admits a fiber functor and has a unique semisimple abelian block (in the general case that $\D$ is not semisimple). We describe the structure of such categories and their corresponding Hopf algebras, and construct examples of such categories with a cyclic Picard group. We obtain additional results when the Frobenius-Perron dimension of the unique non-invertible simple object is a prime number.

title: Memoryless BFGS on a nonsmooth convex function: two new results
abstract:
We extend the analysis of Asl and Overton~\cite{AO2021} for memoryless BFGS (also known as L-BFGS-1) using an Armijo-Wolfe line search and applied to the nonsmooth convex function $f(x)=a|x^{(1)}|+\sum_{i=2}^n x^{(i)}$, where $n\ge2$ and $a \geq \sqrt{n-1}$. This function is unbounded below, so the method is successful if it generates function values diverging to $-\infty$, and fails otherwise. For scaled L-BFGS-1, we sharpen the sufficient condition for % az{convergence of the absolute normalized search directions} in Theorem~3.1 of failure in \cite{AO2021} from $a\ge2\sqrt{n-1}$ to $a\ge\sqrt{3(n-1)}$.
  For the unscaled version, we prove success for every $a$: either the method generates a direction along which no Armijo-Wolfe step exists, certifying unboundedness below, or its function values diverge to $-\infty$.
  Both results are consistent with the numerical experiments in \cite{AO2021}. Both proofs given here were derived with help from GPT 6 in discussions directed by the first author and corrected and rephrased afterward.

title: A Goldbach-Type Problem for the Unitary Möbius Function
abstract: Let $g(n)=(-1)^{ω(n)}$, where $ω(n)$ denotes the number of distinct prime factors of $n$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, each ordered additive sign pattern $(g(a),g(N-a))=(s,t)$ occurs at least $N/(128(\log N)^3)$ times. We also prove that, for every $N\ge18$ and every $s,t\in\sgnset$, there is at least one integer $1\le a<N$ such that $(g(a),g(N-a))=(s,t)$. In addition, we establish a one-quarter asymptotic formula for almost all target integers. Finally, we discuss Goldbach-type problems for the ordinary Möbius function and formulate related questions.

title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
abstract: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $χ$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $χ$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.

title: Weighted Logarithm Laws in non-commutative Probability
abstract: We prove analogues of weighted laws of iterated logarithm and laws of logarithm for non-commutative martingales and independent random variables respectively. First we obtain a weighted LIL for non-commutative martingales, extending the sharp unweighted result of arXiv:2509.22037v2 to the case for polynomial weights, then by approximation to a broader class of functions. Then we proved a weighted law of logarithm for triangular array of weights and replacing the coefficient in the denominator by regularly varying functions with index $α$. We show that the normalised sums converge to 0 for $α> 1/2$ and for the case $α=1/2$, we obtain the sharp upper bound with constant $\sqrt{2}$.

title: Divide-and-Conquer is Tail- and Anomaly-Robust: Factor Model Estimation Without Moment Constraints
abstract: We study robust estimation of elliptical factor models with abnormal observations and without requiring the existence of any positive moments. In particular, a divide-and-conquer (DC) estimator averages orthogonal projectors onto the full column spaces of small data blocks, and we rigorously establish its probability bound that allows weak and heterogeneous factors. The derived convergence rate is comparable to that of classical principal component estimators, up to the proportion of anomalies. Building on our DC estimator, we propose a split-sample tail- and anomaly-robust (STAR) estimator for the factor number using sample medians of successive projected coordinate ratios, which is shown consistent under mild conditions. Subsequent factor and common component estimation is also discussed, with the rates of convergence spelled out. Remarkably, given an upper bound on the true factor number, our suite of procedures are free from tuning, require no tail-dependent truncation threshold nor solving an optimization problem, admit parallel block computations, and hence has the same computational complexity as the classical principal component methods. Extensive experiments corroborate our theoretical findings, where DC and STAR are comparable and often outperform state-of-the-art competitors. We also illustrate our methods on a portfolio return dataset.

title: Vázquez Strong Maximum Principle and Compact Support Principle for singular and degenerate elliptical operators
abstract: In this paper, we present adaptations of the classical strong maximum principle and the compact support principle for a certain class of equations, with particular emphasis on the degeneracy of fully nonlinear operators and a new Vázquez-type condition on the nonhomogeneous term. The novelty of our approach lies in the framework of the problem: the coefficients of the operators are bounded, but we introduce a degeneracy depending on the power of the gradient of the solution. Moreover, the source term $f$ on the right-hand side of the equation is treated under a adapted and optimal integrability assumptions.

title: On the Vázquez Strong Maximum Principle for Linear and Nonlinear Elliptic Equations with Unbounded Coefficients and Optimal Conditions
abstract: In this paper, we present adaptations of the classical strong maximum principle for a certain class of equations, with particular emphasis on linear operators in non-divergence form and a new strategy to prove it. The novelty of our approach lies in the setting of the problem: the coefficients of the operators are unbounded, assumed to be merely integrable in the $L^{p,q}$-sense, and the source term $f$ on the right-hand side of the equation is treated under optimal integrability assumptions.

title: Up or down by half: a family of Collatz-type maps
abstract:
Each Collatz step changes a positive integer by roughly half: odd inputs go up and even inputs go down. We vary the directions while keeping the step size. Write x=2^m k (k odd), and let S be a set of positive integers. Define T_S(x)=(3x+1)/2 if m=0, 3x/2 if m is in S, and k otherwise. The map T_S^- differs only at odd x, which it sends to (x+1)/2. The usual Collatz map is T_emptyset.
  Assuming the independence of 2-adic valuations along odd-to-odd steps yields random-walk models with drifts (1+rho(S))log_2(3)-2 for T_S and rho(S)log_2(3)-2 for T_S^-, where rho(S) is an explicit series. Every T_S^- is contracting; T_S is contracting exactly when rho(S)<log_3(4/3), approximately 0.2619. We prove density results, classify interval sets S, and give a criterion ensuring every T_S^- orbit reaches 1 or (2,3). For seven contracting maps T_S, three with rho(S)=1/4 just below the threshold, computations show that every n<2^34 (n<1.668*10^10 for S={1}) reaches one of at most five cycles; stopping-time statistics match the model to 3-5 digits.
  We study branching maps, where any member of a family may be applied at each step. Boundedness of a family implies boundedness of each member; in particular, boundedness of {T_emptyset,T_{3}} would imply that no Collatz orbit diverges. For {T_emptyset,T_{1}}, a rule depending only on x mod 32 has positive drift (10/17)log_2(9/8) for almost every 2-adic starting point. Thus almost all n have reachable sets containing values larger than n^1.05; residues modulo 2^L, L<=10, cannot prove unboundedness.
  Finally, we define unified maps in which valuations also determine the direction at odd inputs. The cases x=1 mod 4 govern their behavior: if they go down, every block is dominated by the corresponding Collatz map (and a census finds only the cycles (1), (2, 3) and (3, 5) with smallest element below 10^9); if they go up, the maps behave like T_S.

title: Costate-Conditioned Dynamic Programming for Parallel-in-Time Solution of Equality-Constrained Optimal Control Problems
abstract: When interior-point methods are applied to solve numerical trajectory optimisation problems, they spend most of their per-iteration time on a structured Newton--KKT system, associated to an equality-constrained linear-quadratic optimal control problem. Riccati-type algorithms exhibit linear complexity in the trajectory horizon. Parallel-in-time algorithms are able to reduce this to logaritmic complexity by distributing several subtrajectories over multiple cores and then stitch together the results by means of an associative scan. Existing exact formulations condition each subtrajectory on its terminal state. Each subproblem then carries the reachability to that terminal state explicitly as constraint rows. The associated reachability decision however is ill-conditioned for weakly actuated systems. In this work we condition each subtrajectory on the terminal costate instead. The resulting subproblems can now be computed by a free-end Riccati recursion without reachability carrying rows. This approach effectively compensates for the ill-conditioning of weakly actuated systems but requires additional bookkeeping with Lagrangian multipliers when stitching together the various subproblems. Numerically the method reproduces a direct solution of the primal-dual Newton-KKT system to $10^{-12}$ in relative terms, on a weakly controllable chain of masses, the accurracy rivals that of a sequential recursion, whereas terminal-state conditioning loses up to six digits or fails. Operation counts on a problem with 64 subtrajectories and a horizon of 4096 stages gives a speed-up of 26 compared with a sequential solve.

title: Convergence of Adaptive Least Squares Finite Element Methods
abstract: We consider a general class of operator equations $\mathcal B u=f$ where $\mathcal B:\mathbb U\to \mathbb L_2$ is a linear isomorphis from a Hilbert space $\mathbb U$ onto an ``$L_2$-type'' space $\mathbb L_2 = L_2(Ω;\mathbb R^q)$. This covers weak first order formulations of stationary elliptic boundary value problems, the Stokes system or systems for linear elasticity as well as space-time formulations of heat or wave equations. Since an $L_2$-residual is uniformly equivalent to the corresponding error in the trial space norm reliable and efficient computable a posteriori error bounds are for free. In contrast to a matured theory of classical adaptive finite element methods, estblishing linear convergence - and eventually optimal complexity - in a least squares setting seems to have remained open. To a large extent this is due to the fact that least squares error indicators do not exhibit any explicit dependence on local mesh-sizes. In this paper we propose a rather different approach to establish under which circumstances standard Dörfler-marking mesh refinement gives rise to linear convergence and rate optimality of adaptive least squares finite element methods as well. A central role is played by a new notion of {\em data-visibility} which is a structural property of the data rather than a smoothness condition.

title: Semifree actions and representation varieties
abstract: A group action on a topological space induces an action on the space's representation variety. We determine the fixed point sets of this latter action for semifree group actions on surfaces and circle bundles over surfaces. We also discuss implications for mapping tori of periodic maps.

title: Full fillings at the accumulation point and triangular limits of almost toric diagrams
abstract: Let $M$ be a closed symplectic four-manifold admitting an almost toric fibration over a disk. The ellipsoid embedding function of $M$ has an infinite staircase if it has infinitely many nonsmooth points. Cristofaro-Gardiner, Holm, Mandini, and Pires showed that these points must then accumulate at a solution of an explicit quadratic equation, and that at this accumulation point the ellipsoid embedding function agrees with the volume obstruction. We call this a full filling at the accumulation point, and study it in terms of almost toric fibrations. We show that if $M$ admits a sequence of almost toric base diagrams, each with a Delzant corner, converging nontrivially to a triangle, then $M$ has a full filling at its accumulation point. For the one-point blowups $H_b$ of $\mathbb{CP}^2$, we also prove the converse. As a consequence, $H_b$ has an infinite staircase if and only if it admits such a sequence converging to a triangle whose hypotenuse has irrational slope.

title: Brown-Gap Healing and Exact Completeness Thresholds for Leading-Unit Positive Linear Recurrences
abstract: We determine the exact completeness threshold for standard positive linear recurrence sequences whose coefficient lists consist of leading units, followed by zeros and a final positive coefficient. Using the generating function of Brown's gaps, we prove a necessary and sufficient condition for completeness, including the boundary case in which the critical gap vanishes. We further establish strict monotonicity of the unrounded threshold in the number of leading units, thereby resolving the corresponding leading-unit monotonicity conjecture.

title: The satisfiability conjecture for random k-SAT formulas. Human-friendly exposition of the recent OpenAI resolution
abstract:
The satisfiability conjecture was one of the most important open problems in discrete probability. It was resolved recently first by Carenini~\cite{GCarenini}, and shortly after by OpenAI~\cite{k-sat-OpenAI}, among other 370 problems solved by its internal model. The conjecture concerned the satisfiability property of random instances of the k-SAT problem. It posits the existence of a fixed value for the clause-to-variables ratio around which the probability that the formula is satisfiable drops sharply from nearly one to nearly zero as the ratio increases. While the case of large constant $k$ was resolved a decade ago by Ding, Sly and Sun~\cite{ding2015proof,ding2022proof} using the heavy machinery of the second moment method, the case of general $k$ eluded proof until ~\cite{GCarenini} and~\cite{k-sat-OpenAI}.
  In this short note we provide a ''human-friendly'' and detailed exposition of the OpenAI's resolution of the conjecture.

title: Adaptive visualization for enumerative problems
abstract: We present an adaptive visualization framework and its implementation in the julia package AdaptiveVisualization.jl. Our algorithm visualizes functions using an adaptive sampling procedure that concentrates the evaluation budget at interesting regions of the domain. We illustrate our package on our main application: visualizing parameter spaces of enumerative problems.

title: Operator-Adapted Multiscale Kernels for High-Contrast Elliptic Inverse Problems
abstract:
We consider the joint recovery of the state and diffusion coefficient in a high-contrast elliptic equation from sparse, noisy state measurements. We seek the coefficient in a parameterized family defined relative to a prescribed reference coefficient. We construct a generalized multiscale finite element basis from the reference coefficient and use it to define a finite-rank kernel for the state. A weak Galerkin residual enforces the equation without pointwise differentiation across material interfaces. For each trial coefficient, the state is obtained by solving a linear least-squares problem. Variable projection eliminates the state coordinates from the objective, and the reduced gradient is evaluated without an adjoint PDE solve.
  We split the state reconstruction error into multiscale approximation, penalty relaxation, and parameter estimation terms. Under an admissible patch decomposition, the squared multiscale approximation error is bounded by a local spectral tail estimate with a contrast-independent interpolation constant. For a fixed coefficient and discretization, the penalty relaxation error is of order $O(\varepsilon^2)$ when the residual weight is proportional to $\varepsilon^{-2}$. The parameter contribution is bounded by local Lipschitz continuity of the projected state. In 50 synthetic tests based on a reference medium of contrast $10^4$, the multiscale space with the weak residual gives mean relative state and log-coefficient errors of 2.37\% and 4.43\%, respectively, the lowest among the four configurations tested.

title: Constructive algebraic methods for bisymmetric means
abstract: We prove continuity for reflexive, bisymmetric binary operations that are strictly increasing in each variable, under certain algebraic conditions. In fact, for some algebraic weights we construct a weighted quasi-arithmetic representation of such functions without assuming continuity. An elementary construction gives the case $r=2/3$. More generally, a word equality whose polynomial difference has a unique simple zero $r\in(0,1)$ forces the representation with weight $r$; every algebraic $r$ with no other conjugate in $(0,1)$ arises this way. The proof uses an affine embedding and a dense-domain extension argument.

title: A Trajectory-Aware Domain-Decomposed Multispace Reduced Basis Preconditioner for Parametric Helmholtz Problems
abstract: Repeated solutions of parametric Helmholtz problems arise in multi-query applications such as sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification. Classical preconditioned iterative solvers do not automatically reuse low-dimensional structures across parameters. Multispace reduced basis (MSRB) preconditioners can exploit such structures by constructing iteration-specific reduced order models (ROMs) from training data, but storing global iteration-dependent bases incurs substantial memory costs. Building on trajectory-aware MSRB training, we develop a domain-decomposed MSRB (DD-MSRB) preconditioner for parametric Helmholtz systems truncated by perfectly matched layers (PMLs). Within flexible GMRES, each reduced space is trained on inverse-action snapshots along the Krylov trajectories generated by the ROM-based preconditioners applied in preceding iterations. To reduce storage, problem-adapted spatial partitions exploit heterogeneous local snapshot compressibility across the physical interior and the PML. Local basis dimensions in each subdomain are determined greedily under a global snapshot-error budget to balance approximation accuracy and storage. The resulting hybrid solver applies DD-MSRB preconditioning during the initial iterations to capture dominant cross-parameter modes and then switches, when necessary, to a shifted-Laplacian preconditioner to reduce error components poorly represented by the reduced spaces. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional half-space propagation, elliptic-obstacle scattering, and three-dimensional waveguides demonstrate significant acceleration over the shifted-Laplacian baseline and substantial memory savings relative to global MSRB. For the largest waveguide system, with 11.0 million unknowns, DD-MSRB reduces deployed ROM storage by 44.9% and mean online solve time by 30.2% compared with global MSRB.

title: GEAR: A GPU-Accelerated Global Solver for Bounded Continuous Nonlinear Programs via Linear Bound Propagation
abstract: We present a novel GPU-accelerated global solver for constrained nonlinear programming (NLP) inspired by the efficient linear bound propagation framework in neural network (NN) verification. Existing work on NN verification, a problem that can be cast as feasibility detection for a nonlinear objective, demonstrated orders-of-magnitude speedups with the linear bound propagation-based framework when compared to traditional solvers. Extending this paradigm to global nonlinear programming requires addressing many challenges: a global constrained NLP solver must effectively exploit all, possibly unstructured, nonlinear constraints to improve the objective, whereas NN verification typically handles simple input box constraints over a well-structured NN and does not directly optimize an objective function. We address these challenges by fully exploiting the linear bounds produced by bound propagation: these linear bounds can be viewed as relaxations of nonlinear constraints and used to provide lower bounds, check infeasibility, and guide the search for a primal solution. In addition, we propose tighter linear relaxations for bilinear, quotient, and other commonly used nonlinear functions in NLP problems, and a projected augmented Lagrangian method tightly coupled to our dual solving procedure to produce primal solutions. Our method solves 421 of 505 bounded and continuous NLP problems in the GAMS and MINLPLib benchmarks under a 180-second limit, more than each of the six global solvers we compare with, including Gurobi and BARON (commercial), and SCIP (open-source). Sixteen of these problems are certified by none of the six global solvers; all of them contain exponential, logarithmic, or trigonometric terms, which are often challenging for traditional approaches. Project webpage is at https://verified-intelligence.github.io/GEAR.

title: High-order long-time stable methods for the forced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations
abstract: We present in this paper two scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) correction steps for constructing long-time stable schemes for the forced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions. A main feature is that the same correction steps apply to any linear predictor satisfying the order and spatial regularity requirements in Assumption~P. Their construction and stability analysis are independent of the particular form of the predictor and require no energy estimate for it. The first correction uses a damped, shifted kinetic-energy variable to obtain a uniform-in-time $L^2$ bound in two and three dimensions, together with a weighted dissipation estimate. In two dimensions, the second correction combines a higher-energy auxiliary variable with a scalar relaxation to yield a uniform-in-time $H^1$ bound. Under the stated assumptions, these estimates hold on arbitrary positive time grids, without restrictions on step sizes or adjacent step ratios. We also derive eventual absorbing bounds; for the two-SAV scheme, these apply to the admissible initial class associated with fixed parameters. The generalized BDF schemes require one constant-coefficient Helmholtz solve per velocity component and one pressure Poisson solve per step; the second correction adds no field solve. Numerical experiments exhibit second-, third-, and fourth-order convergence for the tested BDF schemes and illustrate the long-time stability and efficiency of adaptive time stepping.

title: Nonexistence of positive solutions stable outside a compact set for the Lane--Emden system in a half-space
abstract: We prove that, in every dimension and for all positive exponents, the Lane--Emden system in a half-space with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions admits no positive classical solution stable outside a compact set.

title: Birational Geometry of K-Moduli Spaces of Genus Four Curves
abstract: We study the wall-crossings for K-moduli spaces of (3,3)-curves on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. Together with the boundary polarized Calabi--Yau moduli space, these spaces interpolate between the GIT moduli space of (3,3)-curves and the Baily--Borel compactification of the moduli space of K3 surfaces arising as cyclic triple covers of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ branched along such curves. As applications, we describe the corresponding birational models in the Hassett--Keel--Looijenga program and realize the K-moduli space of degree one del Pezzo surfaces through explicit wall-crossings.

title: Discrete-Time Zero-Sum Markov Games with Control, Stopping, and State-Dependent Discounting
abstract: We study a discrete-time two-player zero-sum stochastic game with control and stopping, where both players can stop the game, the discount factors depends on the states, and the running and terminal rewards may be unbounded. A contraction argument for the constrained Shapley equation establishes the existence of the value and a Nash equilibrium consisting of stationary controls and stopping times. We further provides algorithms for approximating the value and computing an $\varepsilon$-Nash equilibrium. A numerical example with state-dependent discount factors illustrates the results.

title: Polynomial conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov maps derived from train track representatives
abstract: We investigate two kinds of polynomials associated with pseudo-Anosov maps. Each kind consists of three polynomials that are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes and these polynomials contain more information than pseudo-Anosov stretch factors. The first kind is defined by the train track representatives. The second kind is obtained from the first kind by incorporating additional data that encode the transitions among the unpunctured singularities of the invariant foliations. The Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials coincide with those of the second kind. As an application, we prove that the Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes which is also proved by Dodge-Kawamuro, independently.

title: Critical Branching Systems with General Lifetimes: Hunt Motions and Applications to Semilinear Equations
abstract:
We consider a critical monotype Bellman-Harris branching particle system on $E=R^d$ or $E=[0,\infty)^d$, started from a homogeneous Poisson field with Lebesgue intensity. Particles follow a conservative Hunt process with transition semigroup $(P_t)_{t\ge 0}$, have independent lifetimes with distribution $Γ$, and reproduce at death with generating function $f(s)=s+c(1-s)^{1+β}$. We assume Lebesgue invariance and uniform bounds $P_t1_K=O(t^{-q})$ for compact $K$. We also impose a localization condition: the expected number of particles in a fixed compact set at time $t$ descended from ancestors initially outside suitable regions of volume $O(t^q)$ can be made arbitrarily small, uniformly for $t\ge 1$.
  For spread-out lifetimes of finite mean, the system converges to a nontrivial limit of Lebesgue intensity when $qβ>1$ and becomes locally extinct when $qβ\le 1$. For nonarithmetic lifetimes satisfying $\barΓ(t)\sim c_1t^{-γ}$, $0<γ\le 1$, the threshold is $qβ=γ$: the limit is Poisson above it, local extinction holds below it, and a nontrivial subsequential limit exists at equality.
  We verify the hypotheses and determine recurrence-transience regimes for symmetric and anisotropic stable processes, symmetric uniformly elliptic diffusions, generalized squared-Bessel products on $[0,\infty)^d$, and symmetric bilateral Bessel-type diffusions on $R^d$ and their nonsingular linear images. Finally, we derive quantitative sufficient conditions for survival of total mass in semilinear equations with absorption, including time-dependent diffusion rates. Here survival means that the limiting total mass is strictly positive. For a hyperbolic diffusion, this holds for every $β>0$ in the absorption term $-v^{1+β}$.

title: The Dimension Conjecture for Hypersurfaces Is True
abstract: The dimension conjecture in CR geometry is proved for an arbitrary real-analytic hypersurface. More precisely, we prove that the dimension of the algebra of infinitesimal holomorphic automorphisms of a germ of a holomorphically nondegenerate hypersurface in $\mathbb{C}^N$ in this class does not exceed $N^2+2N$. This number is exactly the corresponding dimension for any nondegenerate hyperquadric in the same ambient space. Moreover, equality holds if and only if the germ is equivalent to a hyperquadric.

title: A metric characterization of free unitary quantum groups
abstract: For a compact matrix quantum group $G$ with a fundamental unitary representation $u$ of dimension at least two, the reduced operator norm of the self-adjoint main character satisfies $\left \|χ_u+χ_u^*\right \|_{C_r(G)}\geq2\sqrt2$. Within the category of free quantum groups of Kac type, it is known that the minimum $2\sqrt2$ is attained only by free unitary quantum groups. We establish this characterization in full generality, including the non-Kac setting: this minimum is attained if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to a free unitary quantum group $U_Q^+$ as compact matrix quantum groups.

title: Sample complexity and scalability of adaptive-sampling trust-region methods for zeroth-order stochastic optimization --- Part I: common random numbers meet supermartingales
abstract: We analyze adaptive sampling stochastic model-based trust-region methods that build their models in random subspaces and use common random numbers (CRN) within an iteration, and obtain, within a STORM-type analysis, the first $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ bound on the number of function evaluations needed to reach $\varepsilon$-stationarity, both almost surely and in expectation. The subspace model reduces the per-iteration computational cost, which allows scalability. The analysis relies on a general framework for the complexity of adaptive stochastic processes that carries the almost-sure analysis of ASTRO-DF into the STORM setting and adds expected bounds by a direct counting argument, without the renewal-reward argument of Blanchet et al. (2019). The bounds are obtained for two variants of a stochastic model-based trust-region method that differ in how the function evaluations used to measure progress are generated. The first algorithm, ASTRA-F, proceeds in a STORM-like manner: the trial point and the incumbent are re-evaluated on an independent set of replications, so that the estimates entering the acceptance test are independent of the model, as every existing STORM-type analysis requires their accuracy to be assessed conditionally on the model. The second, ASTRA-R, allows a practical approach: the trial point is evaluated on the replications already drawn to build the model, which avoids re-evaluating the incumbent, needs one adaptive sample size per iteration instead of two, and reduces the randomness entering the iteration. To our knowledge, no STORM-type analysis has been able to accommodate the latter approach as the accuracy of an estimate at a point chosen from the samples cannot be assessed conditionally on the model; we overcome this with a probabilistic chaining argument.

title: Stability in the Non-Neutral and Neutral Regimes of the Holonomy-Based Inverse Problem in the Class \(\mathcal{OC}\)
abstract: We study anchor reconstruction stability in return-map inverse problems for class $\mathcal O_C$. Local identifiability is governed by the first nonvanishing derivative of the holonomy map $H = T_γ- \text{Id}$. In the non-neutral case, we prove local Lipschitz stability and multiplier estimates. In the neutral regime, using Faà di Bruno equations and Malgrange preparation, we derive quantitative $1/k$-Hölder estimates for order-$k$ anchor perturbations. We also establish finite jet stability, real-analytic dependence, and global $C^0$-stability of order $O(\varepsilon_F^{1/k})$. Numerical benchmarks on circular-core return geometries validate these theoretical convergence rates and square-root laws.

title: The Whitney Extension Problem in Carnot groups
abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a Carnot group, let $E \subset \mathbb{G}$ be compact, and suppose we are given a function $f: E \to \mathbb{R}$. The $C^1_H$ {\em Whitney Extension Problem} asks the following: what must be true about $f$ to guarantee that there exists a smooth, horizontal function $F \in C^1_H(\mathbb{G})$ extending $f$, i.e., there is some $F:\mathbb{G} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $F|_E = f|_E$ and $XF$ is continuous for every horizontal left invariant vector field $X$? We adapt the method of G. Glaeser and C. Fefferman to answer this question in this non-commutative setting. Moreover, we provide an alternative solution to the $C^1$ Whitney Extension Problem for horizontal curves in the Heisenberg group.

title: Laplace approximation of the parameter posterior with embedded error for efficient uncertainty quantification of expensive model calibrations
abstract: In practical engineering, there is a clear need for uncertainty quantification (UQ) of models used in design because forward UQ puts probabilities on performance predictions. However, without surrogate building, most forward engineering models are too expensive for traditional UQ methods like Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. Our goal is to provide inexpensive, approxi- mate UQ that can be applied after an expensive traditional least squares fit, where the UQ handles both uncorrelated noise and parameter variance as in the embedded-error treatment developed by Sargsyan, Najm, and Ghanem (2015). After developing the basic theory to connect a Laplace-like approximation to Bayesian calibration, we compare the proposed method to black-box variational inference in terms of cost and fidelity. Then we demonstrate the method on real-world calibration of solid material models.

title: Questions of minimality for DDMOGs and cycle ornaments
abstract: Difference distance magic oriented graphs (DDMOGs) are oriented graphs whose vertices admit a bijective labeling by consecutive positive integers such that every vertex has weight zero, where the weight is the sum of the labels of its in-neighbors minus the sum of the labels of its out-neighbors. We investigate minimality and sparsity questions for DDMOGs and their ornaments. First, we develop new constructions of cycle-based ornaments that reduce the number of cycles required for a given number of attachment nodes and identify minimal cycle lengths in several cases. Second, we determine the minimum number of arcs in a nontrivial DDMOG of order $n$, combining computational enumeration for small orders with theoretical lower bounds and constructions. Langford sequences provide a key tool in these constructions, enabling us to partition consecutive labels into difference triples and thereby construct sparse DDMOGs. Finally, we use related constructions to obtain generalized ornaments with no internal arcs. These results advance the study of minimal constructions in difference distance magic labeling and provide new methods for building sparse DDMOGs.

title: A Geometric Construction of the Radial Dunkl and Heckman-Opdam Processes
abstract: We provide a geometric construction of the radial Dunkl and Heckman-Opdam processes for arbitrary root systems and arbitrary nonnegative real root multiplicity parameters. This is a broad class of processes including the classical Bessel process, Dyson Brownian motion, and the Dyson Bessel process. We find that, when $x_t$ is a certain anisotropic Markov diffusion process in a symmetric space $G/K$ or its tangent space at the origin, invariant under an appropriate $K$-action, the evolution in the space of orbits can be described as a radial Dunkl or Heckman-Opdam process (respective to whether the diffusion is on the tangent space or $G/K$ itself). These processes can have arbitrary nonnegative real root multiplicities, analogous to arbitrary values of $β$ in Dyson Brownian motion. In a freezing limit, analogous to $β\to \infty$ for Dyson Brownian motion, these processes become motion by mean curvature of the orbits. A connection to finite free probability is also discussed, in which we provide a geometric interpretation of certain properties related to finite free position.

title: Linear Response for Self-Consistent Transfer Operators on Graphons
abstract:
We develop the response theory of the equilibrium state of a large heterogeneous network of weakly coupled uniformly expanding circle maps. The thermodynamic limit of such a network is governed by a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator (STO) acting on measures fibred over a graphon $W$, as introduced in \cite{MPT2025}. We prove that in the weak coupling regime the unique attracting fixed point $φ^\star(α)$ of the STO depends on the coupling strength in a Lipschitz, and then differentiable, way in a scale of fibrewise Sobolev spaces, and we derive a linear response formula.
  Our main result is that at zero coupling the response factorises: its derivative along the fibre $z$ equals $\barW(z)\,\Up$, where $\barW$ is the degree function of the graphon and $\Up=-(\Id-P)^{-1}[P(H_ρρ)]'$ is a universal profile depending only on the local dynamics and on the coupling function. To first order the heterogeneity of the statistical response across the network is therefore dictated by the degree profile alone, and the finer topology is invisible; the susceptibility of a node is proportional to its degree, so hubs respond most. The topology enters at higher order through a tree expansion: the perturbative coefficients of the equilibrium, defined unconditionally by an explicit recursion, are combinations --- with universal coefficient functions --- of the rooted homomorphism densities of trees with $m$ edges. We prove that the first two coefficients are the genuine asymptotic ones, the second producing the mean degree of the neighbours of $z$. We also obtain a response formula for perturbations of the graphon itself, Green--Kubo expressions for observables, and the prediction that in a finite network the linear susceptibility of a node is proportional to its normalised degree.

title: Higher properties T and finiteness properties for twin building lattices
abstract: Properties $[T_k]$ and finiteness properties $FP_k(\mathbb{Q})$ and $F_k$ are refinements of the following fundamental notions for groups: Kazhdan property T in the first case, and finite generation/presentation in the last two cases. Under suitable hypotheses on the thickness, we prove that every twin building lattice of $(k+1)$-spherical type $(W,S)$, where $k\geq 1$, has property $[T_k]$ and is of type $FP_k(\mathbb{Q})$. If $(W,S)$ is classical, that group is even of type $F_k$. To the best of the author's knowledge, this produces the first examples of infinite finitely presented simple groups with property $[T_k]$ for some $k\geq 2$, and the first examples of finitely presented simple Kazhdan groups that are Frobenius stable and not Frobenius approximable. Along the way, we establish new criteria for property $[T_k]$ for groups acting on CW complexes that extend results of Dymara--Januszkiewicz and Grinbaum-Reizis--Oppenheim. As a key step in our proofs, we determine high acyclicity and, in classical type, high connectivity properties for the opposite complex of a Moufang twin building of $(k+1)$-spherical type and suitable finite thickness.

title: The Idempotent Measure Conjecture beyond solvable and stable groups
abstract:
Pym's theorem [Pym62] states that a regular Borel probability measure on a locally compact group is idempotent if and only if it is the normalized Haar measure of a compact subgroup. The Idempotent Measure Conjecture, the definable-group counterpart of [GHK25, Conjecture (A)], proposes an analogous characterization: a global fim Keisler measure on a definable group is idempotent if and only if it is the unique global Keisler measure concentrating on a type-definable subgroup and invariant under translation by elements of that subgroup.
  We prove this conjecture for virtually solvable definable groups in arbitrary theories. More generally, we establish it for definable groups admitting a finite series of definable normal subgroups whose successive quotients are either virtually solvable or stably embedded with stable induced structure.
  Finally, we disprove [GHK25, Conjecture (A)] in its automorphism-group formulation in the theory of dense linear orders without endpoints.

title: Topological Lifting of Mundici Equivalence and Di Nola--Lettieri Equivalence
abstract: We prove that summability characterises precisely when a topological MV-algebra can be realized as the unit interval of a lattice-ordered topological abelian group, thereby providing a topological lifting of both Mundici equivalence and DiNola--Lettieri equivalence. Applications include a Birkhoff--Kakutani-type metrisation theorem, a second-countability criterion, and a topological extension of a key continuity lemma from the proof theory of first-order Łukasiewicz logic---following Baaz--Metcalfe's hypersequent approach to approximate completenesss---and provides an $A$-valued topological semantics for the approximate strong completeness of~$\mathbf{G}\text{Ł}\forall$, where $A$ ranges over summable topological MV-algebras.

title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-1: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
abstract: We study obstructions of deformations of foliated complex analytic structures. We describe obstructions in terms of Cech resolutions. From foliated complex analytic families in Part I and unfolded complex analytic families in Part III, we deduce the integrability conditions. We identify infinitesimal deformations and obstructions in terms of Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes from the integrability conditions. Then we describe the correspondences of infinitesimal deformations and obstructions between Cech resolutions, and Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes.

title: Cross-Domain Channel Estimation for MU-MIMO-OFDM
abstract: Conventional channel estimation for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) relies on the pilot interpolation without explicitly identifying the sparse delay-angle (DA) components. To exploit DA sparsity while maintaining backward compatibility with existing MIMO-OFDM systems, we propose a cross-domain channel estimation scheme for multiuser MIMO-OFDM (MU-MIMO-OFDM) systems. The scheme exploits the circular convolution structure in the DA domain to identify candidate DA pairs by correlating delay-domain observations with DA pilot responses. These pairs and the known pilots then define a time-frequency (TF) dictionary for refining the DA coefficients from TF observations through least-squares or sparsity-regularized fitting. The refined coefficients and candidate pairs reconstruct the aggregate channel across antennas and subcarriers aligning with the geometric channel model. Numerical results show approximately 10 dB and 7 dB lower normalized mean-square error than the conventional OFDM estimation schemes for integer and fractional delay and angle indices, respectively.

title: Rigidity of spacelike graphs in generalized Robertson-Walker spacetimes via the infinity-Laplacian
abstract: In the search for new characterizations of spacelike slices in generalized Robertson-Walker spacetimes, we introduce a new approach. The main tool for addressing this question is the infty-Laplacian with respect to the Riemannian metric induced on the spacelike hypersurface, together with a Liouville-type property for the infinity-Laplacian on any complete Riemannian manifold by Araujo, Mari and Pessoa in 2021. Starting from the infinity-Laplacian of the height function of a spacelike hypersurface, we derive several differential equations involving the infinity-Laplacian of suitable compositions of the height function, namely, the warping function f(h), its primitive P=\int f, and the logarithmic composition log(f(h)). Under some natural assumptions, including timelike and null energy conditions, global rigidity results are established in the parametric setting. Some of these results specialize naturally to complete spacelike hypersurfaces in the Steady State spacetime and in Einstein-de Sitter spacetime. Finally, we consider a second-order PDE involving the infty-Laplacian and study the uniqueness of its entire solutions on the fiber of the generalized Robertson-Walker spacetime. This leads to new Calabi-Bernstein-type uniqueness results in the non-parametric setting.

title: On transportation of constrictions on phase-lock areas of overdamped Josephson junction by means of isomonodromic deformation of the associated special double confluent Heun equation
abstract: An example of computation of locations of constrictions on the phase-lock area in the parameter space for the equation modeling dynamics of overdamped Josephson junction is discussed. Several conjectures of qualitative character are inferred from the heuristic data thus obtained. The method applying isomonodromic deformations of the special double confluent Heun equation associated with the noted model is used. Such a deformation is controlled by the data provided by solution to a Third Painlevè equation for which a new representation in conjunction with the corresponding non-linear second order differential equation fairly efficient in the treatment of the problem in question is proposed.

title: The microstructure of information through mean field learning interaction
abstract: We study how knowledge about partially observable model parameters is being created and propagated in large scale systems. Information is generated from observational signals whose dynamics depend endogenously on the learning history, the learning duration, the decisions and the related costs encountered by a continuum of decision makers. Such characteristics give rise to a new class of sequential testing problems in which there is continuous endogenous feedback. Adopting the classical approach of Shiryaev, we relate the problem to an optimal stopping one for the representative belief process, whose generator now depends on the evolving interactions. Considering a fixed point for the latter, we introduce a notion of mean field game and prove the existence of an equilibrium. Our arguments, which are based on a combination of pde and probabilistic techniques, involve a detailed analysis of the underlying variational inequality and the geometry, stability and continuity of the free boundaries.

title: Bijecting $m$-Tamari intervals, trees, and tight gradings
abstract: Tight gradings, which are certain integer gradings on maximal Dyck paths, provide a combinatorial framework for computing all coefficients of wall-functions in rank-$2$ cluster scattering diagrams. We construct a bijection between a special subset of tight gradings and the intervals of the $m$-Tamari lattice, providing a new combinatorial proof of the central wall-function formula proved by Reineke. Inspired by the structure of these gradings, we introduce a class of plane trees called $m$-leafy trees that give a new model for $m$-Tamari intervals. The defining condition of an $m$-leafy tree is simple: in every full subtree, the number of leaves is greater than $m$ times the number of internal vertices. The leafy tree perspective gives rise to a quadratic functional equation with a catalytic parameter, providing an alternative way to enumerate $m$-Tamari intervals.

title: Double sums involving quotients of binomial coefficients
abstract: This paper is the third part of our detailed investigation of double sums where the inner sum is binomial but incomplete. We prove many identities for these double sums involving quotients of binomial coefficients and additional parameters. In addition, we evaluate some quadratic incomplete sums using Legendre polynomials.

title: Finiteness of local cohomology modules over arbitrary regular local rings
abstract:
In this paper, we consider arbitrary regular local ring $S$ and an ideal $J\subset S$ whose minimal primes are cohomologically complete intersection. Using the Mayer-Vietoris spectral sequence, in Section 2, we construct examples of local cohomology modules $H^i_J (S)$, whose set of associated primes is finite. As a special case we show that the set of associated primes $H^i_J (S)$ is finite when minimal primes of $J$ are part of a specific regular system of parameters and satisfy a `Dropping Condition'.
  In Section 3, we prove Theorem 2.3 along with its asssociated corollary in a more general setting, without the use of `Dropping Condition'.
  These examples of local cohomology modules include the cases whose associative primes also can contain prime number $p$.

title: A recursion relation for the coefficients of Swinnerton-Dyer type polynomials
abstract: We study a family of polynomials that are very closely related to the Swinnerton-Dyer polynomials. As main result, we determine a recursion relation for the coefficients of this family of polynomials. We briefly explain our own and others' interest in this family of polynomials.

title: Nonconstant Congruence Speeds of Integer Tetration in Non-Squarefree Radices
abstract: We further develop the theory of congruence speed for integer tetration in non-squarefree numeral systems, building on Appendix B of [M. Ripà and G. Di Pietro (2026), A compact notation for peculiar properties characterizing integer tetration, Notes on Number Theory and Discrete Mathematics, 32(3), 477-496]. For bases coprime to the radix, we establish an eventual floor-difference representation and determine the exact spectrum of attainable least periods. We construct explicit arithmetic progressions containing infinitely many prime bases with nonconstant congruence speed for every non-squarefree radix, thereby proving the coprime-infinitude conjecture posed in Appendix B. We also derive a uniform quadratic bound for the least coprime base with nonconstant congruence speed and establish exact natural densities of nonstabilizing bases, both among integers coprime to the radix and among those not divisible by its radical, together with the corresponding relative density among primes. Finally, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for the perfect-power congruence-speed identity (Equation (2.12) of the cited paper) to hold in arbitrary radices, determine the exact least eventual period when stabilization fails, and establish a separate criterion for the boundary case of the original parameter restriction.

title: Excluding 54 of the 76 Nontrivial Factorization Patterns of the Cuboid Polynomial $P_{a,b,u}(t)$
abstract: Let $P_{a,b,u}(t)$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$12$ third cuboid polynomial, with positive pairwise distinct rational parameters. We prove a uniform normal form for its complete factorization over $\mathbb{Q}$. Every factorization consists of at most two even quadratic factors, even irreducible factors of higher degree, and pairs of irreducible factors exchanged by $t\mapsto-t$. After dividing all degrees by the contribution of this symmetry, the normal form satisfies one degree equation, one sign equation, and an obligatory-factor alternative: an even irreducible factor of degree at least six, or an even irreducible quartic with positive rational-square constant term. The arithmetic input is a uniform construction over $\mathbb{Q}_2$, using Newton polygons, Hensel lifting, and a norm obstruction from $\mathbb{Q}_2(i)$. Valuations at all finite primes constrain rational factor constants to signed squares, while the real root equation gives exactly two simple negative roots of the auxiliary sextic. The normal form leaves exactly $22$ of the $76$ nontrivial partitions of $12$, thereby excluding $54$ complete irreducible degree patterns by one argument. Of these exclusions, $37$ follow from evenness alone and $17$ from the additional arithmetic restrictions. All local cases are proved explicitly, and an exact verification script accompanies the algebraic identities and exhaustive partition enumeration. The remaining patterns are necessary possibilities; their realization is not asserted, and full irreducibility remains open.

title: Uniqueness and stability of Appleton's solitons
abstract: We prove that Appleton's noncollapsed steady gradient Ricci solitons on complex line bundles over positive Kähler--Einstein manifolds are the unique such solitons arising from his metric ansatz. We then show that the four-dimensional examples on $O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}(-k)$, $k \geq 3$, are strictly linearly stable. By a result of Deruelle, this implies dynamical stability under the Ricci flow.

title: Directional Ergodic Theorems, Ergodicity, and Weak mixing for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions
abstract:
In this paper, we study Birkhoff and von Neumann type ergodic theorems for $\mathbb Z^2$-measure preserving systems along irrational directions. This leads us to a further investigation of directional ergodicity and weak mixing. Additionally, we show that our framework (dynamical definitions) is equivalent to the spectral definitions of directional ergodicity and weak mixing introduced by Robinson, Rosenblatt and Şahin \cite{RRS2023} for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions.
  We note that in their recent paper \cite{RS2026}, Robinson and Şahin established the equivalence between dynamical and spectral directional weak mixing for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions using an approach fundamentally different from the one employed in the present paper.

title: Liftable braid factorizations from line arrangements: Hironaka's relations and a Zariski pair
abstract: We realize Hironaka's generalized lantern relations by lifting positive braid factorizations. For a nonpencil real line arrangement with no parallel lines, we construct a family of branched coverings on the regular fibers of a blown-up pencil of spheres. The motion of the branch points gives a factorization of a power of the full twist into least liftable powers of half-twists. The Artal-Carmona-Cogolludo-Marco Zariski pair gives two such factorizations of the same braid for a single simple branched covering of the disk. Their lifts are Hurwitz inequivalent even up to simultaneous conjugation by page homeomorphisms. The corresponding Milnor fibers fill the same planar contact three-manifold and have the same incidence matrix. They are homeomorphic and lie in distinct strong symplectic deformation classes.

title: Characterizations of minimal Hermitian completions via moments and subdifferentials
abstract: Given a Hermitian matrix $A_0$ and a real subspace $W$ of Hermitian matrices, we study the matrices $A_0+W_0$, $W_0\in W$, of minimal spectral norm, which we call $W$-minimal. The main motivation is the Hermitian matrix completion problem, where $W$ is spanned by the Hermitian matrix units corresponding to the unspecified entries. Our main tool is the moment of a subspace $S\subseteq\mathbb{C}^n$ relative to $W$, a compact convex subset of $\mathbb{R}^r$, $r=\dim(W)$, which we relate to the joint numerical range and to the $k$-dimensional field of a family of matrices. We compute the subdifferential of $\|A_0+W(x)\|$ in terms of the moments of the eigenspaces of the extreme eigenvalues of $A_0+W(x)$, and we obtain several equivalent characterizations of $W$-minimality: in terms of eigenvectors, of moments, of subdifferentials and of norm one functionals that annihilate $W$. When the identity belongs to $W$, every $W$-minimal matrix has balanced spectrum, and minimality is equivalent to the moments of the eigenspaces of the maximum and minimum eigenvalues having nonempty intersection; we show that this characterization fails if $I\notin W$. We illustrate the results with several examples, and we prove that the adjacency matrix of a connected graph is minimal for its completion problem if and only if the graph is complete bipartite.

title: Transport Less, Solve Faster: Exploiting sparsity in algorithm design for Unbalanced Optimal Transport
abstract: In this paper, we study the computational aspects of the Unbalanced Optimal Transport (UOT) problem between two given positive measures $μ$ and $ν$. The UOT is a variant to the classic Optimal Transportation problem in which the linear constraints modeling mass preservation are relaxed and replaced by a convex penalty $\Dphi$ in the objective function. First, we show that any UOT problem admits a discrete solution as long as $μ$ and $ν$ are discrete, allowing us to express the optimality conditions characterizing the solution to the UOT problem in an easy-to-handle form. By exploiting the optimality conditions we provide an upper and lower bound on the marginals of the solution as well as a bound on the mass that any solution assigns to any couple of points. The bounds on the mass assigned to each couple of points reveal that, under suitable conditions, the support of any solution to the UOT is contained within a compact set that does not depend on the measures $μ$ and $ν$, but only on the penalty function $\Dphi$ and the cost function $c$. We then introduce a truncated version of the UOT problem that fully leverages the sparsity of the optimal solution by introducing a parameter $R$ that saturates $c$. We show that any solution to the truncated problem naturally yields an approximation of the optimal solution for the standard UOT problem and bound the primal sub-optimality gap between the real solution and the solution induced by the truncated problem via a decreasing power-like function of $R$. Lastly, we study the convergence speed of the Pairwise Frank-Wolfe algorithm when applied to the truncated UOT problem and show that such routine is able to identify the support of the solution within a finite number of iterations.

title: Cobordism maps and Atiyah-Floer isomorphisms for framed instanton homology I
abstract: We prove that isomorphisms of the type constructed by Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy, between framed instanton homology and the Lagrangian Floer homology of a Heegaard splitting, intertwine the cobordism maps of Kronheimer and Mrowka with maps defined by holomorphic curves alone, over the field of two elements. This holds for every connected cobordism between connected three-manifolds carrying a framed arc between its ends and an $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ bundle trivialized along the ends and the arc. The symplectic maps count holomorphic triangles in moduli spaces of flat connections on surfaces, with the correspondence of a compression body as boundary condition for one- and three-handles. Consequently these maps are independent of the handle decomposition and of the Heegaard data, and form a functor isomorphic to framed instanton homology; where both are defined, our isomorphisms agree with those of Daemi, Fukaya and Lipyanskiy modulo two. The proof rests on two analytic results for the mixed anti-self-duality and holomorphic curve equation: an adiabatic limit in which a compression body collapses next to a holomorphic strip and becomes the Lagrangian boundary condition of its flat connections, and an excision theorem along a torus.

title: Finite Subgroups of Birational Automorphism Groups of Severi--Brauer Surfaces
