abstract: We prove that a finite group acting birationally on a non-trivial Severi--Brauer surface $S$ over a field $\mathbb{K}$ of positive characteristic not equal to $3$ is isomorphic either to a subgroup of group of biregular automorphisms of $S_{\mathbb{K}^{per}}$ or to a subgroup of $μ^3_3$, where $μ_3$ is a cyclic group of order $3$ and $\mathbb{K}^{per}$ is the perfect closure of a field $\mathbb{K}$. Combined with results about classification of finite subgroups of the group of biregular automorphisms of $S$, this gives a classification of finite subgroups of the group of birational automorphisms of $S$.

title: Coefficient Riemann--Hilbert for an Affine Singular Foliation
abstract: For the affine foliation $\langle x\partial_x,y\partial_x\rangle$, we prove that smooth coefficient integration is a strictly unital $A_\infty$ quasi-equivalence on every ordinary open subset of $\mathbb R^2$, for globally bounded, degreewise finite-projective real coefficient bodies, allowing internal cohomology of nonconstant rank. A horizontal-hull restriction of a finite Lie $2$-groupoid model admits a smooth simplicial section of the comparison from full Maurer--Cartan integration, with a homotopy relative to all unit-generated simplices. Strict differentiation and two relative Hom models yield a real-linear chain map whose internal-degree diagonal is the identity. Its inverse is a finite sum acting directly on the possibly rank-jumping body complex. Global acyclicity of the differentiation kernels gives invertible counits that are the identity on the body. Infinitely flat and nongeneric rank-jumping examples illustrate the nonregular theorem. Separately, regular two-term coefficients admit a residue classification and an exact ordinary-quotient descent criterion. Nonzero residue obstructs pullback through any strict map to an ordinary groupoid nerve with represented objects in the stated raw coefficient theory. For regular vertical families over $S\times\mathbb R^2$, we also prove a finite-projective bundle-valued theorem natural under smooth parameter pullback; its two-term invariants are bundle arrows, rather than pointwise rank profiles.

title: An Alternative Proof of the SPR Synthesis Theorem for Polynomial Segments of Arbitrary Order
abstract: For any positive integer n and any two monic real Hurwitz polynomials of degree n, every convex combination of the two is Hurwitz stable if and only if there exists a common numerator of degree n that makes both endpoint transfer functions strictly positive real. We give a unified proof based on convex separation, contact interpolation, and analytic properties of weakly positive real functions.

title: On the homotopy automorphism group of simply-connected homology $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$
abstract: In this paper, we compute the group of homotopy equivalences of closed, smooth, simply connected $6$-manifolds whose integral homology groups are isomorphic to whose of the complex projective space $\mathbb C \mathrm P^3$, building on computations of their mapping class groups.

title: Local Aronson-Bénilan estimates for the porous medium and fast diffusion equations on collapsing manifolds
abstract: We establish local Aronson-Bénilan estimates for positive solutions to the porous medium and fast diffusion equations on complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds with a small scale-invariant integral bound on the negative part of the Ricci curvature in $L^p$, where $p>n/2$. No uniform lower bound on the volume of unit balls is assumed, and hence the results apply to manifolds that may collapse. For the fast diffusion equation, we obtain the estimate in the range $1-2/n<m<1$. The auxiliary function method, which was designed for the heat equation under integral curvature conditions, is not directly applicable to those two nonlinear equations. The pressure operator in both cases contains a solution-dependent coefficient, which produces a residual term involving $\partial_t J$ in the evolution inequality. Its treatment requires a positive lower bound for $J$, and moreover, control of $-\partial_t\log J$. We obtain these bounds by linearizing the auxiliary equation, applying Duhamel's formula, and combining local Dirichlet heat kernel estimates with a singular Volterra inequality. Additionally, in the fast diffusion case, the negativity of $v$ changes the sign structure of the evolution inequality, so a separate coercive estimate is required to close the argument. Local Aronson-Bénilan estimates follow for both diffusion regimes and integrating them along space-time curves gives the corresponding Harnack inequalities.

title: A Hierarchical Variational Inequality Approach to Generalized Nash Equilibrium Seeking with Nonlinear Shared Constraints
abstract: We study the computation of variational generalized Nash equilibria (v-GNE) in games with strongly monotone pseudo-gradients and nonlinear convex shared constraints. We show that the v-GNE problem is exactly equivalent to a hierarchical variational inequality, whose lower level is given by the gradient of a smooth convex penalty of the constraint violation over the local action sets. Building on this reformulation, we propose a hierarchical regularization scheme that operates entirely in the primal space and requires only projections onto the local action sets. In the centralized setting, we prove last-iterate squared distance convergence to the v-GNE with rate $O(1/t^{\scriptscriptstyle 2/3})$ under a local error bound condition, which holds, e.g., under Slater's condition, improved to $O(1/t)$ under a global error bound condition. We then extend the scheme to the partial-decision information setting, where the agents communicate over a network and maintain local estimates of the joint action. We derive a distributed algorithm with a constant stepsize operating in the primal space and converging to the v-GNE with rate $O(1/t)$.

title: Restrictions to a principal $A_1$-subgroup
abstract:
We consider simple simply-connected algebraic groups $G$ over the complex numbers, and a principal $A_1$-subgroup $A \leq G$. We show that for most types of $G$ all its irreducible representations $V(λ)$ ($λ$ a dominant weight) are determined by their restrictions to $A$ up to graph automorphisms.
  The exceptions are groups $G$ of type $A_l$ with $l \geq 5$ and $G$ of type $D_l$ with $l = 4^m$ and $m \geq 2$.

title: On the index of two-dimensional elliptic end-periodic operators
abstract: This paper investigates the index problem for elliptic end-periodic differential operators on a two-dimensional manifold with a cylindrical end. We define the topological index as the sum of the contribution of the interior symbol, expressed by an Atiyah--Singer type integral, and the contribution of the limit operator, expressed in terms of the Melrose type eta-invariant and a correction term that depends on the lower order terms of the limit operator. We prove the homotopy invariance of the topological index, which allows us to reduce the original problem to the study of operators of a simpler form by employing $K$-theoretic methods.

title: Discrete Spoilers: Introducing Abstract Undergraduate Mathematics Using Graph Theory
abstract: Students often have serious difficulties with many key concepts of the undergraduate mathematics curriculum. We argue that many of these difficulties can be eased by explicitly separating the key ideas from the technical details. To do so, we present finite graphs as a setting where the basic concepts appear more transparently, because on a graph most proofs only require basic techniques from linear algebra. We illustrate this approach in three areas that cover a large part of the curriculum. First, we explain basic operators from vector calculus, such as the gradient and the divergence, through the incidence matrix of a graph. Second, we show that the diffusion equation has a simple solution on a graph. We also solve the graph Dirichlet problem, in which the values at some vertices are fixed. Third, we introduce a second incidence matrix that illustrates homology, cohomology and the Helmholtz decomposition in a simple way. Finally, we outline how to apply this approach to other branches of mathematics.

title: Consistency considerations for rare-event importance sampling
abstract: We consider the problem of estimating a small probability $p = P(X \in A)$ by importance sampling with auxiliary density $g$, where $X$ is drawn according to some density $f$. We establish a simple necessary and sufficient condition for the consistency of the importance sampling estimator in triangular schemes where the dimension, the densities $f$ and $g$ and the set $A$ may evolve. It allows to refine the results of Chatterjee and Diaconis [Ann. Appl. Probab. 28 (2018), no. 2, 1099-1135] by establishing the exact minimal sample size required for consistency. Moreover, it allows to study the regime $p \to 0$ which, despite being the relevant mathematical regime for rare-event estimations, has received very little attention so far. We perform an in-depth study of the hyperplane case $A = \{x: x^\top u \geq α\}$ with Gaussian densities, showing that in this case, the optimal importance sampling density considerably improves consistency compared to the standard Monte Carlo estimator. However, we conclude the paper with moment considerations which suggest that, whenever the Monte Carlo and optimal importance sampling estimators both converge, convergence may occur faster for the Monte Carlo estimator.

title: The inscribed $4$-polytope of maximal volume with nine vertices
abstract: We prove that a $4$-polytope with nine vertices inscribed in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $\frac{5}{24}\sqrt{10 + 2\sqrt{5}}$, and that, up to orthogonal transformations, equality holds only for the convex hull of a square and a regular pentagon inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ in orthogonal $2$-planes through the origin. For the combinatorial type of this polytope, whose boundary complex is the join of a $4$-cycle and a $5$-cycle, we write the signed volume as the pairing, through the Hodge star, of the area vectors of the two cycles, and bound each area vector by finite Fourier analysis; the bound holds for every choice of nine points on the sphere. Since an optimal polytope is simplicial, by a result of Horváth and Lángi, it remains to exclude the other simplicial types, which we do by sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic.

title: Prime supports and vanishing in restricted coprime representations
abstract: We study the prime supports that eliminate every representation of an even integer $N$ by two positive integers coprime to $6P$. Let $J(k)$ be the largest vanishing instance obtainable with at most $k$ factors of $P$ not dividing $N/2$. We prove $k(\log k)^2\ll J(k)\ll_\varepsilon k^{4+\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. The upper bound follows by comparing a classical family of shifted-prime representations with a two-dimensional upper sieve for the loss at each additional factor. Retaining the same local density factor in both estimates yields a weighted survival criterion and positivity whenever the number of noncolliding factors above $N^θ$ is sufficiently small compared with $N^θ$, for fixed $0<θ<1/4$. An exact reduction separates a minimum prime cover into forced prime-pair contributions and a residual problem, and gives the lower bound for $J$ along powers of two. Residue occupancies characterize the extremal concentration at a first zero. Explicit discrepancy estimates show that supports with at most eleven factors cannot eliminate every representation when $N>2780460$, nor supports with at most seven noncolliding factors when $N\ge2266292$. Positivity for the complete support of primes up to $\sqrt N$ remains open.

title: On the dynamics of weighted shifts on Fréchet sequence spaces over trees
abstract: In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fréchet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of Köthe spaces $λ_p(A,V)$, where $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ and $V$ is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces $\ell^p(V)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$, and $c_0(V)$.

title: Topological and measurewise amenability for locally compact groupoids
abstract: We prove the equivalence of topological and measurewise amenability for $σ$-compact locally compact groupoids with a Hausdorff unit space and a continuous Haar system. This in particular includes the second countable locally compact Hausdorff case. Our proof averages arbitrary Radon probability measures along strictly positive densities to obtain quasi-invariant measures. We overcome the lack of absolute continuity of the original measure with respect to its quasi-invariant substitute by also averaging the Reiter functions along the same density.

title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension six
abstract: We summarize a coordinate-free classification of six-dimensional real Lie algebras up to isomorphism. Instead of solving the overdetermined Jacobi system of 120 quadratic equations on 90 structure constants modulo $\mathrm{GL}(6,\mathbb{R})$, the method uses the Levi--Malcev decomposition, Mostow's nilradical constraints, and the Skjelbred--Sund cohomological central extension technique. In the semisimple sector, the four real forms of $A_1\oplus A_1$ are classified by Killing signature invariants, with explicit matrix representatives for $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})_{\mathbb{R}}\cong\mathfrak{so}(3,1)$. For non-solvable algebras with three-dimensional radical, representation-theoretic rigidity shows that $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ cannot couple indecomposably with non-abelian radicals, yielding exactly three indecomposable classes governed by $\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$. In the solvable category, Mostow's theorem restricts the nilradical dimension to $\{3,4,5,6\}$. The nilpotent sector in dimension six has twenty-four indecomposable isomorphism classes plus decomposable counterparts. Solvable non-nilpotent algebras are classified by nilradical codimension, with explicit real Jordan matrix representations for codimension one and two that resolve continuous moduli under gauge actions. The work also computes the minimal faithful representation dimension $μ(\mathfrak{g})$ under Ado's theorem, relates the classification to invariant complex structures on nilmanifolds, and provides a deterministic, page-breakable identification algorithm.

title: An introduction to discrete dynamics in condensed sets: orbits, periodic loci, and arithmetic examples
abstract: We formulate discrete dynamics internally in the topos Cond of condensed sets. For an endomorphism $f\colon X\to X$, we construct orbit quotients, backward histories, preimage trees, and periodic loci as objects evaluated on profinite parameter spaces. The framework recovers global-section dynamics, fully faithfully embeds compact Hausdorff systems, characterizes the invertible extension, and is compatible with inverse limits. It organizes $p$-adic congruence towers and shows, for a Cantor-type non-Archimedean Julia set, that classical periodic points can be dense although the internal periodic locus is not isomorphic to the compact condensed Julia set.

authors: with an appendix written jointly with Anand Deopurkar
title: Extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces without Gaussian maps and classification of prime Fano threefolds
abstract: In arXiv:2409.03960 an approach to the question of extendability of projective varieties via degeneration to ribbons was introduced, and in arXiv:2503.12661 it was used to give a new proof of optimal results on the extendability of general non-prime $K3$ surfaces and the classification of non-prime Fano threefolds. In this article we treat the prime case. We give a new proof of the optimal results on the extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces of every genus, of the classification of prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank one due to Fano, Iskovskikh and Mukai, and of the irreducibility of their Hilbert schemes. This involves degenerations of $K3$ surfaces to ribbons on embedded rational normal scrolls, called $K3$ carpets. We compute exactly the cohomology of the twisted normal bundle of these $K3$ carpets, instead of computing coranks of Gaussian maps of the canonical curve sections. The key challenge is to analyze the coboundary map of the sequence relating the normal bundle of the $K3$ carpet to the normal bundle of the scroll. We give a deformation theoretic interpretation of this map. Given such a $K3$ carpet and its hyperplane section, which is a canonical ribbon, we show that the coboundary map corresponds to the obstruction to lifting a first order deformation of the underlying scroll fixing the underlying rational normal curve to a first order deformation of the $K3$ carpet fixing the canonical ribbon. To compute the obstruction, we use a result on extensions of non-split ribbons on any curve to a unique $K$-trivial carpet in a canonical way.

title: How good are spline spaces for the Kolmogorov $n$-width of a Sobolev ball?
abstract: This paper studies the approximation power of polynomial splines on a uniform one-dimensional mesh. The quality of the best approximation of the unit ball of $H^{s}$ by an $n$-dimensional subspace, measured in the $L^{2}$ norm, is quantified by the sup-inf of that space: for each function in the Sobolev ball, take its minimal approximation error over the space, and then take the supremum of these errors over the ball. The infimum of this sup-inf over all $n$-dimensional spaces is the well-known Kolmogorov $n$-width $d_{n}$. Choosing the $n$-dimensional subspace to be the piecewise polynomial space of degree $k$ with smoothness $C^μ$ ($-1\leμ\le k-1$) gives our sup-inf $E$. The approximation accuracy of spline spaces is then examined by comparing $d_{n}$ and $E$. The two quantities are determined by two eigenvalue problems, through which we obtain a lower bound for $d_{n}$ and an upper bound for $E$. Under the restriction $k\ge s-1$, the upper bound for the error of the maximally smooth spline space ($μ=k-1$) is asymptotically equal to the lower bound for $d_n$, showing that uniform $B$-splines are asymptotically optimal among all $n$-dimensional spaces. For $μ<k-1$, we prove that $E/d_n$ is bounded below by a constant strictly larger than $1$, except when $k>s-1$ and $μ=k-2$ hold simultaneously. This reveals the superiority of $B$-splines in the sense of $n$-widths. Numerical experiments corroborate these bounds and, in some cases (e.g. the exception above), show that they are sharp.

title: Quenched large deviation estimates for skew product systems with the almost-sure fiber specification property
abstract: We establish quenched level-2 large deviation estimates for empirical measures of measurable skew products with compact metric fibers over an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation on a Polish space. Our hypotheses are formulated through lower and upper energy functions, which describe the exponential decay of conditional measures of fiber Bowen balls. Under almost-sure fiber specification, we prove lower bounds for open sets. Upper bounds for closed convex sets require only the upper energy condition, and upper semicontinuity of fiber entropy removes the convexity restriction. When these hypotheses hold with a common energy function \(T\), we obtain a quenched level-2 large deviation principle with a good rate function \(I_T(ρ)=\int T\,dρ-h_ρ(F)\) on invariant measures with the prescribed base marginal, and \(+\infty\) otherwise. We also derive quenched level-1 large deviation principles for bounded continuous observables and a quenched Laplace principle. As an application, we consider skew products that are Anosov and topologically mixing on fibers. For Gibbs equilibrium states associated with random potentials $f$ having integrable two-sided Bowen variation, we construct bounded strictly positive common energy functions by coboundary corrections. This construction identifies the large deviation rate on invariant measures as \(π_F(f)-h_ρ(F)-\int f\,dρ\), where \(π_F(f)\) denotes the fiber topological pressure.

title: Calculation and Recurrence Relations of the Determinants of the Hessenberg - Toeplitz Matrices
abstract: The determinant D(n) of a n x n Hessenberg - Toeplitz matrix is given as product of certain functions of its elements. A compact expression of D(n) is presented and recurrence relations involving determinants and matrix elements of the Hessenberg -Toeplitz matrices are found.

title: Automorphisms of Kummer and Artin-Schreier curves defined by Chebyshev polynomials
abstract: Let phi_m be the monic Chebyshev polynomial characterized by phi_m(t + t^-1) = t^m + t^-m. We study the geometric automorphism groups of the smooth projective models of y^n = phi_m(x) and y^p - y = phi_m(x). We classify the hyperelliptic family in genus at least two, in characteristic zero and odd characteristic. For every m >= 5, with p not dividing m in positive characteristic, we determine the projective stabilizer of the roots of phi_m together with infinity. For tame Kummer covers, we describe the normalizer of the cyclic deck group and compute it explicitly for m >= 6. It is the full group when m > 2n. If m >= 3 and n > 2m, the full group has order 2n in characteristic zero and in every characteristic prime to 2nm. The proof uses the dihedral Galois closure of the map to the y-line and Dickson's subgroup classification. In odd characteristic, we also classify all Artin-Schreier curves in the family with genus at least two. For m >= 3 prime to p >= 5, the group has order 2p. In characteristic three, exactly five degrees are exceptional. We give the groups and their actions, and treat the quadratic cases separately.

title: A tale of two periodicities
abstract: We provide a common explanation for two 4-periodic phenomena arising in the study of connective real K-theory: first, the family of twists of ko over $B\mathbb Z/2$, and second, the torsion in the Picard group of $Q_1$-local $\mathcal A(1)$-modules. These phenomena have been previously studied, as they lead to 4-periodic patterns in Smith homomorphisms, resp. in the ko-homology of $(B\mathbb Z/2)^n$. In this paper, we exhibit both of these 4-periodicities as consequences of an isomorphism of two extraspecial groups of order 32.

title: Non-Uniqueness of Weak Solutions to the Unforced Two-Dimensional Euler Equations with Vorticity in $L^1\cap L^p$, Part II: The Nonlinear Construction
abstract: This paper and its companion Part I prove that the incompressible Euler equations in the plane, without external force, admit two distinct renormalized weak solutions with the same initial vorticity $f$, where $f$ is radial and nonnegative and lies in $(L^1\cap L^q)(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for every $q<\infty$ but is not bounded. One solution is radially symmetric and stationary. The other is $3$-fold rotationally symmetric, is equimeasurable with $f$ at every time, and departs from $f$ in finite time; the two solutions are distinct in $L^\infty_t(L^1\cap L^q)_x$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^2$ for every $q\in(4/3,\infty)$ and every sufficiently large $T$. The nonstationary solution belongs to $C([0,\infty);L^q(\mathbb{R}^2))$ for every $q\in[1,\infty)$. Part I establishes a compactness criterion for non-uniqueness and conditional linear instability results for a vortex ring. Part II establishes the hypotheses of those results and proves the nonlinear non-uniqueness theorem.

title: Local vanishing density of order $1$ and Divisor moments
abstract: We establish a general framework relating local vanishing densities of order $1$ to logarithmic growth of divisor moments on regular arithmetic curves. As applications, we recover classical divisor moment estimates for polynomial values and establish their function field analogue. Furthermore, under GRH, we obtain a result on divisor moments for polynomials in the Fourier coefficients of non-CM cuspidal eigenforms with trivial nebentypus and trivial inner twist. The Fourier coefficients need not be integers, and the polynomials need not be squarefree. Under additional analytic hypotheses, we also allow a Sato--Tate angle restriction.

title: Lagrangian tori in the three-dimensional quadric and mirror symmetry
abstract:
In the three-dimensional quadric, we study the Oakley--Usher torus and its Chekanov counterpart as defined by the authors in the companion paper \cite{OU1}. Computing the versal deformation of the $Ψ$-invariant of Shelukhin--Tonkonog--Vianna, we find that the Chekanov Oakley--Usher torus is knotted in a strong sense: it is not Hamiltonian isotopic to the Biran-lift of any Vianna torus in the two-dimensional quadric. Furthermore, we investigate enumerative properties of the Oakley--Usher torus in $Q^3$ and prove its non-displaceability, settling an open question asked by Oakley--Usher. We relate this to mirror symmetry by proving a split-generation result for the monotone Fukaya category of $Q^3$. This should be viewed as the analogue of a result by Abouzaid--Diogo after compactifying. Interestingly, in the compactification, the monotone copy of the $(S^1 \times S^2)$-generators of Abouzaid--Diogo becomes displaceable. On the other hand, the Oakley--Usher torus still appears as a generator.
  In the appendix joint with Soham Chanda, we give an alternative construction of the Chekanov Oakley--Usher torus using a double solid torus mutation. This allows us to compute its disk-potential using wall-crossing results.

title: Zero extension for the Dirichlet problem on graphs
abstract: Solutions of the Dirichlet problem on a finite part of a weighted graph are extended by zero, together with their source, to a larger connected part. A necessary and sufficient condition is proved for the extended function to remain a solution of the corresponding Dirichlet problem on the enlarged domain: at every newly included vertex adjacent to the original part, the weighted sum of the solution over its neighbors in that part must vanish. The admissible sources are characterized as the orthogonal complement of the harmonic extensions from the enlarged domain to the original part, their space has dimension equal to the number of vertices of the original part minus the rank of the interface coupling, and an exact energy identity for the extension error follows from a Schur complement of the graph Laplacian. The same reduction covers other boundary conditions, including the Neumann problem, and extends to higher powers of the Laplacian, where the boundary data must be compatible with the lower-order interface traces. The discrete criterion is compared with its continuous counterpart, and no result in this form has been reported on Riemannian manifolds.

title: Restricted Quantum unique ergodicity under Generalized Lindelöf conjecture
abstract: Assume the generalized Lindelöf hypothesis. Let $u$ be an even Hecke--Maass cusp form on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}$, normalized in $L^2$ with respect to hyperbolic area, with Laplace eigenvalue $1/4+T^2$. For every fixed $ψ\in C_c((0,\infty);\mathbb{C})$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove that \[ \int_0^\infty ψ(y)|u(i y)|^2\frac{d y}{y} =\frac{6}π\int_0^\infty ψ(y)\frac{d y}{y} +O_{ψ,\varepsilon}(T^{-1/4+\varepsilon}) \] as $T\to\infty$, uniformly in $u$. In particular, the restriction mass equidistributes on every fixed compact segment of the imaginary axis in $\mathbb{H}$.

title: Total Variation Regularized Barycenters in Wasserstein Space
abstract: We study total variation regularization of Wasserstein barycenters on bounded connected Lipschitz domains. We prove existence for arbitrary prescribed probability measures and uniqueness when at least one is absolutely continuous. Our main results are attained dual formulations in terms of relative perimeters and vector fields with zero normal trace. These yield necessary and sufficient optimality conditions and a variational characterization of superlevel sets. We also establish a maximum principle on convex domains, stability of minimizers, and an exact reduction to a single TV-JKO step in one dimension. The existence, uniqueness, and perimeter duality results extend to costs $|x-y|^p$, $p>1$, under the same assumptions.

title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
abstract: We prove that every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits, near each point, a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, and that this universal dimension is optimal. A Gram criterion constructs a regular analytic embedding of the Euclidean metric from a rational positive semidefinite tensor obtained by signed evaluations. A specified finite-field minor certifies characteristic regularity. The real-principal-type construction of Nakamura and Maeda gives openness of the metric map on a fixed ball. Rescaling then applies it to arbitrary smooth metrics.

title: Strong relaxed dynamics in stochastic control
abstract:
We characterize relaxed dynamics for which any finite family of strong state solutions, together with their relaxed inputs, can be approximated by the prescribed controlled dynamics, ground-stably in law.
  Relaxed inputs include parametrizations of relaxed controls over the unit interval. Unlike relaxed controls, these parametrizations determine action couplings. The proposed relaxed dynamics is driven by a single cylindrical Brownian motion in a Hilbert space. For each relaxed input, its state is the unique strong solution of the corresponding equation. The collection of these states, over all relaxed inputs, satisfies the approximation requirement.
  Conversely, suppose one assigns to each relaxed input a continuous adapted state process on a fixed probability space. Pairwise approximation forces the assignment to be the strong solution map of the same dynamics, for a unique cylindrical Brownian driver. In fact, even for a state map indexed by (non-parametrized) relaxed controls, the relevant relaxed control class admits coherent parametrizations under separability and finite-family approximation assumptions, and the same type of dynamics is recovered again.

title: On the structural aspects of Convex Subhyperlattices under different orders
abstract: Nayak et al. (2025) introduced the concept of convex subhyperlattices of a strong join hyperlattice $\mathfrak{L}$ and demonstrated that the collection of all convex subhyperlattices, $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$, together with empty set, forms a lattice. In particular, for $P$-hyperlattices and Nakano hyperlattices, they obtained a unique representation of convex subhyperlattices in terms of hyperideals and hyperfilters. In the present work, we extend these studies by proving that $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L}) \cup \{\emptyset\}$, under set inclusion, forms an algebraic lattice. Moreover, we introduce two new orders on $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$ and examine their properties, including conditions for equivalence of these orders. In the class of $P$-hyperlattices, we characterize convex subhyperlattices in terms of initial and final segments, providing a structural insight into their formation. When convexity is extended to arbitrary join hyperlattices, many results known for $P$-hyperlattices and Nakano hyperlattices fail to hold. To address these limitations of convexity in arbitrary hyperlattices, we introduce the notion of strongly convex sets, denoted $\operatorname{SC}(\mathfrak{L})$, which naturally generalizes the concept while preserving its fundamental properties and extends the applicability of results to a wider setting. We establish several results for $\operatorname{SC}(\mathfrak{L})$ that do not hold for $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$.

title: An Introduction to Applied Probability and Stochastic Processes: Open Lecture Notes
abstract: These open lecture notes provide a broad introduction to measure-theoretic probability and stochastic processes, with a focus on applications. Topics include probability spaces, conditional expectation, generating and characteristic functions, Markov chains in discrete and continuous time, convergence of random variables, Brownian motion, stochastic calculus, stochastic differential equations and their connection to partial differential equations, jump diffusions, stochastic control, optimal stopping, and Monte Carlo methods. Most chapters include exercises, and solutions are provided. The notes were written for a two-quarter course for first-year PhD students in applied mathematics, and should also be useful to graduate students in statistics, engineering, economics and finance. The LaTeX source is freely available on GitHub under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license, and readers are encouraged to fork the notes and contribute corrections, improvements, and new material.

title: Compact metric spaces as exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces
abstract:
The class of compact metric spaces (metric spaces which induce a compact topology), despite being an important class of metric spaces, is not closed under many natural constructions. For instance, infinite metric products of compact metric spaces will often fail to induce a compact topology, while on the other hand, the topological product of any family of compact metric spaces is always a compact topological space, evidencing a discrepancy between topological and metric products.
  The notion of metric compact Hausdorff space -- compact Hausdorff spaces equipped with a lower semi-continuous metric -- provides a class of spaces which keep track of metric data and topological data separately, thereby forming a complete and cocomplete category, while including all compact metric spaces.
  Our main contribution is that this inclusion can be characterised via universal property: the compact metric spaces are the exponentiable metric compact Hausdorff spaces with respect to a natural monoidal structure on the respective category.

title: New lower bounds for even and odd values of the partition function
abstract: Let $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ denote the numbers of integers $0\leq n< X$ for which the ordinary partition function $p(n)$ is odd and even, respectively. The Parkin--Shanks conjecture predicts that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)$ and $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)$ are both asymptotic to $X/2$. Bellaïche and Nicolas proved that $N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X} \log \log X$, while Zheng, building on work of Ono and Swaminathan, recently proved that $N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X)\gg \sqrt{X}$. We improve both bounds simultaneously by proving $\min\{N_{\mathrm{odd}}(X), N_{\mathrm{even}}(X)\}\gg X^{3/4}/(\log X \log \log X)$.

title: Martingale representations without finite or well-defined mean
abstract: The classical Strassen theorem characterizes convex order through martingale representations under the assumption of finite first moments. We show that a natural reformulation of the theorem remains true on the real line for distributions without finite or even well-defined means. We further investigate the higher-dimensional setting, where this equivalence fails in general. Martingale representations are nonetheless guaranteed in higher dimensions when every nonzero linear projection of the second marginal has undefined mean.

title: A novel Non-Homogeneous Local Representation of the Braid Group
abstract: We construct a non-homogeneous local representation of the braid group $B_n$ by tracking the labels of individual strands through successive crossings. Each generator acts through a $2\times2$ block whose position is determined by the crossing and whose coefficients depend on the ordered labels of the participating strands. Starting with the ansatz \[ M_{xy}=\begin{pmatrix}a_x&a_y\\ b_{xy}&c_{xy}\end{pmatrix}, \] for $n\geq3$, the cubic braid relations for arbitrary ordered triples of strands determine $c_{xy}=0$ and $b_{xy}=(1-a_x)/a_x$ in the nondegenerate branch. The moving-label rule leads to an explicit semidirect-product representation, for which we prove the Artin relations and use exact evaluations of the resulting symbolic matrices. In the special homogeneous specialization, where $a_x=a$ for every strand label $x$, the resulting matrix representation is diagonally equivalent to unreduced Burau. We prove that a non-homogeneous specialization of our representation detects Bigelow's explicit nontrivial $B_5$ Burau-kernel commutator. Thus the strand-dependent coefficients distinguish a nontrivial braid that is invisible to the classical Burau representation. This separation provides evidence that the non-homogeneous strand-tracking construction is a promising candidate for a faithful Burau-type representation.

title: Quantum channel bounds for constant-composition codes
abstract:
We extend the quantum-channel optimization of Alrabiah and Guruswami to $q$-ary constant-composition codes. We study explicit channel and flag constructions that recover selected classical asymptotic upper bounds, including the Ben-Haim--Litsyn, moving-subspace and Horn-channel bounds. We give two equivalent formulations, Gram and flag, and prove stability of the obtained upper bounds under permutation transport and generalized shortening. A hierarchy defined by bounding the output-state ranks within each flag improves strictly between consecutive levels at every composition and every positive distance below the Plotkin threshold.
  We provide finite matrix parametrizations of these bounds (i.e., the number of variables does not depend on the length of codes under consideration). Numerical optimization rapidly produces improvements over the known asymptotic upper bounds throughout all tested nonbinary parameter ranges. For rational input data, each finite level admits near-optimal feasible rational descriptions of polynomial length. Their feasibility can be checked exactly and their objective values computed to any prescribed accuracy in polynomial time; the associated threshold problem with a prescribed gap belongs to $\mathsf{PromiseNP}$.

title: Parallel domains in $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$ and the ideal triangle reflection group
abstract:
For a given positive triple of flags, we associate an open set, called a parallel domain, in the symmetric space of $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})$ whose boundary is parametrized by three spacelike geodesics of the pseudo-Riemannian symmetric space $SL_3 (\mathbb{R})/GL_2 (\mathbb{R})$. This construction is a higher-rank analog of how three points in the ideal boundary of the hyperbolic plane have an associated ideal triangle.
  As an application, using the fact that positive triples determine a representation of the ideal triangle reflection group into $SL_3(\mathbb{R})$, we show that these parallel domains are fundamental domains for the group action in the symmetric space. Moreover, using the explicit construction and combinatorial properties of the Farey tessellation, we compute the asymptotics for the critical exponent in the symmetric space and the Hilbert critical exponent as the triple ratio of the triple of flags goes to infinity.

title: Euclidean view-obstruction in dimensions eight to ten and the asymptotic deficit
abstract: The Euclidean view-obstruction problem asks for the critical radius of balls centered at the half-integer lattice that meet every positive ray from the origin. Writing $Δ_n$ for its square, we determine $Δ_8=8/17$, $Δ_9=1087/1980$ and $Δ_{10}=7/11$ by computer-assisted proofs using Kahlon's seven-dimensional theorem.The upper bounds combine full-support subspace averaging, projected lattice coverings and exact finite certificates; dimension ten also requires a finite search through short integer relations. Explicit directions attain all three values, including a ten-dimensional direction previously listed by Gritsenko, Skoruppa and Zagier. In arbitrary dimension, we express their theta-block invariant in geometric normalization and derive the known bounds $c\log(n+1) \le n/12 - Δ_n \le C\log^3(n+1)$, with repeated coordinates allowed throughout. Thus $Δ_n \sim n/12$, while the deficit tends to infinity more slowly than every positive power of $n$. The supplementary archive contains the executable verifiers, exact certificates and archived verification records.

title: The J-twist of the Dirac operator, spectral Einstein functionals and the noncommutative residue
abstract: We study spectral Einstein functionals associated with the $J$-twist of the Dirac operator on almost product Riemannian spin manifolds. On closed even-dimensional manifolds, we compute the corresponding noncommutative residue in terms of the Einstein tensor, the curvature of the connection determined by $D_J^2$, and its zero-order endomorphism. For four-dimensional compact manifolds with boundary, we consider two boundary residue functionals obtained by inserting two covariant derivatives in the first factor of the compositions $π^+(D_J^{-2})\circπ^+(D_J^{-2})$ and $π^+(D_J^{-1})\circπ^+(D_J^{-3})$. Under the stated collar and almost product structure assumptions, we calculate their interior and boundary contributions and obtain Dąbrowski--Sitarz--Zalecki type formulas. We also present applications of these results in physics and noncommutative geometry, focusing on spectral actions, spectral distance, and mean-curvature boundary contributions.

title: Embeddings for Orlicz potential spaces with applications to mixed local-nonlocal problems
abstract: In this paper, we provide further insight into potential spaces within the nonstandard framework of Orlicz functions. More precisely, we establish continuous and compact embeddings of potential spaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$ into both unweighted and weighted Orlicz spaces. Special attention is devoted to the radial setting, for which compactness results are obtained through Strauss- and Ni-type inequalities. As an application, we prove the existence of positive radial solutions to a class of Henon-type problems involving both local and nonlocal contributions in the Orlicz framework.

title: Nonlocal bilinear differential operators induced by a third order hypermetric in $\mathbb{R}^n$
abstract: The third order hypermetric $ρ(x,y,z)$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is given by the Euclidean distance of the point $(x,y,z)\in(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$ to the diagonal $Δ^{(3)}=\{(x,x,x):x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}$ of $(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$. In this paper, we consider local and nonlocal fractional versions of bilinear differential operators generated by the geometry induced by $ρ(x,y,z)=ρ(0,x-y,x-z)$ instead of the usual $|(x-y,x-z)|$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. In doing so, we obtain a fractional nonlocal version $\mathbb{D}^s(f,g)$, $0<s<1$, of the Dirichlet bilinear operator $\nabla f(x)\cdot\nabla g(x)$ which converges to this classical form when the fractional parameter approaches its endpoint $s=1$. We consider both the kernel approach and the Fourier multiplier version.

title: Unramified case of Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms
abstract: The Colliot-Thélène conjecture on quadratic forms asserts that any rationally isotropic nondegenerate quadratic form over a semilocal regular domain with $2$ invertible is isotropic. We prove the Colliot-Thélène conjecture for semilocal regular domains that are geometrically regular over a discrete valuation ring with $2$ invertible. In particular, this includes unramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, where $p\neq 2$.

title: Taylor Formulas for H-structures
abstract: We give a uniform second-order Taylor formula for tensorial Riemannian $H$-structures in Riemannian normal coordinates whose initial frame is $H$-adapted. For a defining multi-tensor $ξ$ with intrinsic torsion $T$, the linear coefficient is $T_q\diamondξ$, and the quadratic coefficient features the covariant derivative of $T$, its iterated diamond action, and curvature. The formula applies componentwise to tensors of arbitrary type and recovers the known $G_2$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(7)$ expansions. We also give the almost Hermitian specialisation and prove that vanishing of the complete second-order torsion contribution forces the intrinsic torsion to vanish at the centre of the coordinates.

title: DMP-Oriented Anisotropic Mesh Adaptation for SUPG Finite Element Methods for Time-Dependent Convection-Diffusion Problems
abstract: We study discrete bound preservation for fully discrete piecewise-linear streamline upwind Petrov--Galerkin (SUPG) finite element approximations of time-dependent convection--diffusion equations on anisotropic triangular meshes. Although the continuous homogeneous-source problem satisfies a parabolic maximum principle, SUPG approximations can exhibit nonphysical undershoots and overshoots. We derive sufficient nodal discrete maximum principle (DMP) conditions that account for the stabilized mass matrix, the combined effects of physical and streamline diffusion, time-step restrictions, and transfer between successive meshes. The analysis identifies a SUPG-effective diffusion tensor and motivates an anisotropic metric aligned with its inverse. We construct a combined metric that retains the effective-tensor geometry while introducing solution-dependent mesh density through recovered Hessian information. The resulting DMP conditions provide a theoretical basis for anisotropic mesh design. Numerical experiments for time-dependent transport problems with isotropic and moderately anisotropic diffusion demonstrate that, under mass-compatible limited SUPG stabilization, the combined metric substantially reduces measured undershoots relative to other methods at matched nominal mesh budgets, although improved bound behavior can carry an accuracy penalty. A controlled tensor--density comparison in the anisotropic transport test supports a contribution from the effective tensor beyond the prescribed mesh density.

title: The Gorsky-Oblomkov-Rasmussen conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$
abstract: We prove a generation theorem for the homology of certain Koszul complexes which naturally arise as the $E^1$ pages of the stable Rasmussen spectral sequence of torus links. Combining this theorem with recent work of Ballinger, Gorsky, Hogancamp, and Wang, we compute the stable Khovanov-Rozansky $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ homology of torus links and determine its Poincaré series, resolving conjectures of Gorsky, Oblomkov, and Rasmussen and their $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ analogs, over $\mathbb{Q}$. Using these results, we determine the Khovanov homology of $T(n,n-1)$ and $T(n,n)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, confirming conjectures of Shumakovitch and Turner and of the first author, which in turn allows us to compute the Khovanov skein lasagna module of $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.

title: Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels
abstract: This paper studies multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) quantum communication systems employing polarization-encoded discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), based on entanglement swapping, with the goal of extending secure communications beyond the reach of a direct link. The FSO channels are subject to atmospheric absorption, diffraction, beam wander, pointing errors, and turbulence-induced fading, while background noise and detector imperfections degrade the performance. An eavesdropper controlling the channels and the relay is also considered. To analyze the performance of the considered system, both hops MIMO channels are decomposed into parallel spatial eigenchannels via singular value decomposition (SVD), photon loss is modeled using Kraus operators, and a threshold-detector model is developed for the relay. Based on these models, closed-form per-eigenchannel expressions for the relay gain are derived, which are then used to obtain expressions for the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secret key rate (SKR). Numerical results demonstrate that entanglement swapping maintains a low QBER over longer distances than direct transmission, extending the communication range beyond the noise-limited cutoff of the direct link, at the cost of a lower SKR at short distances. The crossover distance beyond which entanglement swapping prevails is determined mainly by the background noise and the detector technology, and it is demonstrated to increase with MIMO configurations. Moreover, the reach gain is shown to be maximized for a midpoint relay. Finally, since each swapping event requires a single-pair emission from both sources, a near-deterministic entangled-photon source is required, which spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources do not provide at practical key rates, whereas MIMO substantially relaxes this requirement.

title: Error Estimates and Convergence Analysis for Learning Mechanism--AI Coupled Dynamical Systems
abstract: Mechanism--AI coupled dynamical systems retain known mechanisms while learning unknown dynamics from data. We study how neural approximation, numerical integration, finite observations, and optimization jointly affect the accuracy of this learning process. For time-dependent learned terms in a fixed compact admissible class, we derive a four-component objective error bound within an optimal control formulation. Explicit estimates are obtained for constrained ReLU approximation and Euler integration, with deterministic quadrature and random sampling treated separately. Under joint refinement, we establish $Γ$-convergence of the approximate objectives and show that approximate minimizers approach the continuous optimal set when the global optimization gaps vanish. We also derive conditional stability estimates for state-dependent learned terms. Numerical experiments with a susceptible--infected--recovered (SIR) model illustrate the analysis and show how solver resolution affects continuous-trajectory accuracy even when training losses are similar.

title: On the connected zero forcing polynomial of finite trees
abstract: Given a graph $Γ$ with vertex set $V(Γ)$ and a set of colored vertices S, the zero forcing rule is an iterative graph coloring process which states that a colored vertex with exactly one uncolored neighbor forces that neighbor to become colored. If repeated application of this rule eventually colors every vertex of $Γ$, the set $S$ is called a \emph{zero forcing set}. Now, if the induced subgraph $Γ\vert_S$ is connected, then $S$ is called a \textit{connected zero forcing set}. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the \emph{connected zero forcing number} $Z_C(Γ)$. A \emph{connected zero forcing polynomial} of a finite graph $Γ$ is a monic polynomial $Z_C^Γ(x) \;=\; \sum_{k} a_k x^k$, where $a_k$ counts the number of connected zero forcing sets of $Γ$ of size $k$, which we denote by $Z_C(Γ,k)$. In this paper, we find the connected zero forcing polynomial of any finite tree $T$. We then establish sharp lower bounds for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices. We also identify a family of trees, which we call uniform trees, and we prove that for any tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, there exists a uniform tree on $n$ vertices and $p$ many pendant vertices, whose connected zero forcing polynomial bounds as an upper bound, the connected zero forcing polynomial of the tree coefficient wise. Again for $2\leq p\leq 4$, we establish a sharp upper bound for each coefficient of the connected zero forcing polynomial, over all trees on $n$ vertices with $p$ many pendant vertices.

title: Optimal rational spherical designs on the circle
abstract: The minimum numbers of points in rational equal-weight spherical designs on the circle are $2304$, $4608$, $9216$, and $9216$ at strengths $4$, $5$, $6$, and $7$, respectively. We construct two nonisometric optimal designs at each strength. At arbitrary strength $t$, we obtain an explicit cardinality divisor $D_t$ with $\log D_t=(1/2+o(1))t\log t$. Applied to the antipodal pairs of a $4608$-point design, Gromov's torus construction gives a flat minimal immersion of $\mathbb{T}^2$ into $S^{4607}$ with $2304$ distinct integral frequencies, attaining Petrunin's sharp Euclidean normal-curvature bound.

title: Marginal Congruences and Elements for Two Commutator Words in Completely Regular Semigroups
abstract: Motivated by Problem 13 posed by Araújo, Araújo and Kinyon \cite{Araujo2025} concerning marginal elements, subsemigroups and marginal equivalences associated with commutator words in completely regular semigroups, in this paper we investigate the two commutator words $ ω_1(x,y)=x^{-1}y^{-1}xy$ and $ ω_2(x,y)=(yx)^{-1}xy$ on completely regular semigroups. We prove that their marginal equivalences $\sim_{ω_r}$ ($r=1,2$) coincide and are congruences. More precisely, for a completely regular semigroup $S$, we show that $a\sim_{ω_r}b$ ($r=1,2$) if and only if $a^0=b^0=p$ and $b^{-1}a\in Z(pSp)$, where $Z(pSp)$ is the center of the monoid $pSp$, and so both words have the same set of marginal elements: \[ M_ω(S) =\bigcup_{p\in E(S)} \bigl(Z(pSp)\cap H_p\bigr), \] where $E(S)$ is the set of idempotents in $S$. We also characterize when this set is a subsemigroup and establish alternative descriptions of the common marginal congruence and marginal elements.

title: Sharp Constants and First-Order Asymptotics in a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu Formula for Riesz Potentials
abstract: We investigate sharp constants and asymptotic properties of a pointwise inequality of Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type in dimension \(n\geq2\), involving Riesz potentials and Spector's nonlinear fractional differential operator \(\mathcal D^α\) of order \(0<α<1\). For every \(n\geq3\) and \(0<α<1\), we determine the optimal constant without symmetry restrictions and prove that it is attained by smooth radially monotone functions centered at the evaluation point. The proof combines geodesic-flow invariance, kernel monotonicity, and circular rearrangement. In dimension two, we establish the leading-order asymptotic behavior of the optimal constant and derive an explicit formula in the radial class. We further refine the pointwise limit established by A. Claros and C. Pérez [Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu formula for Riesz potentials, Adv. Math. 503 (2026), Art. 111226] by obtaining an explicit first-order correction with a quadratic remainder uniform in the spatial variable. Finally, we strengthen their convergence-in-measure result on compact subsets for functions in \(W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)\) by establishing almost-everywhere convergence as \(α\to1^-\), without passing to a subsequence.

title: A Lie-theoretic approach to the type $C_n^{(1)}$ partitions of Capparelli, Meurman, Primc and Primc
abstract: Capparelli, Meurman, Primc and Primc (CMPP) extended the frequency conditions in Gordon's partition theorem to paths in coloured arrays. Their conjecture for type $C_n^{(1)}$ identifies the generating function of admissible arrays with a principally specialized character. We prove this conjecture for arbitrary boundary data by constructing an ordered Poincaré--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) basis of the corresponding integrable highest weight module. A decomposition of the admissible arrays and a tensor product argument establish linear independence of the corresponding monomial vectors. To prove spanning, we use relations from annihilating fields and PBW bases for modules over finite Levi subalgebras. Principal specialization then yields the conjectured product. The same basis identifies the number of parts with the degree in the associated graded module for the PBW filtration.

title: Curvature estimates for stable hypersurfaces of the Euler-Dierkes-Huisken functional
abstract: A hypersurface $Σ\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is called EDH-stable if it is a critical point of the Euler-Dierkes-Huisken functional $\mathcal{E}_α(Σ)=\int_Σ|x|^α\, d\mathcal{H}^n$ with nonnegative second variation, which was introduced by Dierkes and Huisken in \cite{[DH-24]}. In this paper, we first establish a Bellettini-type $ε$-regularity theorem and use it, together with tangent cone analysis, to derive curvature estimates for EDH-stable hypersurfaces with $2\leq n \leq 6$.

title: Geometric classification of Noether invariants of the Time-Dependent damped Duffing Oscillator
abstract: We present a systematic geometric classification of the Noether point symmetries of time-dependent conformal Lagrangians of the form $L = A(t)\left(\frac{1}{2}g_{ij}\dot{x}^{i}\dot{x}^{j} - V(x)\right)$, whose Euler--Lagrange equations describe dynamical systems with time-dependent linear damping. The classification is carried out by coupling the temporal parameters of the conformal factor $A(t)$ with the homothetic algebra of the kinetic metric $g_{ij}$ through a set of compatibility and integrability conditions. The central result is a main theorem which determines the Noether generators, the associated gauge functions and the resulting invariants. The theorem splits naturally into two cases according to whether the quantity $D - 2ψ$ is non-zero or zero, with further subcases depending on whether the homothetic vectors are gradient or non-gradient. The theorem imposes no restrictions on $A(t)$, $g_{ij}$ or $V(x)$, and is therefore fully general and covariant. We apply the theorem to the time-dependent damped Duffing oscillator (DDO) in Euclidean space $E^{3}$ with $A(t) = e^{γt}$ and potential $V = \frac{1}{2}a\,r^{2} + \frac{% λ}{4}r^{4}$. For the damped harmonic oscillator ($λ= 0$) the theorem reproduces the classical Bateman invariant as a special case. For the anharmonic case we obtain a new exact time-dependent quadratic invariant, valid when the linear stiffness satisfies $a = 2γ^{2}/9$. Each invariant is verified explicitly by direct differentiation along the equations of motion. The new invariant provides a rare example of a global conservation law for a fully nonlinear dissipative system, and can be used for the integration and quantization of the DDO.

title: Absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology
abstract: We construct absolute mod-two gradings on framed real monopole Floer homology, for real 3-manifolds such that the image of the fixed point set in the quotient is nullhomologous. This allows us to fix the sign of Miyazawa's degree invariant. Our construction uses a mod-two index-theoretic correction term, the Arf invariant.

title: An Optimal First-Order Active-Hull Method for Convex Composite Hölder Smooth Optimization
abstract: We consider the problem (P): ${\min}_{x\in \mathbb{R}^n}\, f(x)+g(x)$ under the Euclidean geometry, where $f$ is convex and $(M,ν)$-Hölder smooth on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and $g$ is proper, closed and convex on $\mathbb{R}^n$, admits a generalized linear minimization oracle (GLMO), and has bounded domain with diameter $D$. An first-order active-hull (AH) method has access to both the first-order oracle (FO) of $f$ and the GLMO of $g$, and outputs a point that lies in the convex hull of all the past GLMO returns. We propose a new first-order AH method for solving (P), which is based on our newly developed ``recentered homotopy smoothing framework''. We show that in the high-dimensional regime, this method achieves the optimal FO and GLMO complexties simultaneously for all $ν\in[0,1]$.

title: The Brualdi--Quinn conjecture on strong edge-coloring holds fractionally and asymptotically
abstract: Let $G$ be a bipartite graph with parts $A$ and $B$, and let $Δ_A$ and $Δ_B$ be the maximum degrees of the vertices in $A$ and in $B$, respectively. Brualdi and Quinn conjectured that the strong chromatic index of $G$ is at most $Δ_AΔ_B$. We prove that the fractional strong chromatic index of $G$ is at most $Δ_AΔ_B$, and that the conjecture holds asymptotically: $χ_s'(G)\le(1+o(1))Δ_AΔ_B$ as $\max\{Δ_A,Δ_B\}\to\infty$. The error term is $12(\lnΔ)^{1/2}Δ^{-1/4}$ with $Δ=\max\{Δ_A,Δ_B\}$. Both results rest on a smart partition of edges and Lovász Local Lemma.

title: Eaton Triples, Polar Representations, and Lie Triple Systems
abstract: An Eaton triple consists of a finite dimensional real inner product space, a closed subgroup of its orthogonal group, and a closed convex cone that meets every orbit and satisfies an extremal inner product inequality. In the literature on group majorization and invariant norms it is a standing hypothesis that the triple admits a reduced triple, obtained by restriction to the span of the cone. We prove that this is always the case: the axioms force the span of the cone to be a section of a polar representation, and Gichev's orbit intersection theorem applies. The reduced group is a finite reflection group, crystallographic when the group is connected; Eaton cones are its closed chambers, unique up to the group action; and a compact linear group admits an Eaton cone if and only if its representation is polar with a finite reflection group as Weyl group. For connected groups we construct a Lie triple system on the space, determined by the inner product and the orbits alone, for which the cone is a Weyl chamber; unlike Dadok's orbit equivalence with a symmetric space, it involves no choices.

title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is sufficiently large. This strengthens the author's prior results and recovers Ebin's to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.

title: Efficient SC-Flip Decoding for Polar Codes through Decision-Boundary Normalization
abstract: Accurate first erroneous position (FEP) identification is key to improving the error-correction performance of successive cancellation flip (SCF) decoding. However, FEP identification remains challenging with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. To address this issue, we propose decision-boundary normalization (DBN) to improve FEP identification and develop a novel DBN-SCF decoding algorithm. DBN normalizes the magnitude of each decision log-likelihood ratio (LLR) by the standard deviation predicted by the Gaussian approximation (GA) for the corresponding bit-channel. This allows a single normalized threshold to be shared across bit-channels within each code configuration, giving it a consistent statistical meaning and avoiding per-channel calibration. DBN-SCF decoding selects candidate flip positions from the information set in the natural successive cancellation (SC) decoding order using a threshold, without sorting. Moreover, DBN-SCF decoding achieves better error-correction performance with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. It also requires lower average decoding complexity than existing SCF decoding methods at a comparable level of error-correction performance.

title: Gradient Estimation for LLM-Embedded Simulation Optimization
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded in operational simulators to represent context-dependent human decisions, which opens new possibilities for simulation optimization. However, the LLM acts as a black box, so derivatives through its decisions are unavailable for gradient-based policy search. Finite difference estimation can avoid this requirement, but the required paired simulations that sample LLM actions independently often disagree, and such action switches persist under small perturbations, which inflates the gradient variance to order $c^{-2}$ for perturbation radius $c$. To control this variance, we develop a behavioral common random number framework. It first applies maximal coupling to the LLM's action distributions, preserving each simulation's behavioral law while making action switches as rare as possible, which reduces the variance bound to $O(c^{-1})$. It then applies first-switch conditioning, which averages over whether a switch occurs, together with an impact-aware extension that prioritizes influential switches. Under suitable stability conditions, both keep the variance bounded as $c$ shrinks. We further establish improved complexity bounds for projected stochastic approximation. Experiments on synthesized and LLM-embedded simulators confirm the theory and show substantial performance gains.

title: BP-based qLDPC Decoding under Long-range Correlated Noise: Trapping Configurations and Prior Mismatch
abstract: We study the robustness of two state-of-the-art BP-based qLDPC decoders, Relay-BP and beam search, designed for independent noise when applied to spatially correlated noise with unchanged single-mechanism error probabilities. We generate correlated errors with a hidden Gaussian Markov random field, which lets us control the strength and range of the correlation while keeping every marginal error probability exact. This setting complements correlation-aware decoding: it asks how existing decoders perform when their assumed joint error model is mismatched. Across multiple tested circuits and code instances that we simulated, we observe that correlations can change logical error rates by orders of magnitude, reduce the finite-size distance advantage, and alter the relative ranking of Relay-BP, beam search, and BP-OSD. On one of the two tested circuits, Relay-BP and beam search become worse than BP-OSD, and increasing relay memory or beam width does not compensate for the degradation. Configuration analysis indicates that correlation primarily increases the probability of trapping configurations that are known to challenge these decoders; at matched error weight, correlated errors still cause decoding failures several times more often than i.i.d. errors. Finally, supplying the decoders with the marginals conditioned on the hidden field recovers most of the lost performance in the tested settings identifying prior mismatch as a major contributor to performance degradation under correlation.

title: Linear structure graphs associated with commuting graphs of Lie algebras
abstract: The commuting graph (CG) of a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field of characteristic zero forgets the linear structure, and a non-trivial center creates redundant vertices. We introduce linear structure graphs (LSGs), whose vertices are the nonzero vectors of a vector space and whose edge set is stable under linear operations. Each vertex generates a finite ascending sequence of subspaces, which defines its LSG-depth; this depth governs connectivity. We characterize LSGs of depth at most 1 and show that the CG of a Lie algebra with trivial center has depth at most 1 if and only if the algebra is a commutative transitive Lie algebra (CTLA). The reduced commuting graph (RCG) restricts the CG to a complement of the center; it is well defined up to LSG-isomorphism, preserves the connectivity, diameter and number of components of the CG, and is compatible with direct sums. Finally, we characterize almost abelian Lie algebras (AALAs) by their RCGs.

title: A sufficient condition for the Liouville property of solutions to the Euler-Lagrange equations of variational integrals with nonstandard growth in terms of the ellipticity modulus near the origin
abstract: We consider entire solutions $u$: $\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of the Euler-Lagrange equation $\operatorname{div}(\nabla f(\nabla u))=0$ with convex density $f$: $\mathbb{R}^{n}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ of nonstandard growth and nonuniform ellipticity. It turns out that the Liouville property can be characterized through the behavior of $D^{2}f(p)$ for points $p\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ close to the origin: if, for example, $D^{2}f(p)$ behaves as $|p|^{ρ-2}\mathbf{1}$, $\mathbf{1}=\text{unit matrix}$, with exponent $ρ\ge2$ and for $|p|\le1$ then the validity of $n\leρ+2$ together with the boundedness of $u$ implies its constancy.

title: A new butterfly in the meadow: magnetic lattice graphs with a circulant vertex coupling
abstract: We analyze the spectrum of quantum square lattice graph exposed to a homogeneous magnetic field with a rational flux through plaquette, assuming all nontrivial cases of the vertex coupling which is circulant and scale-invariant, with a particular attention to those of them that give rise to a dynamics violating the time reversal invariance. Except for two cases with partially decoupled edges, the remaining twelve split into two spectral classes; the second one offers a hitherto unknown butterfly pattern.

title: Directional weak mixing and directional Kronecker for $\Z^2$-actions
abstract: Let $T$ be a measure preserving $\Z^2$-action on a Lebesgue probability space $(X,μ)$ and let $L\subseteq\R^2$ be a $1$-dimensional subspace. For a rational subspace $L$, direction $L$ weak mixing corresponds to weak mixing for the measure preserving transformation $T^{\vv_0}$, where $\vv_0$ is a primitive vector in $\Z^2$ generating $L$. For an irrational direction $L$, we study two different definitions of direction $L$ weak mixing, and show that they are the same: ``Dynamical'' direction $L$ weak mixing is defined to be the absence of any direction $L$ Kronecker factors. These factors are defined in terms of almost periodicity along a finite width direction $L$ strip in $\Z^2$. ``Spectral'' direction $L$ weak mixing is defined as the absence of any direction $L^\perp$ line segments $I\subseteq\T^2$ with positive spectral measure. We also give a spectral characterization of the directional Kronecker property defined in \cite{liuxu}, and provide examples of $\Z^2$-actions $K$ that are direction $L$ Kronecker.

title: A 43-vertex 4-chromatic unit-distance graph in the plane with girth 5
abstract: We exhibit a set of 43 points in the Euclidean plane whose unit-distance graph has 83 edges, girth 5 and chromatic number 4. The smallest previously known 4-chromatic unit-distance graph of girth 5, due to Hochberg and O'Donnell (1996), has 45 vertices. The new graph is 4-critical, has trivial automorphism group, and has exactly 2n-3 edges; it is a Laman graph and its unit-distance realisation is infinitesimally rigid. The coordinates are algebraic numbers, specified as the unique real solution of an explicit system of 82 quadratic equations inside an explicit rational box. Every claim is certified by exact computation: existence and uniqueness of the realisation by a rational contraction-mapping certificate (independently re-checked with interval Krawczyk arithmetic), and non-3-colourability both by exhaustive search and by a DRAT proof verified with drat-trim.

title: A quantitative two-interval criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
abstract: We aim to study whether the Weil form can detect a zero of the Riemann zeta function away from the critical line using two functions with increasingly narrow, widely separated supports. We prove that the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on every such pair at all sufficiently large separations, provided the component widths decrease subexponentially. A zero to the right of the critical line forces the normalized cross term to exceed an exponential at arbitrarily large separations, with any exponent smaller than the horizontal displacement of that zero. In particular, reciprocal-width intervals suffice. Our proof combines a short-support positivity estimate, a smooth partition of fixed test functions and a pole obstruction for a one-sided Laplace transform. We also express the cross term through prime powers in a moving multiplicative interval. The resulting criterion specifies a uniform arithmetic inequality whose proof would establish the Riemann hypothesis.

title: The $ν$-core label order and noncrossing partitions
abstract: We prove that the poset of $s$-noncrossing partitions is isomorphic to the core label order of the $ν$-Tamari lattice introduced by Préville-Ratelle and Viennot.

title: A silting theorem for extended module categories
abstract: We generalize the silting theorem of Buan and Zhou to extended module categories. For a $(d+1)$-term silting object $\mathbf{P}$ over a proper $d$-truncated non-positive dg algebra $A$, we construct a $(d+1)$-term silting object $\mathbf{Q}$ over the $d$-truncated dg endomorphism algebra $B$ of $\mathbf{P}$. The $s$-torsion pairs induced by $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ yield equivalences of Brenner-Butler type between the torsion class on either side and the torsion-free class on the other. There is also a dg algebra homomorphism from $A$ to the $d$-truncated dg endomorphism algebra of $\mathbf{Q}$, which is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf{P},\mathbf{P}[i])=0$ for all $i\leq-d$. Moreover, we describe Auslander-Reiten theory in ${d\text{-}\operatorname{mod}\!B}$ in terms of that in ${d\text{-}\operatorname{mod}\!A}$.

title: Optimal Sampling and Transmission Policy for Information Freshness in Gossip Networks
abstract: We study the optimal sampling and transmission policies for a transmitter communicating with n gossiping receivers with the objective of tracking a source's status over time using a semantic freshness metric: Version Age of Information (VAoI). The transmitter observes the version changes in the source, and can acquire a new information version by paying a sampling cost. The receivers gossip, allowing information exchange among each other without direct transmission. Gossiping can save on transmission cost, but it may propagate stale version information, necessitating transmitter intervention. With imperfect communication links, we formulate an infinite horizon average cost Markov Decision Process (MDP) in order to jointly optimize receivers' VAoIs, sampling and transmission costs in a time slotted fully connected (FC) gossip network. We first solve the MDP using Relative Value Iteration (RVI) algorithm. Then, we prove that the sampling decision has a threshold structure in the transmitter VAoI. Further, under reliable gossiping links, we show that transmission and idling has an VAoI-difference threshold structure with minimum VAoI activation. Numerical results obtained using RVI show that the optimal policy consistently outperforms natural baselines. These results characterize how source sampling, direct transmission, and receiver gossip should be jointly coordinated for cost-aware semantic freshness in gossip networks.

authors: Miguel de los Ríos de Antonio
title: Quantum synchronizable codes, polynomial and quasi-polynomial shifts
abstract: Quantum synchronizable codes protect quantum information against Pauli errors and against misalignments of the block boundaries. Almost all known constructions use cyclic codes, because the channel shifts the transmitted block cyclically. We study what happens when the algebraic shift of the code differs from the physical one. When one uses a twisted padding, constacyclic codes synchronize at no cost, and they are the only polycyclic codes with this property for a linear padding. For the other polycyclic codes, we measure the cost of each misaligned position, and we show that the phase damage it causes can be corrected as erasures. Using annihilator duality, we extend the construction to quasi-polycyclic codes, in which the cost is confined to a single block. We prove that the usual quasi-cyclic families have a distance bound that does not grow with the length, and show that quasi-polycyclic codes over repeated-root trinomials overcome it, giving synchronizable codes with larger dimension and distance than the known synchronizable codes of the same length.

title: Sharp Constants and Maximizers for Weighted Moser--Trudinger Inequalities on the Heisenberg Group
abstract: This article concerns Moser-Trudinger inequalities on the entire Heisenberg group, focusing on sharp constants, maximizers, and applications to subelliptic PDEs. We address several questions on the existence of maximizers in the singular case $0<β<Q$, where the singular weight yields compactness. We first establish an Adimurthi-Druet-type weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality without blow-up analysis and determine its sharp constant. We also prove its equivalence with the critical weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality. For the subcritical inequality of Lam, Lu and Tang \cite{Lam-Lu-Tang-2014}, we obtain two-sided asymptotic bounds near the sharp threshold and prove existence of maximizers in a suitable regime. This inequality also yields insight into borderline Sobolev theory and an asymptotic Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg interpolation-type inequality. We further establish a weighted Moser-Trudinger inequality under inhomogeneous norm constraints and prove its equivalence with the subcritical inequality, thereby characterizing the associated supremum and its maximizers. An improved subcritical weighted inequality is also derived, and its maximization problem is shown to admit a maximizer. Finally, these inequalities are applied to normalized subelliptic equations driven by the $Q$-sub-Laplacian with nonlinearities having singular critical exponential growth at infinity. We prove the existence of nontrivial ground states for every prescribed mass $a>0$, provided the nonlinearity is sufficiently large in a suitable sense depending on $a$.

title: Hypervolume-based column-and-constraint generation for bi-objective two-stage robust mixed-integer programs
abstract: Extending column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) for two-stage robust mixed-integer programs from the single-objective to the bi-objective setting is challenging: for a fixed first-stage decision and scenario, the second stage yields an entire nondominated set rather than a single objective value. We develop a C&CG algorithm that uses the hypervolume indicator - one of the most widely studied quality indicators in multi-objective optimization - to evaluate these sets and seeks a first-stage decision maximizing the worst-case hypervolume over a finite set of scenarios. To avoid the nonlinearities of an exact hypervolume formulation, we introduce a slab decomposition of the objective space that yields a linear mixed-integer master problem with an explicit bound on the discretization error. This bound enables a computable optimality-gap certificate and supports an adaptive algorithm that alternates between adding scenarios and refining the decomposition. We prove the correctness of the algorithm and establish sufficient conditions for its finite termination. Computational experiments on two-stage robust selection and assignment problems show that only a small number of scenarios need to be included in the master problem, even when the full scenario set contains 128 scenarios. Moreover, we identify the number of initial slabs as a key factor influencing the running time and develop a simple, instance-dependent rule for choosing the initial slab width that outperforms fixed choices on average for the selection problem and remains competitive for the assignment problem.

title: A high-order structure-preserving ALE--SAV finite element method for moving contact line flows
abstract: We develop a structure-preserving arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) finite element method for incompressible Navier--Stokes flow with gravity and moving contact lines, based on a scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) reformulation. The reformulation expresses the geometric energy quadratically in the auxiliary variable and permits linear treatment of the capillary, wetting and gravitational forces.
