The method combines high-order isoparametric elements in space with a linearly implicit, second-order Crank--Nicolson discretization in time. Second-order extrapolation supplies the predicted geometry and known coefficients of the linear fluid--SAV system. Mesh motion changes the kinetic-energy inner product and requires a compatible discretization of the time-derivative terms in the ALE formulation. We discretize these terms using an $L^2$-isometric velocity transfer to retain the kinetic-energy balance after the geometry update. We also construct a boundary update that preserves area or volume exactly using only linear solves. The resulting scheme satisfies a discrete SAV energy-dissipation law and preserves area or volume exactly. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions demonstrate high-order spatial and second-order temporal convergence and confirm SAV energy dissipation and area or volume conservation.

title: Propagation phenomena in spatial periodic bistable reaction-diffusion equations around an obstacle
abstract: This paper is concerned with propagation phenomena for a spatially periodic bistable reaction--diffusion equation around an obstacle. It is known that an entire solution emanating from a pulsating front converges to the same front as \(t\rightaroow+\infty\) under complete propagation and an additional technical assumption. We remove the technical assumption and prove that the entire solution coming from a pulsating front converges to the same pulsating front as \(t\rightarrow+\infty\) under the complete propagation.

title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. II
abstract: Let $λ$ denote the Liouville function, and put \[ I_λ(X)=\int_0^1\left|\sum_{n\le X}λ(n)e^{2πi nα}\right|\,dα. \] In this paper, we prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log I_λ(X)}{\log X} \ge \frac{1}{3}. \]

title: New Classes of CCZ-Inequivalent APN Functions with Boomerang Uniformity One in Odd Characteristic: Differential and Boomerang Spectra
abstract: Let $q=p^n>3$ be an odd prime power and let $g:\F_q\to\F_q$ be an even perfect nonlinear (PN) function with $g(0)=0$. We construct almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions $G_{λ,M}(x)=g(x)+M(x)+λ(x^{q-1}-1)$, where $λ\in\F_q^*$, $-λ\notin g(\F_q)$, and $M$ is an $\F_p$-linearized permutation polynomial. These one-point modifications of $g+M$ have boomerang uniformity one, the smallest possible value for APN functions in odd characteristic. We give complete differential and boomerang spectrum formulas and obtain closed-form evaluations for selected constructions based on Coulter--Matthews monomials and Dembowski--Ostrom polynomials. For $q>7$, comparison of differential spectra establishes CCZ-inequivalence to all APN monomial families listed in the paper and every APN binomial in the original Ness--Helleseth family or its extension by Zeng et al. We characterize CCZ-equivalence within our construction, showing that any two linearly inequivalent even PN functions over the same field yield CCZ-inequivalent APN functions. We obtain three pairwise CCZ-inequivalent APN functions with boomerang uniformity one over $\F_{p^{15\ell}}$ for every $\ell\ge1$, six over $\F_{p^{120r}}$ for every $r\ge1$, and unbounded numbers of such classes in characteristic three. We further prove that CCZ-equivalence and EA-equivalence coincide for functions at Hamming distance at most $m$ from a PN function, provided that $m(m+1)<q-q/p$. We also show that all our APN functions have the maximal possible algebraic degree $n(p-1)$. Finally, we exhibit both CCZ-equivalent and CCZ-inequivalent APN pairs with boomerang uniformity one at Hamming distance one.

title: Local turnpike property for a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model
abstract: We study a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model. It couples Hamilton--Jacobi and Fokker--Planck equations for the harvesters with a reaction-diffusion equation for the resource. The coupling is nonlocal in space and time. For standard second-order mean field game systems, exponential turnpike estimates are known under assumptions such as monotonicity of the coupling. For the present system, Kobeissi, Mazari-Fouquer, and Ruiz-Balet proved algebraic convergence to a stationary solution in a space--time averaged sense, but no exponential turnpike estimate has been obtained. We prove such an estimate near a stationary solution with strictly positive density components. Inspired by the relative entropy method, we add the relative entropy of the resource density to the standard energy for local turnpike estimates. In the time derivative of this modified energy, the nonlocal coupling terms cancel. The two key assumptions are coercivity of a quadratic form determined by the stationary resource density and smallness of the relative density perturbations in $L^\infty$. Under these assumptions, we bound the absolute value of the modified energy by two terms that decay exponentially away from the initial and terminal times. We derive weighted $L^2$ exponential turnpike estimates for the harvester density, the resource density, and the gradient of the value function. We give sufficient conditions for coercivity. For each fixed $T>0$, classical solutions satisfying these assumptions exist for initial and terminal data sufficiently close to the stationary solution. We extend the modified energy estimate to a more general reaction term under the corresponding assumptions.

title: Solid factors associated to the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ on $\mathbb{Z}^n$
abstract: Let $n\geq 2$ be an integer. Set $Γ_n=SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ (respectively $PSL_2(\mathbb{Z})$) for $n$ even (respectively for $n$ odd). Then $Γ_n$ acts on $\mathbb{Z}^n$ through the restriction of the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that that the von Neumann algebra $L(\mathbb{Z}^n\rtimes Γ_n)$ is a solid factor. This generalizes the case $n=2$ proved by N. Ozawa.

title: Optimal orders for Hilbert-valued Littlewood--Paley functions of symmetric semigroups
Port-Hamiltonian Systems Beyond Joules: A Review of Unexpected Application Domains
abstract: The port-Hamiltonian framework was built for mechanical and electrical systems, where the Hamiltonian is stored energy and the ports carry power. Over the past fifteen years it has spread to chemistry, cell biology, fusion plasmas, musical instruments, district heating, electricity markets, macroeconomics, predator-prey ecology, optimization algorithms and neural-network training. This review maps that spread. We classify each application by what its Hamiltonian really is: physical energy, a thermodynamic potential such as free energy or exergy, or an abstract storage function with no energetic meaning. The review keeps only sources whose bibliographic record we checked against Crossref. The picture that emerges is a continuum. Where a genuine thermodynamic potential exists, the theory is deep and constructive. Where the energy is borrowed, the framework still pays off through compositional interconnection and dissipation inequalities, but the work is younger and scattered. We close with a set of deliberately speculative research directions, including open port-Hamiltonian models of epidemics, opinion dynamics and supply chains, and learned port-Hamiltonian digital twins for structural health monitoring.

title: Trivial solutions in Generalized Fermat equations
abstract: The modular method is a powerful tool to study generalized Fermat equations. Trivial solutions often become an obstruction to the method. While using hypergeometric motives to construct Galois representations, some of these solutions give rise to newforms with complex multiplication. In the present article, assuming a standard conjecture in Darmon's program, we prove that asymptotically any newform with complex multiplication cannot be related to a non-trivial primitive solution. This allows to discard all such newforms, including those associated to trivial solutions.

title: Automorphism of reduced finitary power monoids
abstract: Let $H$ be a multiplicatively written monoid with identity element $1_H$. The family $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)$ of all finite subsets of $H$ containing $1_H$ is a monoid with identity $\{1_H\}$ under the setwise multiplication induced by $H$. We prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)) \cong \operatorname{Aut}(H)$ whenever $H$ satisfies either of the following two conditions: (1) $H$ is commutative, cancellative, and contains an invertible element of infinite order; (2) $H$ is an abelian group which is not isomorphic to the Klein four-group.

title: On the domain of attraction of source--type solutions of the porous medium equations
abstract: We study the rate of convergence to Barenblatt profiles of the solutions to porous medium equations in $\R^n, n \ge 1$, by means of a certain class of Energy distances, a class of discrepancies between probability measures which have been recently widely used in problems related to AI, in particular for tasks related to machine learning. If $n \ge 3$, it is shown both that the rate of decay in Energy distance is improved with respect to known results which are based on the decay of relative entropy, and that, with respect to this distance, any initial value of bounded mass belongs to the domain of attraction of the source--type solution. Similar results are shown to hold for the fast diffusion case.

title: Formal Proof of an Anisotropic Calderón Uniqueness Theorem
abstract: We announce a Lean~4 formal proof of a special case of the smooth anisotropic Calderón uniqueness theorem released by OpenAI on October 6, 2026. We consider smooth Riemannian metrics on the three-dimensional unit ball, with full boundary measurements and Euclidean extensions outside the ball. OpenAI's release did not include a Lean proof of their uniqueness result. Our formalization uses results from Mathlib and Tau Ceti, and it is given as a solution to a Lean comparator challenge whose check permits only the standard axioms of Lean. The Lean proof is not a line-by-line translation of the OpenAI manuscript.

title: Holomorphic Isometric Embeddings of the Unit Disk into the Symmetrized Bidisk
abstract: We give a complete characterization of the holomorphic isometric embeddings $F:(\mathbb{D},k\,ds^2)\rightarrow (\mathbb{G}_2,ds^2)$ of the unit disk into the symmetrized bidisk with respect to the Bergman metric up to a scalar constant. We show that the isometric constant $k$ can take only the values $k=1$ and $k=3$. For $k=3$, we prove that $(2z,z^2)$ is the unique isometry up to a reparametrization. For $k=1$, we construct an isometric embedding which intersects the royal variety at a single point and does not admit a holomorphic lift to the bidisk via the symmetrization map. We further show that this isometric embedding is unique up to reparametrizations. Finally, none of the isometries are totally geodesic.

title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
abstract: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.

title: Removing the floor from Hoeffding and Bernstein inequalities for finite-population U-statistics
abstract: Let $C$ be a uniformly sampled $n$-element subset of a finite population $D$ of size $N$, and let $U_C$ be the complete U-statistic of order $k$ built from a bounded kernel on the $k$-subsets of $D$. We prove a product inequality for the uniform distribution on $\binom{D}{n}$ and deduce from it the comparison $ \log \mathbb{E}\left[e^{θ(U_C-\mathbb{E}U_C)}\right] \le \frac{n}{k}\log \mathbb{E}\left[e^{\frac{kθ}{n}(Y-\mathbb{E}Y)}\right]$, where $Y$ is a single kernel value taken at a uniformly sampled $k$-subset of $D$. This yields Hoeffding, Bennett and Bernstein inequalities for $U_C$ with effective sample size $n/k$ in place of the $\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ available so far. The gain is negligible when $n$ is much larger than $k$, but it approaches a factor of two in the exponent when $k$ is close to $n$.

title: Positive sectional curvature on all smooth 13-spheres
abstract: Every smooth homotopy $13$-sphere admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive sectional curvature. We construct a special $S^3$--$S^3$ bundle over $S^{13}$ whose star quotient represents the nonzero class $\pmα_1β_1\inΘ_{13}\cong\mathbb Z/3$. The defining equivariant map factors through the Blakers--Massey map by a smooth Hopf construction representing an unstable $J$-generator. This factorisation retains the prescribed base representation and makes Schultz's plumbing composition formula applicable; a normal-invariant computation in smoothing theory then identifies the smooth structure. On the quotient we implement the compatible-disk strategy with complete curvature estimates on arbitrary two-planes, matching boundary metrics, and a strictly positive sum of outward second fundamental forms. A direct smoothing argument completes the metric construction. Orientation reversal gives the remaining nonzero class in $Θ_{13}$.

title: An exact Kähler form on $(\mathbb C^*)^2$ without a global SYZ fibration
abstract: We construct an explicit exact Kähler form on \((\mathbb C^*)^2\) admitting no almost-toric fibration and hence no smooth Lagrangian torus fibration. For the logarithmic holomorphic volume form, we also rule out any special Lagrangian fibrations with compact fibers and dense regular locus, even when arbitrary compact connected singular fibers are allowed. For higher dimensions, taking products also yields explicit exact Kähler forms on \((\mathbb C^*)^n\), for every \(n\ge2\), admitting no smooth proper Lagrangian torus fibration.

title: Spectral distribution for biased orientations of random graphs
abstract: We study the Hermitian adjacency matrix of the second kind for biased orientations of Erdos-Renyi random graphs. In the model $D(n,p,p')$, an edge is present with probability $p$ and, conditional on its presence, is directed from its smaller to its larger endpoint with probability $p'$. Both parameters may depend on $n$, and biased tournaments are the special case $D(n,1,p')$. We prove a global semicircle law whenever $n(p(1-p)+3p^2p'(1-p')) \to \infty$, for both the centered and the uncentered matrix, and also for the expected empirical spectral measure. Our second theorem gives the exact spectrum of the mean matrix and the limits of the extreme eigenvalues on the scale $np$, under a sufficient density assumption. The main difference from the unbiased random orientations (where $p'=1/2$) is emergence of multiple large eigenvalues. The proofs include the closed-walk counting, control of the moment variances, an explicit diagonalization of the deterministic bias, and the passage from centered to uncentered spectral measures.

title: An explicit basis for the unipotent Specht modules of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$
abstract: For each partition $λ$ of $n$ we construct an explicit basis of the unipotent Specht module $S^λ$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, defined recursively over horizontal strips. Each basis vector is $g\,x_τ$, where $τ$ is a semistandard tableau of shape $λ$, $x_τ$ is obtained from a Steinberg-type vector by alternately applying a permutation matrix and a Fourier sum over a unitriangular group, and $g$ runs over an explicit set of coset representatives. Grouping the basis by the standardization of $τ$ gives exactly $q^{\mathrm{maj}(s^T)}$ vectors for each standard tableau $s$, which is the numerical form of the Dipper-James standard basis problem. The same family is a basis over every field containing a nontrivial $p$th root of unity, including fields whose characteristic divides $|\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)|$, and a subfamily chosen layer by layer gives a basis of the simple quotient $D^λ$. We also give a basis of the $U$-fixed vectors of $S^λ$ and computed values of $\dim D^λ$ for $\mathrm{GL}_n(2)$.

title: Abelian categories and double décalage
abstract: We show that an additive category is abelian if and only if its functorial nerve is a double décalage of a pseudo-simplicial object in Cat. In this characterization, the canonical isomorphism between the image and coimage is encoded by a coherent pseudo-simplicial identity.

title: On maximum volume polytopes inscribed in the sphere
abstract: We combine degree sequence bounds with a supporting tangent plane method to study maximum volume polytopes inscribed in the sphere $\mathbb S^2$. Building on the vertex-star estimates and combinatorial reductions in Wimmer's dissertation, we determine the exact maximum for ten vertices and the unique maximizing combinatorial type for eleven vertices. Moreover, using explicit computational certificates we identify a unique possible maximizing type for polytopes with thirteen and fifteen vertices, and two possible types for sixteen vertices; this approach also recovers Wimmer's fourteen-vertex combinatorial theorem. Finally, we derive a facial inequality which holds for every degree pattern, and prove that the maximum volume for polytopes with thirty-two vertices is $\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{10(5-\sqrt{5})}$, attained precisely by an inscribed realization of the pentakis dodecahedron, which is the convex hull of the regular icosahedron together with its normalized facet centers. Wimmer had already determined this configuration and its optimality within its own combinatorial type. We also obtain a global degree sequence envelope and a universal affine volume bound.

title: A Bayesian oriented exploration and reinforcement learning in continuous-time mean-variance portfolio optimization
abstract: We propose a new reinforcement learning (RL) framework for the continuous-time mean-variance portfolio optimization with unknown market parameters. To better reflect the impact of improved information of the unknown drift on the degree of exploration, we consider a novel randomization based on continuous-time stochastic filtering. Specifically, we construct a continuous-time analog to Thompson Sampling by treating the unknown drift as a random draw from a generalized sampling distribution parameterized by the filter's posterior mean and variance. The new learning objective measures the tradeoff between the wealth performance and the weighted KL divergence between the policy and the true Bayesian posterior, which transforms the classical feedback control into an information guided stochastic policy. As a result, the degree of exploration endogenously depends on the Reward-Biased Maximum Likelihood Estimation that decays with the shrinking filter's variance. This allows us to devise an efficient model-based learning algorithm in the mean-variance portfolio optimization with theoretical guarantee and superior learning performance.

title: Nonlinear stability and time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system in $\mathbb{R}^3$
abstract: We prove the global-in-time nonlinear stability and establish explicit algebraic time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system of an ideal polytropic gas in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Given a smooth initial rarefaction profile of small wave strength \(δ>0\), we first construct the corresponding global one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier solution \(U_b(t,x_1)\) and show that it converges toward the self-similar Euler rarefaction fan in \(L^\infty(\mathbb{R})\) at rate \((1+t)^{-12/25}\). For the three-dimensional Cauchy problem under small weighted $H^3(\mathbb{R}^3)$ perturbations with zero integral of mass, momentum, and total energy, we prove that there exists a unique global strong solution $U(t,x)$ converging toward $U_b(t,x_1)$ in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$, with $\nabla(U-U_b)$ decaying in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$.

title: A Prey-Predator Framework for Tumor-Immune Dynamics: Circuit-Based Modeling with Hilfer-Katugampola Fractional Derivatives
abstract: This study focuses on modeling tumor--immune interactions through a fractional-order prey--predator framework, where tumor cells act as prey and immune effector cells as predators. To capture the hereditary and memory effects inherent in biological systems, we employ the Hilfer--Katugampola fractional derivative, which flexibly interpolates between Riemann--Liouville and Caputo formulations. In addition, a circuit-based analogy is introduced to map tumor proliferation, immune regulation, and therapeutic interventions onto resistive, capacitive, and inductive elements, providing intuitive interpretation of the dynamics. Analytical investigations, including equilibrium analysis and stability criteria, are conducted across varying fractional orders. Numerical simulations reveal that lower fractional orders lead to delayed oscillations, prolonged tumor persistence, and increased sensitivity to treatment strategies compared with classical integer-order models. The integration of fractional calculus with circuit analogies offers novel insights into tumor--immune dynamics and supports the design of memory-aware therapeutic interventions.

title: Dominant permutations, positive mixed-variable formulas, and product-splitting equivalence for (double) Schubert polynomials
abstract:
We present new positive combinatorial formulas for triple Schubert coefficients in mixed-variable products of double Schubert polynomials, $\mathfrak{S}_u(x;y)\mathfrak{S}_v(x;z)$, expressed in the $\mathfrak{S}_w(x;y)$ basis, in the case where $u$ is dominant. This result complements earlier results where $v$ was assumed dominant. To generalize further, we introduce a relation on permutations that we call ``domination,'' under which dominant permutations dominate all others. When $u$ dominates $w$, we obtain an explicit positive formula for $c^w_{u,v}(y;z)$, which in particular yields positivity when $u$ and $v$ have separated descents.
  In addition to these new positivity results, we establish a product--splitting equivalence for double Schubert polynomials, relating triple Schubert coefficients to splitting coefficients. This equivalence highlights structural symmetries and provides reduction methods for computing coefficients that are otherwise difficult to access. Taken together, these results extend the range of double Schubert polynomial products for which positivity can be established combinatorially and yield explicit formulas that can be implemented computationally.

title: Spectral gaps and mixing rates of primitive matrices
abstract: We obtain lower bounds on spectral gap/upper bounds for mixing rate for arbitrary $n$-state (not necessarily reversible) primitive Markov chains which have exponent $-O(n)$ rather than $-O(n^2)$, a significant improvement on the order obtained from classical arguments. Our improvements come from using the irreducibility distance and chainable index (which are at most linear in $n$) rather than the primitivity index (which can be near $n^2$). This also yields corresponding bounds for arbitrary nonnegative primitive matrices.

title: On the Bendixson criterion for attractors of dynamical systems in metric spaces
abstract: We revisit the Bendixson criterion for attractors, originally proposed by R.A. Smith for the finite-dimensional case and subsequently extended by M.Y. Li and J.S. Muldowney to Banach spaces. First, we give a concise proof of the criterion for general dynamical systems (semiflows, mappings, cocycles) in metric spaces using Čech cohomology. This approach allows for a significant weakening of previously known conditions while simultaneously resolving existing misunderstandings. Second, for compact invariant sets of semiflows that are topologically one-dimensional and possess zero first cohomology (e.g., attracting a superset with zero first cohomology), we prove that any chain recurrent point within the invariant set must be an equilibrium. In the proof, we construct a global strict Lyapunov function using Whitney-Bebutov sections. Third, we generalize and refine R.A. Smith's theorem concerning the finiteness of the set of fixed points for analytic mappings, as well as M.L. Cartwright's theorems on to almost periodic flows.

title: Admissible geometries for Talenti's Pólya--Szegő principle
abstract: Talenti symmetrization rearranges functions on an open connected set $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, endowed with a measure $μ$ with continuous positive density, along the superlevel sets of a given function $f$. Talenti proved a Pólya--Szegő principle for it, provided that these sets are $μ$-isoperimetric, have connected boundaries, and are crossed by straight lines of steepest ascent. We show that, if $X$ is convex, these requirements are very rigid: they force the superlevel sets of $f$ to be either parallel half-spaces, or concentric balls, or complements of tubes around an affine subspace of codimension at least two. This identifies the only geometries in which Talenti's Pólya--Szegő principle can be applied. We also prove a family of weighted isoperimetric inequalities in convex cones, showing that complements of tubes around affine subspaces of every codimension at least two do occur.

title: Neural Operator Surrogates for Landweber Iteration in Solving Inverse Problems
abstract: Neural operators can accurately approximate well-posed mappings, but for unbounded or discontinuous operators, common in inverse problems, we verify that their network parameters often blow up in architectures such as DeepONet and FNO. To solve inverse problems stably, we use Landweber iteration, which requires only a forward map and the adjoint of its derivative (linearisation). To reduce repeated PDE forward evaluations, we replace the forward operator and its derivative with a differentiable neural-operator surrogate. We show that encoder-network-decoder operators, including generalised DeepONets and fully coupled Fourier operators, approximate both the forward map and its derivative. A modified discrepancy principle ensures decreasing error before finite stopping. With a compact preconditioner, the iterates remain in a compact set where accurate surrogates exist, and the stopped reconstructions converge as data and surrogate errors vanish under a regularity condition. We also relate the theory to derivative-informed training along finite directions, showing that the preconditioner determines which derivative errors affect the Landweber iteration update. Experiments on identifying a reaction coefficient in an elliptic equation show that smoothing reduces late-iteration deterioration for less accurate surrogates but slows sharp-feature recovery, and that smaller derivative errors along training directions do not by themselves improve reconstruction accuracy.

title: Mean Field Limit Towards Kinetic Equation with Repulsive Dirac-Delta Potential
abstract: A one-particle effective kinetic equation with repulsive Dirac-Delta potential in one dimension is rigorously derived from a moderate interacting second order particle system. It is proved that the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure and the solution of Vlasov equation converges to zero. A convergence rate is obtained by a combination of the estimates for particle trajectory and a smoothed version of modulated energy.

title: Iteration-Clock Selection for Euler Schemes of Degenerate Diffusions
abstract: We study Euler--Maruyama approximation of the driftless one-dimensional SDE $dX_t=σ(X_t)\,dW_t$ when $σ$ vanishes at the origin and weak uniqueness fails because solutions may remain at zero for an arbitrary time. The central object is the logarithmic coefficient profile $q(Q)=-\logσ(e^{-Q})$. Under a two-sided logarithmic increment condition, with both indices in $(0,1/2)$, we show that weak-solution selection is governed by a deterministic iteration clock: if $N_q(Q)$ is the number of iterates of $q$ needed to reach a fixed reference depth and $hN_q(\log(1/|x_h|))\to d$, then the Euler scheme started from $x_h$ converges to the fundamental zero-sojourn diffusion delayed by $d$. This single theorem yields the common-index generalized-power law $d=θ/|\logα|$ when $h\log\log(1/|x_h|)\toθ$, an effective translation-number formula for periodically modulated logarithmic profiles, a two-index delay window, and a sharpness construction in which, for one coefficient and one initialization family, the cluster set is the entire delay window. Thus the macroscopic selection mechanism is the iteration count of the logarithmic coefficient profile; the explicit double-logarithmic law of the homogeneous power case is its common-index closed form.

title: Remarks on spectral gaps on Gaussian path space
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the relationship between spectral gaps of Ornstein--Uhlenbeck/$L^2$ operators on Gaussian path space and the underlying Volterra kernel $F$. This framework includes fractional Brownian motion $B^H$ with Hurst index $H\in(0,1)$. For the fractional Wiener measure $μ_H$, the logarithmic Sobolev inequality with respect to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck Dirichlet form holds for $H\geq\frac12$, whereas the corresponding weak Poincaré inequality fails for $0<H<\frac12$. The damped/$L^2$ Dirichlet forms satisfy logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for every $H\in(0,1)$.

title: Analytic criteria for criticality of subordinated Schrödinger operators
abstract: For a subordinated Schrödinger operator, we introduce a quantity that plays a role analogous to the bottom of the spectrum of a Schrödinger operator, and establish analytic criteria for subcriticality, criticality and supercriticality of a subordinated Schrödinger operator.

title: On the error term in Gauss's mean value formulas for class numbers
abstract: Combining the frameworks of Chamizo--Iwaniec and Chamizo--Ubis with the recent character-sum and exponential-sum estimates of Bellotti and Kerr, we improve the error term in Gauss's mean value formulas for class numbers of binary quadratic forms from $O(N^{21/32+\eps})$ to $O(N^{55/84+\eps})$. If no Dirichlet $L$-function vanishes in $\mathrm{Re}\,s>7/8$, the exponent becomes $2274811/3487744$; under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions, it becomes $118/181$.

title: Learning-Assisted Beamforming Optimization for Hybrid XL-RIS-Aided Communication
abstract: Hybrid active-passive extremely large-scale reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS) architectures mitigate the double-hop path loss of passive RIS while enabling near-field spatial energy focusing, but impose a computationally intensive mixed discrete-continuous beamforming design problem under strict radio-frequency (RF) power constraints. This paper investigates a hybrid XL-RIS-assisted downlink multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) system in the near-field regime. The joint optimization of the base station (BS) precoder, discrete XL-RIS phase shifts, and active-element amplification gains is addressed via a discrete coordinate ascent (DCA)-based alternating optimization (AO) framework, in which discrete variables are updated through local index-domain searches and the BS precoder is derived in closed form via a noise-aware minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criterion. To reduce the per-sample computational cost for XL-RIS apertures, a deep unfolding (DU) framework is proposed as a low-complexity alternative, unrolling a fixed number of Riemannian gradient ascent steps on the sum-rate objective and recovering the discrete phase configuration via quantized phasor projection, with one learnable step size per layer trained in a self-supervised manner. Numerical results under near-field spherical-wave channel models confirm that the DU framework achieves sum-rate performance close to the AO scheme with substantially lower and nearly constant runtime, and that both schemes consistently outperform manifold optimization under discrete hardware constraints.

title: On Relative Greedy Weights
abstract: Relative greedy weights were introduced by Li and Liu in [19] as a measure of information leakage in coordinated two-party wire-tap channels of type II when the adversary follows a greedy strategy. Their definition can be viewed as a relative version of the CEZ greedy weights, which are only locally greedy. In this paper, we revisit the concept of greediness and relative greediness introducing new measures, and we discuss other perhaps more relevant applications of relative greedy weights than the coordinated two-party wire-tap channel of type II. We pay special attention to bottom-up greedy weights, which correspond to an adversary with an ultimate greedy approach, and we present families of nested codes for which such weights are larger than the relative CEZ greedy weights.

title: The cofinite regularity spectrum of $F$-irregular graphs
abstract: For a connected graph $F$, a graph $G$ is $F$-irregular if the numbers of copies of $F$ containing its vertices are pairwise distinct. We characterize which connected patterns admit regular $F$-irregular hosts of every sufficiently large degree. Stars admit no regular $F$-irregular host; for every other $F$, every sufficiently large integer $r$ is realized by a connected $r$-regular $F$-irregular graph of diameter two and order $r+o(r)$, optimal to first order. For triangles, and equivalently four-vertex paths in regular graphs, we construct such hosts of order less than $r+73r^{\log29/\log58}$ above an explicit threshold, with the constant reduced to $44$ for even $r$. Lexicographic words encode distinct rooted subgraph counts, while layered connections allow the common degree to be prescribed. Rooted-homomorphism expansions and spectral amplification establish separation for general patterns; an exact uniform-increment identity gives the quantitative triangle construction. The finite seed graphs are explicitly constructed, and their required rooted-count distinctions are verified by exact-arithmetic certificates.

title: On naturality of cohomological support for small quantum groups
abstract: We apply the theory of hypersurface support by Negron and Pevtsova to prove the naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum Borel groups, with respect to restriction to Levi subalgebras. This in turn implies naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum groups for modules that lift to Lusztig's big quantum group, for instance tilting modules. This allows us to make the recent conditional classification of tensor ideals of abelian type in the category of such tilting modules unconditional.

title: Diophantine definitions of nonsplitting for central simple algebras over global fields
abstract: For every global field and every fixed degree, we prove that the structure constants defining nonsplit central simple algebras form a diophantine set. We formulate a local witness principle separating reliable localization, exact localization, and local detection. Adapted Kummer and Artin--Schreier presentations provide a common construction of witnesses through a uniform radical formula and ramification matching. This gives an independent proof of the non-characteristic case, which also follows from Morrison's nonnorm theorem, and treats the characteristic-degree case by the same method. We recover prime-degree nonnorm definability and give applications to rootless polynomials, anisotropic quadratic forms in all characteristics, and generalized Severi--Brauer varieties.

title: Sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints for composite hypotheses
abstract: We consider the problem of sequential anomaly identification with sampling constraints, where multiple independent data sources are observed over time, but only a limited subset can be sampled at each instant. The objective is to identify the anomalous sources while controlling the probabilities of at least one false alarm and at least one missed detection below prescribed levels. An identification policy must jointly determine when to stop sampling, which sources to declare anomalous, and how to allocate observations across sources under the sampling constraints. We seek policies that minimize the expected time to decision to a first-order asymptotic approximation as the error probabilities vanish. The observations from each source follow an unknown density belonging to one of two disjoint sets, corresponding to regular and anomalous behavior. Focusing on a nonparametric framework, which allows greater flexibility in modeling regular and anomalous statistical behavior, we establish general conditions for asymptotic optimality and provide a unified characterization of asymptotically optimal policies for composite hypothesis testing under sampling constraints. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed policies, and the robustness of the nonparametric framework.

title: Vertex splitting, global rigidity and nondegenerate equilibrium stresses
abstract: We prove Whiteley's conjecture that every nontrivial vertex split of a generically globally rigid graph preserves generic global rigidity in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), for all \(d\geq1\). We give two proofs of the stronger assertion that the split graph is infinitesimally rigid at every generic coincident realisation of the two split vertices. Both proofs use maximum-rank equilibrium stress matrices and then apply the coincident-rigidity criterion of Cruickshank, Jackson and Tanigawa. The second construction also shows that every generically globally rigid graph admits a nondegenerate equilibrium stress of maximum rank at every generic realisation, establishing a conjecture of Jordán and Tanigawa.

title: The moduli stack of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type
abstract:
The goal of this article is the classification of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type over a compact complex manifold $X$. More precisely, let $E$ be a fixed holomorphic vector bundle over $X$ and $\mathcal{E}$ the associated locally free sheaf. We will assume that there exists an effective divisor $D$ on $X$ such that $H^1(X,\mathcal{E}(D))=0$. This condition is always satisfied when $X$ is a projective complex manifold.
  We define in a natural way the moduli stack of affine bundles on $X$ whose linearisation is isomorphic to $E$, and we prove that this moduli stack is isomorphic to the quotient stack $\big[H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)/H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D))\ltimes \mathrm{Aut}(E)\big]$ of the complex vector space $H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)$ by the semi-direct product of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(E)$ (which is always an affine algebraic group) by the complex vector space $H^0(X,{\cal E}(D))$. Our isomorphism is obtained by constructing explicitly comparison functors $\mathscr{A}$, $\mathscr{T}$ between the two stacks and explicit natural isomorphisms $\mathscr{A}\circ\mathscr{T}\stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{id}$, $\mathrm{id} \stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{T}\circ\mathscr{A}$.

title: Superlinear problems related to Fully Non Linear singular or degenerate operators in punctured balls
abstract:
We study Fully Nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations with a higher differential term degenerate or singular, coupled with a zero order term singular at the point $0$, and an absorbing super-linear term of $p$ power type. 
We will limitate to punctured balls and positive radial solutions. In the continuity of two previous works in \cite {BDL1}, \cite{BDL2}, we will provide a complete classification depending on $p$ of the asymptotic behaviour of the solutions near the singular point $0$.

title: A Low-Rank Augmented Lagrangian Frank-Wolfe-Based Method for SDPs with Unbounded Feasible Regions
abstract: In contrast to HALLaR (Monteiro et al. 2026), which is designed for solving problems with a trace-bounding constraint, this work develops a new augmented Lagrangian (AL) method, HALLaR+, for solving large-scale semidefinite programming problems without such constraint. Even though a trace constraint which preserves an optimal solution can always be added, choosing its bound is challenging: a value that is too small may exclude all optimal solutions, whereas one that is too large may substantially increase the computational effort. HALLaR+ is also a low-rank inexact AL method but, in contrast to HALLaR, it doubles the penalty parameter at every AL iteration and its AL subproblems have unbounded feasible regions that are approximately solved by a relaxed unbounded Frank--Wolfe (RUFW) variant. Its analysis relies on a uniform bound on the diameters of the sublevel sets of all generated AL subproblems instead of a bounded feasible set. Assuming that a primal--dual KKT pair exists and the primal optimal set is nonempty and bounded, it is shown that HALLaR+ returns a $\varepsilon$-primal-dual feasible solution in $\tilde {\mathcal O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ total RUFW iterations. Numerical results suggest that HALLaR+ has very promising competitive performance against current state-of-the-art solvers.

title: Holomorphic interpolation and the Levi problem
abstract: On a nonsingular locally Stein Riemann domain over a Stein space, we prove that holomorphic forms of top degree interpolate jets of any fixed order on every closed discrete set finite over the base. For unramified domains, this yields jet interpolation by holomorphic functions, answering a question of Colţoiu and Joiţa for nonsingular sources. More generally, we establish a twisted interpolation theorem over weakly pseudoconvex spaces admitting injective holomorphic immersions into projective space. We also give negative answers to the Levi problem over singular Stein spaces: the Coeuré-Loeb space yields a non-Stein locally Stein unramified Riemann domain over a normal Stein threefold, and a related construction gives a relatively compact, non-Stein locally Stein open subset of a normal Stein fourfold. Finally, the punctured anticanonical bundle of Fornaess' ramified surface is a holomorphically separable increasing union of Stein manifolds that is not Stein, answering a question of Vigna Suria.

title: Schauder exponential basis which is not Riesz
abstract: We show that there exists a Schauder basis $\{e^{i λ_n t}\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with real frequencies in $L^2(-π,π)$ which is not a Riesz basis.

title: Integral Compensation for Discrete-time Bearing-only Target Localization and Circumnavigation
abstract: This paper investigates the discrete-time control problem of driving an agent to localize and circumnavigate an unknown target at a prescribed radius using bearing measurements. Discretizing existing continuous-time circumnavigation controllers can introduce steady-state orbit bias, even at sampling rates that preserve stability. To eliminate the sampling-induced orbit bias, we propose an adaptive compensator for a circumnavigation controller formulated directly in discrete time. Driven by the estimated agent-to-target distance, the proposed compensator dynamically learns the geometric correction required to achieve the desired circumnavigation radius. Unlike existing static correction methods, neither the proposed controller nor the compensator update explicitly uses the sampling interval. Exponential convergence is rigorously established using Lyapunov-based analysis. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithms.

title: Rigid Lie Algebras from Semisimple Lie Algebras and Their Symplectic Modules
abstract:
We consider two extensions associated with a nonzero finite-dimensional symplectic module $V$ over a complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{s}$, and study their rigidity. The toral extension adjoins a derivation acting as the identity on $V$ and trivially on $\mathfrak{s}$; the Heisenberg extension uses the invariant symplectic form on $V$ to define a central bracket.
  For the toral extension, we compute the first and second adjoint cohomology groups in terms of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak{s}}(V)$, and obtain rigidity precisely when $V$ is irreducible. These results hold for arbitrary nonzero finite-dimensional modules. For the Heisenberg extension, we express the second adjoint cohomology as the kernel of a map combining the symplectic centralizer with an equivariant Jacobi map. A Killing-form argument shows that every multiplicity-free sum of irreducible symplectic modules gives an algebraically rigid Heisenberg extension. We also treat constructions with independent toral generators or Heisenberg centers. Repeated summands lead to explicit nonrigid examples, including a deformation to $\mathfrak{sl}_3$. The proofs use invariant cochains and recover several previously studied families.

title: Local regularity and p-harmonic approximation for weak inverse mean curvature flow
abstract: We prove local Lipschitz regularity for locally bounded $BV$ solutions of the calibration equations for inverse mean curvature flow. We also approximate every prescribed variational weak flow locally by Moser's logarithmic transforms of positive $p$-harmonic functions. On a fixed smooth domain, with the trace of a calibrated Lipschitz solution prescribed, both the uniform error and the absolute difference of total variations are $O((p-1)^{1/3})$ as $p\downarrow1$. In particular, the approximations converge strictly in $BV$.

title: From many-body Schrödinger dynamics to magnetic Vlasov equation
abstract: We analyse the combined mean-field and semiclassical limit from the time-dependent Schrödinger dynamics of $N$ spinless fermions in a non-constant magnetic field to the magnetic Vlasov equation with scaling $\hbar = N^{-1/3}$. With the velocity-shifted coherent states and the induced magnetic Husimi measure, we derive an exact BBGKY hierarchy with a remainder of order $\hbar^{1/2-}$. The main result is the weak $L^1$ convergence of the $k$-particle magnetic Husimi measures to the $k$-copies of the solution to the magnetic Vlasov equation. Furthermore, the convergence holds in the Wasserstein distance $\mathbb{W}_2$ when the second moment of initial Husimi measure correspondingly converges.

title: Stretched near-groups
abstract: We study stretched near-group fusion categories over $\mathbb{C}$ of type $G+k|G|$ for abelian groups $G$ and positive integers $k$, describing the structure of the double including fusion rules, modular data, and Frobenius--Schur indicators under a variety of assumptions. For cyclic $G$, when enough invertible objects exist in the double, we describe all associated de-equivariantizations which connect the existence of stretched near-group fusion categories to the existence of other stretched quadratic categories. All of our results apply to the case $k=1$. In particular, the known existence of $C_{m^2}+m^2$ near-group categories for all positive integers $m$ implies the existence of Haagerup--Izumi fusion categories for all cyclic groups. As a further application, we provide a general conductor bound severely restricting the existence of stretched near-group categories, and for infinitely many abelian groups $G$ of square order, among them $C_4\times C_2^{2j}$ with $j\geq2$, we show that a near-group fusion category $G+k|G|$ exists if and only if $k=0$.

title: Optimal Dividends and Voluntary Liquidation under Omega-Type Regulatory Termination
abstract: We study a joint optimal dividend and voluntary liquidation problem for a company whose surplus follows a spectrally negative Lévy process and is subject to Omega-type regulatory termination. Dividend payments are modeled as a singular control, while voluntary liquidation is an optimal stopping decision with a state-dependent liquidation payoff. When the surplus falls below a regulatory solvency threshold, an Omega clock accumulates the time spent in distress and may terminate the firm before voluntary liquidation occurs. Under dynamic programming and continuity assumptions for an auxiliary Markov subproblem, we characterize its value as the smallest controlled stochastic supersolution of the associated quasi-variational inequality. We prove that any regular stochastic solution with a dividend barrier coincides with the value function over all admissible dividend and liquidation policies, and hence is unique within this class. Using $ω$-scale functions, we construct single-band, singleton, and no-liquidation candidates, establish sufficient conditions for global optimality, and give conditions under which these candidates supply the unique regular barrier stochastic solution. Brownian and Cramér--Lundberg examples illustrate how regulatory parameters affect dividend and liquidation boundaries and generate transitions between policy regimes.

title: The $(t-1)$-chromatic Ramsey number of cycles for three colours
abstract: For integers $t\ge 2$ and $\ell\ge 3$, let $R^t_{t-1}(C_\ell)$ be the least integer $n$ such that every colouring of the edges of $K_n$ with $t$ colours contains a cycle of length $\ell$ whose edges use at most $t-1$ colours. Bucić and Khamseh determined the analogous number for paths and asked for its value for cycles. We answer this question for three colours: we show that $R^3_2(C_\ell)=\ell+\lfloor(\ell+1)/6\rfloor$ for every $\ell\ge 11$, and we determine the values for $3\le \ell\le 10$.

title: Fefferman-Stein Type Distribution Function Inequalities on Product Spaces
abstract:
We establish on $R^n\times R^m$ a Fefferman--Stein type distribution function inequality in which the nontangential maximal function of the product Poisson extension is controlled by the Lusin area integral function: \[
  |\{N>λ\}|\le C\left(|\{A>λ\}|+λ^{-2}\int_{\{A\leλ\}}A^2\,dx\right). \] The central idea is to establish a local $L^2$ estimate for the radial maximal function. This yields a new proof of the corresponding one-parameter inequality, avoiding Green's formula and the treatment of sawtooth regions, and extends to the multiparameter setting.

title: Exactly integrable field theory in $(2+1)$-dimensional space-time: the spectral equations
abstract: The primary object in quantum field theories is the one-step relativistic evolution operator. In this paper we consider the evolution operator defined on the auxiliary Kagomé lattice with the $q$-oscillator algebra of observables, the local ingredient of the evolution operator is the $q$-oscillator $R$-matrix of the Zamolodchikov tetrahedron equation. We construct explicitly the complete system of equations (which can be seen as a specific form of nested Bethe Ansatz equations) defining the spectrum of the evolution operator. This system of equations is valid for an arbitrary initial data (occupation numbers), and the thermodynamical limit is well defined for this system.

title: A second-order estimate linear in the gradient for complex Hessian equations
abstract: We use the maximum principle to prove a second-order estimate with linear dependence on the gradient for the nondegenerate complex Hessian equation on a compact Kähler manifold. The proof combines $C^0$ compactness and a refined concavity inequality with the use of nearby smooth admissible functions. A standard interpolation argument then yields the known uniform gradient and complex Hessian bounds.

title: Well-posedness and attractors for the sub-quintic weakly damped wave equation with low-regularity forcing on $\mathbb{R}^3$
abstract: We study the weakly damped semilinear wave equation on $\mathbb{R}^3$ with a sub-quintic nonlinearity $f(u)$ and a forcing term of low regularity, $g\in H^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^3)$. By absorbing the forcing term into a stationary solution $h$ and then expanding the solution around $h$, we reduce the problem to a wave equation with potentials. Relying on Strichartz estimates for this equation, obtained through the Besov spaces associated with the Schrödinger operator, we establish the global well-posedness of weak solutions by an iteration argument on the Besov scale. In particular, uniqueness holds unconditionally in the energy class for $3<p<5$. Combining a refined decomposition of the solution with uniform tail estimates for trajectories starting from bounded sets, we then prove that the associated solution semigroup is asymptotically compact and, consequently, possesses a compact global attractor in the energy space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)\times L^2(\mathbb{R}R^3)$.

title: A Quarter-Power Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
abstract: For every nonempty finite set $S$ of $N$ positive integers we prove $-\min_{x\in\mathbb{T}}\sum_{s\in S}\cos(2πsx)\gg (N/\log(2N))^{1/4}$. The proof uses a reversible phase kernel whose one-step and two-step laws are close in total variation. Comparison of rows and a height cutoff produce a partition into pieces of bounded mean. A Fourier rounding estimate then forces many additive triples to cross the partition. Two choices of phase density yield bounds in terms of negative mass and an exact conditional-pair defect, respectively. A logarithmic refinement gives a log-free bound at low triple density. At fixed positive triple density the log-free bound is a corollary of known boundary estimates. We give a separate spectral proof using an integer difference count and a theorem of Yip.

title: The Fourier kernel and invariant trace formula of $\rm{GL}(3)$
abstract: Trace formula is an important method to study the Langlands program. Arthur obtains the existence of stable trace formula for connected reductive group. In this paper, we will give the explicit invariant trace formula of GL(3). For general reductive groups, Arthur gave an inductive proof of the existence of the invariant trace formula and provided explicit examples for GL(2). For GL(3), we successively compute the invariant distributions, give all the Fourier kernels for the GL(2) cases, and finally obtain the concrete invariant trace formula.

title: QoS-Aware Energy-Efficient Sub-THz Near-Field Multiuser Hybrid MIMO Systems Employing Circular Arrays
abstract: Near-field communications have emerged as a promising technology for future sixth-generation (6G) networks. However, designing energy-efficient hybrid beamfocusing schemes for multiuser (MU) systems remains challenging due to the non-convex quality-of-service (QoS) constraints and hardware limitations of hybrid architectures. In this paper, we investigate a hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) architecture for a near-field sub-THz MU downlink system employing a large uniform circular array (UCA) at the base station. A QoS-aware transmit power minimization problem is formulated for energy-efficient beamfocusing and addressed through a two-stage penalty-driven joint optimization (PDJO) framework, where auxiliary variables are introduced to reformulate the QoS constraints into second-order cone (SOC) constraints. Furthermore, a near-field polar-domain codebook is developed via joint angle- and distance-domain sampling. We establish that the fully digital (FD) beamfocuser lies within the column space of the proposed codebook, enabling hybrid precoder design to be formulated as a multiple measurement vector (MMV)-based sparse approximation problem. The formulated problem is then solved using a low-complexity simultaneous orthogonal matching pursuit (SOMP) algorithm under hardware and transmit power constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves spectral- and energy-efficiency performance close to the ideal FD beamfocusing scheme while providing a favorable trade-off between hardware complexity and system performance.

title: A uniform lower bound for logarithmic Trudinger-Moser suprema in dimension $N\ge3$
abstract: Let $B$ be the unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\ge2$, and let $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)$ denote the critical Trudinger-Moser supremum of Calanchi and Ruf for radial functions in the Sobolev space with logarithmic weight $(-\log|x|)^{β(N-1)}$, $0\leβ<1$. We prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)>(2N-\frac25)|B|$ for every $β\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge 3$. This lower bound is uniform in $β$ and lies strictly above the upper bound $|B|\big(1+e^{1+\frac12+\cdots+\frac1{N-1}}\big)$ for the concentration level obtained by Carleson-Chang for $β=0$ and, for $β>0$, by Roy for $N=2$ and by Roy and Nguyen for $N\ge 3$. As a consequence, we prove that $\mathrm{MT}_N(α_{N,β},β)$ is attained for every $β\in[0,1)$ and $N\ge3$, which was previously known only for $β>0$ small enough. For $N=2$, the existence of extremals for every $β\in [0, 1)$ was recently obtained by de Oliveira.

title: Financial Connectedness: Heavy Tails andResponse Attribution
abstract: A financial market can appear mainly dependent on its own shocks under a variance account and mainly dependent on external shocks under a cumulative-response account. We establish how these opposite diagnoses arise from the same propagation system. For a given cumulative magnitude, squaring gives greater weight to responses concentrated across sources and time. Source priorities can therefore reverse even in stable Gaussian systems with known parameters. Heavy tails raise a separate question: whether the reported shares have a fixed population basis. One innovation with an infinite second moment removes the full network's finite covariance input. We characterize when normalized shares nevertheless stabilize and construct rank-amplitude connectedness, a cumulative-deviation target without finite first or second moments. It can be consistently estimated under local dependence and identification conditions. With fitted dynamics and rank scatter fixed, changing attribution replaces 3.14 names in the daily Top 10 of forty stocks, selecting recipients with greater external persistence relative to their own adjustment. In five futures contracts, mean external share rises from 28.0% to 55.9%, and 70.9% of recipient-dates switch from own to external dominance.

title: Extremal graphs for Alon's graph coupon-collector conjecture
abstract: Let \(G\) be a finite simple graph without isolated vertices. Starting with every vertex uncovered, at each step sample a vertex uniformly and independently and cover one of its uncovered neighbors, chosen uniformly, if any. Let \(\cc(G)\) denote the expected number of steps required to cover all vertices. Alon conjectured that disjoint unions of \(K_{d+1}\) maximize \(\cc(G)\) among \(d\)-regular graphs of a prescribed order whenever such unions exist. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture for every fixed \(d\ge2\) and give a complete characterization of the extremal graphs for \(d=2\) at every order \(n\ge3\). In particular, all but at most six vertices of any such extremal graph lie in four-cycle components.

title: Regularity and Asymptotic Radial Symmetry of Solutions to Mixed Local-Nonlocal Parabolic Equations
abstract:
We study the regularity and the long-time asymptotics of the solution to the following mixed local-nonlocal parabolic problem
  \[
  \left\{
  \begin{alignedat}{2}
  \partial_t u - Δu + (-Δ)^s u &= f \qquad &&\text{in }Ω\times(0, T),
  u&=0 \qquad &&\text{in }\bigl(\mathbb{R}^{n}\setminusΩ\bigr)\times[0, T),
  u(\,\cdot\,,0)&=u_{0} \qquad &&\text{in }Ω,
  \end{alignedat}
  \right.
  \]
  where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ is a bounded domain, $s\in(0,1)$ and $(-Δ)^s$ denotes the fractional Laplacian.
  We first develop the well-posedness theory for the problem on finite time intervals ($0<T<+\infty$).
  Existence and uniqueness of weak solutions are established in the natural energy space, followed by interior $H^{2,1}$-regularity and global $L^\infty$-bounds.
  Then, under the restriction $s\in(0,1/2)$ and $0<α\le 1-2s$, we prove that weak solutions become classical ones, obtaining $C^{2+α,1+α/2}$-regularity up to the boundary via the method of continuity and a perturbation argument.
  The accompanying a priori estimate guarantees that these classical solutions can be extended globally in time, thereby allowing us to consider the parabolic problem on the whole half-line ($T=+\infty$).
  Finally, for the special case $Ω=B_1(0)$ and $f=0$, we employ the moving-plane method together with the previously established boundary regularity to show that every positive classical solution is attracted, as $t\to +\infty$, by a steady state that is radially symmetric and strictly decreasing.

title: Fingerprints of feedback cycles in stationary diffusions
abstract: When does the stationary density of a $d$-dimensional diffusion process driven by standard Brownian motion uniquely determine its drift? In general, it does not: the $d$ drift components enter the stationary Fokker-Planck equation only through a single scalar divergence. We consider drifts whose component functions only depend on a subset of their input variables, and encode this dependence with a directed graph. We exclude 2-cycles, which admit rotations that leave the stationary density invariant, but otherwise allow arbitrary graphs, including those with feedback cycles. We show that if the stationary density is sufficiently $s$-concave, e.g., strictly log-concave, then the drift is uniquely determined among graph-structured drifts in a weighted Sobolev space. For drifts with linear self-regulation, a single locally strictly convex level set of the stationary density is sufficient to identify the drift in the region it encloses. Both results follow from Raychaudhuri equations. Excluding 2-cycles allows treating nontrivial rotational and symmetric terms simultaneously, extending the scope of the corresponding Bochner- and Reilly-type arguments. We illustrate the results by recovering the Hill-type regulation of a stochastic genetic repressilator from samples of its stationary distribution.

title: Finite torsion in Hodge--Witt cohomology groups
abstract: For a bounded coherent complex of graded modules over the Raynaud ring $R$, we compare three descriptions of finite torsion: Ekedahl's pieces $A_f^2$ and $A_{\SSpart}^1$ of the biduality filtration, the nilpotent and semisimple parts of the torsion of the Illusie--Raynaud cœur, and the corresponding parts of the finite torsion $t^1$ of Ekedahl's diagonal cohomology. We show that finite torsion in bidegree $(0,i+1)$ measures the failure of the $i$th flat Artin--Mazur formal group to be smooth; we deduce that all flat Artin--Mazur formal groups of a Mazur--Ogus variety are smooth. For a smooth projective surface, we identify the three possible dual pairs in terms of the $p$-primary torsion of the geometric Néron--Severi group and the local-local and local-étale parts of the finite Picard quotient.

title: Beating the Probabilistic Bound for Hashing and Improving Lower Bounds for Trifferent Codes
abstract: We improve the probabilistic lower bounds on the rates of hash codes and list-recoverable codes. For perfect $q$-hashing, we prove $R_q>B_q$ for every $q\geq 3$. Our main result concerns non-perfect hashing. For every $q\geq 4$, we prove $R_{q,3}>B_{q,3}+\frac{1}{250000}.$ In particular, the case $q=9$, combined with the Tetra code, strictly improves the Körner-Marton lower bound $R_3\geq \frac14\log(9/5)$ for trifferent codes. We also extend the method to $(p,2,3)$-list recovery. For every $q\geq 4$ and $0\leq p<\frac{q-2}{12(q-1)}$, we prove $R_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)>B_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)$. For every fixed $0\leq p<1/18$, the rate improvement is bounded below by a positive constant independent of $q\geq 4$. The same holds for every fixed $0\le p<1/12$ when $q$ is sufficiently large.

title: Rayleigh's conjecture in dimensions four and five
abstract: We prove Rayleigh's conjecture for the clamped plate in dimensions four and five. In fact, we obtain a sharp comparison with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue: on every open set of finite positive measure, the first plate eigenvalue is at least the square of the Dirichlet eigenvalue multiplied by the ratio attained on a ball. The proof uses a homogeneous transformation of a trial function and its gradient. Two divergence identities reduce the comparison to positivity of a quadratic form in the Hessian. We establish the required Bessel inequalities by rational estimates for entire profiles and their remainders. An exact defect identity accounts for regular nodal sets, so the argument allows trial functions of either sign and imposes no boundary regularity. The domains may be disconnected or unbounded. We characterize equality up to sets of zero Sobolev capacity. We also obtain quantitative stability with the optimal quadratic power of the Fraenkel asymmetry.

title: Approximation by subsequences of matrix transform means of Vilenkin--Fourier series
abstract: In this paper we study the rate of approximation by matrix transform means of a special subsequence of partial sums of Vilenkin--Fourier series in the spaces $L_p(G_m)$ $(1\le p<\infty)$ and $C(G_m)$.

title: Phase Transitions for Random Least Common Multiples with Memory
abstract: We study the least common multiple of a random subset of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ when the selection follows a correlated Bernoulli process with memory. The copying rule preserves the marginal retention probabilities and creates a genealogical forest. At fixed density, the logarithmic least common multiple exhibits a fluctuation phase transition at the memory parameter $a=1/2$. The boundary limits depend on how genealogical families are distributed among the divisibility classes carrying the leading arithmetic weight. Our proofs combine the von Mangoldt representation with a reduction to large primes. At fixed density, an exact expansion separates an innovation martingale from a memory term. An asymptotic projection onto the retained count identifies the contribution of memory. Marked point-process convergence and estimates for rare genealogical families give the boundary limits.

title: All-genus mirror symmetry for the type-$D$ minimal resolution Calabi-Yau threefold
abstract: Let $Y$ be the product of a minimal resolution of a binary dihedral surface singularity with an equivariant line, with volume-preserving scalar action. We identify its stable equivariant descendant Gromov--Witten theory and its free energies in genus at least two with the sign-sector topological recursion of the degenerate type-$D$ relativistic Toda spectral curve. The $R-$matrix calibration is determined at a partial large-radius limit, where the trivalent exceptional curve retains a nonzero Kähler parameter, while the remaining parameters vanish. The limiting theory on the mirror side is a sum of twisted point theories and the local $(-2,0)$ curve theory. Moreover, we identify the equivariant K-group supported on the surface zero section with an integral relative homology group of the mirror. Explicit cycles for the dual tautological bundles realize their Gamma central charges and all stable Gamma-framed descendants.

title: Onsager--Machlup Theory and Transition Pathways for Degenerate Stochastic Systems with Multiplicative Noise
abstract: Noise-induced transitions between metastable states are central to many nonlinear stochastic dynamical systems, and most probable transition pathways provide an effective means of revealing the underlying transition mechanisms. In this work, we develop an Onsager--Machlup framework for degenerate stochastic dynamical systems driven by multiplicative Gaussian noise. We first derive the Onsager--Machlup action functional for the additive-noise case using the Girsanov transformation, and then extend the result to multiplicative noise through a Lamperti-type transformation. The resulting functional provides a variational characterization of the most probable transition pathway, from which we derive the associated Hamilton--Pontryagin boundary value problem. We further recast the variational problem as an equivalent optimal control problem and propose a neural-network-based numerical method for computing the most probable transition pathways. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the theoretical framework and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed computational approach.

title: Support enumerators of two-row grids and comb posets
abstract: We enumerate lattice points of preorder polytopes by support size for two-row Ferrers posets and recursively defined comb posets. For two-row posets, the order-ideal inequalities give a reflected-walk model in the nonnegative quadrant. Its transfer operators have a rank-one commutator, from which we derive an identity with five independent parameters. A matching-parameter specialization factors into the enumerators of a Motzkin excursion and a Motzkin bridge and proves the conjectured product of type~A and type~B Narayana polynomials for a two-row grid with its maximum removed. The general identity also records the two row supports separately. For combs, maximum ideal excess leads to a scalar recursion and a cubic generating function with independent spine and tooth weights. This proves a compositional-inverse conjecture of Athanasiadis and Chapoton and gives explicit $γ$-coefficients by Lagrange inversion. We prove $γ$-positivity for all two-row Ferrers cell posets and for the combs. The truncated-grid enumerators have simple negative zeros.

title: Frequency shifts: non-soficity, absence of specification and intrinsic ergodicity
abstract: For $p_c\in(0,1)$, the frequency shift $Σ(p_c)\subset\{0,1\}^{\N}$, introduced by Becker and Baraviera, is the closure of the shift orbits of the set of sequences in which a symbol $1$ is followed by $1$ exactly when the density of ones up to that position does not exceed $p_c$. We show that $Σ(p_c)$ is never sofic and never has the (weak) specification property. For $p_c=\frac{k}{k+1}$, with $k\ge1$, we describe $Σ(p_c)$ completely: $Σ(\frac12)$ is the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^m\}_{m\ge1}$, while for $k\ge2$ the shift $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is not transitive, but every invariant probability measure is supported on the coded system generated by $\{0^m1^{km}\}_{m\ge1}$. For every $k \ge 1$, the topological entropy of $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is $\frac{\log2}{k+1}$, and, using the Climenhaga--Thompson criterion, we prove that $Σ(\frac{k}{k+1})$ is intrinsically ergodic.

title: Support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains
abstract: We study the spatial support of stochastic porous medium equations on bounded domains. Under a local nondegeneracy condition, additive noise gives full distributional support at every fixed positive time. For the Dirichlet problem with nonlocal multiplicative noise, we prove that the solution is either identically zero or has full support; excluding the zero state requires a separate non-hitting assumption. For a Neumann model, nonzero initial mass excludes the zero state and yields full support. The proofs combine Galerkin approximation with terminal Malliavin estimates. Numerical results illustrate the propagation mechanisms.

title: Finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices
abstract: Motivated by the problem of Gragg and Kung on characterizing finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices, we investigate how the consistency of the subgroup lattice $L(G)$ constrains the structure of the underlying finite group $G$. To this end, we first establish several equivalent characterizations of consistency for lattices of finite length in terms of operation-preserving subposets and forbidden sublattices. More interestingly, for complete atomistic lattices of finite length, we introduce the consistency exchange property (CEP) for the canonical closure operator and show that consistency is equivalent to CEP, and that CEP is strictly weaker than the Steinitz-Mac Lane exchange property. We then apply this framework to semidirect products $G=V\rtimes_α C_m$, where $V$ is an elementary abelian $p$-group, $m$ is square-free and $p\nmid m$. Writing $d=o(α)$ and letting $C_α=\langleα\rangle$, we prove that $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $d=1$, or $d$ is prime and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pC_α$-module. For prime $d$, this latter condition is equivalent both to the irreducibility of the minimal polynomial of $α$ over $\mathbb F_p$ and to $\mathbb F_p[α]$ being a field. More generally, we verify that if $G=V\rtimes_θH$ where $H$ acts faithfully on $V$ and $p\nmid |H|$, then $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $H$ is trivial, or $H$ is cyclic of prime order and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pH$-module. We thus obtain a complete solution to the problem of Gragg and Kung for this class of coprime semidirect products.

title: Triangle-overlap cores and density bounds for Tuza's conjecture
abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let $ν(G)$ be the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles and let $τ(G)$ be the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle. We prove $τ(G)\le2ν(G)$ when each edge belongs to at most four triangles, the edges belonging to four triangles form components with at most two edges, and the maximum average degree is at most $25/2$. No upper bound on maximum vertex degree is imposed. We also localize the density condition. Let $K$ be the Hifumi core, defined as the vertex set of the 4-core of the spanning subgraph formed by edges belonging to at least three triangles. It suffices to impose the density condition on $G[K]$, including all original edges between vertices of $K$. More generally, when the four-triangle edges have maximum degree at most two, reductions produce a subgraph $R\subseteq G[K]$ with $τ(G)-2ν(G)\leτ(R)-2ν(R)$. Consequently an empty core gives a density-free sufficient condition. For the first graph class, a quantitative surplus argument strengthens both the global and localized density conditions to the strict bound $25/2+2/56775$. The proof combines edge reductions, discharging, finite certificates and a weak König--Egerváry lemma for links of arbitrary order. The general conjecture and the removal of the density condition from the first graph class remain unresolved here.

title: Lower bound on the size of splitting systems
abstract: For even $t$ and an $n$-set $X$, an $(n,t)$-splitting system is a family ${\mathbb{B}} \subseteq 2^X$ with the property that for each subset $Y \in {X \choose t}$, there exists $B \in \mathbb{B}$ such that $|B \cap Y| = t/2$. The problem of interest is to determine the minimum size of such splitting systems. We show that any $(n,t)$-splitting system has size at least of order $t$, improving the previous lower bound of $\sqrt t$ while the best known upper bound is of order $t^{3/2}$.

title: A seven-element interval of power-semiring varieties
abstract: We determine the interval between the varieties generated by the nonempty and full power semirings of a semigroup satisfying \(xy\approx x^2\). It has two elements for a one-element semigroup, three for a nontrivial left-zero or null semigroup, and seven otherwise, without any finiteness assumption. In the seven-element case the interval is \([\Rvar,\Rvar^0]\), where \(\Rvar=\Mod_{\rm ai}\{xy\approx xz\}\) and \(\Rvar^0\) is its zero-adjunction variety. Every word absorption valid in \(\Rvar\) but not in \(\Rvar^0\) is equivalent over \(\Rvar^0\) to one of six relative identities. We give exact absorption criteria and finite bases for all seven varieties. Three have basis rank two and four have basis rank three; their two-generated free algebras have orders \(15\), \(24\), or \(35\). We also count the finite-rank free algebras of both endpoints.

title: Cylinder spectral curve and 1-cut Matrix model
abstract: For a random matrix, with eigenvalues in a one-body potential $V(x)$ and a 2-body interaction $R(x,x')$, it is known that the resolvent converges in the large $N$ limit to an analytic function in the complex plane minus cuts, called the spectral curve. In the 1-cut case, a two-sheeted neighborhood of the cut is a cylinder with two simple ramification points. We describe these spectral curve data by boundary integral operators and generalized cycles. Vice-versa, given a 2-branchpoints spectral curve in a cylinder, there exists a formal random matrix model that corresponds to it. The goal of this article is to show the method to recover a formal random matrix model, with its potential and 2-body interaction, from the geometry of the spectral curve.

title: The stochastic phase field crystal equation with conservative space-time white noise: well-posedness, regularity and existence of a density
abstract: We study the phase field crystal equation $\partial_tu=Δ[(1+Δ)^2u+u^3-\varepsilon u]+σ\partial_x\dot W$ on $[0,π]$ with the boundary conditions $\partial_xu=\partial_x^3u=\partial_x^5u=0$ at $x=0,π$, perturbed by a conservative space-time white noise. This sixth order equation is the standard model for crystal growth at atomic length scales and diffusive time scales, and the conservative noise is the form of thermal fluctuations used in the physics literature. We prove that for every initial condition in $H^1$ there exists a unique global mild solution, continuous in space and time, which preserves the mean and whose supremum has finite moments of all orders. We determine its Hölder regularity: away from $t=0$, it is Hölder continuous in time with any exponent smaller than $1/4$, and $C^1$ in space with a spatial derivative which is Hölder continuous with any exponent smaller than $1/2$. Finally, using Malliavin calculus and a localization argument, we prove that for $σ\neq0$ the law of $u(t,x)$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure for every $t>0$ and every $x$. A specific feature of the model is a second neutral mode of the linear operator, besides the constant mode, which requires a separate treatment in the a priori estimates.

title: The Herzog--Schönheim Conjecture for Solvable Groups
abstract: The Herzog--Schönheim conjecture states that if a group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, cosets of subgroups, then two of these subgroups have the same index. We prove the conjecture for all solvable groups, finite or infinite. Sun's bound on unions of cosets, applied in a quotient, is combined with divisibility restrictions on local indices relative to the subgroup generated by the $p$-elements, where $p$ is the largest prime divisor of the order of a minimal counterexample. These restrictions are obtained by counting fixed points in a primitive solvable quotient. This suffices except at the prime $7$, where the counting bound narrowly fails and an additional overlap argument is needed. The proof has been formalized in Lean~4 with mathlib.

title: The random matrix hard edge --- applications, exact PDFs and large $N$ expansions
abstract: A hard edge of a Hermitian random matrix occurs when the eigenvalue density is strictly zero on one side of the edge, and nonzero on the other. Another possibility is that the eigenvalues occur in $\pm$ pairs, which creates a hard edge at the origin for the positive eigenvalues. Both review material and new results are presented for random matrix ensembles exhibiting a hard edge.
