The review material has two focuses: one is on applications of the random matrix hard edge, while the other is on exact eigenvalue probability density functions. The new results relate to the large $N$ expansion of correlation functions and conditioned gap probability generating functions with hard edge scaling for the Jacobi ensemble. For all even $β$ we are able to show that these quantities admit expansions in inverse even powers of the variable $N_{\rm hJ}':= N - 1/2 + (a + b + 1)/β$. For the $β=2$ Jacobi unitary ensemble, we can relate the leading (next leading) correction to the limit law to a particular second order (fourth order) differential operator applied to the latter. The analogous second order differential operator is found for $β=1,4$, leading then to its conjectured form for all $β>0$.

title: Zero forcing is not unimodal
abstract: The zero forcing polynomial of a graph counts the number of distinct zero forcing sets of every possible size. In 2018, Boyer et al. asked whether the zero forcing polynomial is always unimodal, and provided some evidence that it is. We answer this question by constructing an infinite family of graphs whose zero forcing polynomials are not unimodal. Our construction also shows that the graph polynomials associated with connected forcing and total forcing are also not unimodal in general.

title: Harmonic functions and comparsion geometry for noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature
abstract: In this paper, we establish several sharp comparsion results for noncompact 3-manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature and with a compact, connected boundary under a boundary mean curvature condition. Then we apply these gradient estimates to establish a Cohn-Vossen type bound for the average of the scalar curvature. This generalizes the work of Colding-Minicozzi \cite{Cold4} and Oronzio \cite{Oro2}.

title: Monk and Pieri rules for forest polynomials
abstract: This article gives Pieri rules for forest polynomials and Monk rule for double forest polynomials. We construct binary relations $\lessdot_i$ and $\prec_i$ based on the local Tamari moves on indexed forests. These relations are explicit and constructive. For ordinary forest polynomials, the $h$- and $e$-Pieri rules are given by all chains of a fixed length along the cover relations, with certain restriction on the left or right endpoints. For double forest polynomials, our Monk rule shows every off-diagonal degree-one structure coefficient is always a single positive root, whose weight is also controlled by Tamari moves. Additionally, we introduce an insertion algorithm on positive injective words that yields a Monk rule for the corresponding slide polynomials. Regrouping this rule along Sylvester classes gives an independent Monk rule for ordinary forest polynomials.

title: Impropriety and resilience of the chromatic number
abstract: We show that, for $p$ bounded away from $1$ and $np\to\infty$, the chromatic number of the binomial random graph $G_{n,p}$ is resilient to removal of a subgraph $H$ with $o(n \log(np))$ edges. It follows that the same assertion holds with $H$ being a subgraph of maximum degree $o(\log(np))$; and both these results are best possible up to a constant factor. We also prove corresponding results for the random $r$-regular graph $G_{n,r}$, when $r\to\infty$ and $r/n$ is bounded away from $1$, where $H$ has $o(n\log r)$ edges or maximum degree $o(\log r)$. Our results rely on a natural connection between chromatic resilience to edge removal and improper graph colouring. This work provides counterpoint to the work of Sudakov and Vu (2008) and Alon and Sudakov (2010), which treated chromatic resilience for $G_{n,p}$ subject to the addition, rather than removal, of edges.

title: An elementary observation on the Robin problem for NLS
abstract: We present an infinite set of explicit solutions of the integrable focusing NLS equation on the half-line that are rapidly decaying and satisfy a homogeneous Robin condition but have very different behaviors on the wall $x=0$. We then argue that a similar phenomenon exists for a small non-homogeneous perturbation of the Robin problem. This renders a potential application of the unified transform method to non-linearizable Robin problems impossible.

title: On Proximity Subgroups of Groups
abstract: By a $\textit{proximity subgroup}$ of a group $G$ we mean a norm $ν$ on $G$ valued in a complete lattice $L$ equipped with a binary sum (an additive counterpart of a multiplicative structure). The idea is that the smaller the value $ν(y)$ is, the closer $y\in G$ is to the subgroup of $G$ defined by the equation $ν(x)=\bot$, where $\bot$ is the bottom element of $L$. We test whether this notion is a suitable substitute for the usual notion of a subgroup (recovered by taking $L=\{\bot,\top\}$ with join as the sum), by showing that the form of proximity subgroups is noetherian. Intuitively, this means that proximity subgroups are as well suited for formulating and proving isomorphism theorems and homological diagram lemmas for groups as the usual subgroups are. We study several questions in relation to this, including what makes the noetherian form of usual subgroups special among all of these noetherian forms, and in fact, all noetherian forms of the category of groups.

title: A Multistage Extension of Witsenhausen's Counterexample with Linear Signaling
abstract: We study a multistage scalar extension of Witsenhausen's counterexample in which controller 1 observes the initial state exactly, whereas every subsequent controller observes only a local noise-corrupted state and does not inherit its predecessors' observations, so that every nonterminal action both regulates the state and shapes the signal available to the next controller. Restricting the signaling controllers to linear policies while leaving the terminal controller unrestricted, we compute the exact value within this class and reduce the optimization to a deterministic dynamic program in a single propagated variance. The optimal intermediate gains are shown to have a shrinkage form, and the value functions of that program are concave. For two stages, the benchmark admits a closed form on a matching locus, where for small effort weights it has two distinct minimizers, and at the standard parameter instance on that locus a two-point nonlinear policy strictly improves upon it. For three stages, numerical continuation at a reference instance reveals three distinct local minima, and two values of the initial variance at which the lowest of the three changes abruptly. Under the terminal-cost normalization we further prove, for every finite horizon, that the optimal linear value becomes asymptotically equal to the signaling-idle benchmark as the initial variance tends to infinity.

title: A unified approach to Manin triples of Lie algebras and the corresponding bialgebra structures
abstract: We introduce self-module Lie bialgebras as a common framework for bialgebra structures associated with different types of Manin triples of Lie algebras. A self-module Lie algebra is a Lie algebra with a specified representation on its underlying vector space; equivalently, it is an NS-Lie algebra expressed in different notation. We define a generic Manin triple as a finite-dimensional Lie algebra equipped with a nondegenerate bilinear form and two complementary isotropic Lie subalgebras, and establish the equivalence among standard generic Manin triples, suitable matched pairs of Lie algebras, families of matched pairs of self-module Lie algebras and self-module Lie bialgebras. The framework recovers Lie, pre-Lie and anti-pre-Lie bialgebras as special cases and admits examples outside these three families. We also introduce the self-module Lie Yang-Baxter equation and show that its solutions yield self-module Lie bialgebras and admit the $\mathcal{O}$-operator characterization. Finally, we obtain solutions in semi-direct product self-module Lie algebras, including constructions arising from self-bimodule pre-Lie algebras.

title: Proximal Myhill-type theorems for $m$-expansive amenable semigroup actions
abstract: The Garden of Eden theorem relates surjectivity to a weak injectivity condition for cellular automata on amenable groups. Li extended the Myhill implication to expansive actions of countable amenable groups with weak specification. We consider two simultaneous relaxations: the group is replaced by a cancellative amenable semigroup, and expansiveness by m-expansiveness. The loss of ordinary expansiveness removes homoclinic rigidity, so we introduce a proximal analogue of pre-injectivity. Our main result shows that, for a surjective action of an infinite countable cancellative left-amenable semigroup on a compact metric space, m-expansiveness plus weak specification forces every continuous equivariant map injective on each proximal set to be surjective. The proof uses entropy detection at a fixed scale, a strict entropy gap from weak specification, and finite multiplicity to produce proximal pairs from uniformly close points. We also give a one-dimensional variant under shadowing and examples clarifying the assumptions.

title: On Size-Biased Distributions and the Chainability of Positive Infinitely Divisible Distributions
abstract: Bar-Lev and Letac (2025) introduced the concept of chainability of infinitely divisible distributions on $\mathbb R$. In this note, we show that a simpler notion of chainability can be used for infinitely divisible distributions on $[0,\infty)$. We derive some properties and give a probabilistic interpretation in terms of so-called size-biased distributions. As an application, we discuss simulation from size-biased distributions associated with an important class of tempered stable distributions.

title: Mean-level arithmetic computation via stochastic reaction networks
abstract: Reaction networks provide a natural model for analog computation in which inputs and outputs are encoded by molecular abundances. Much of the work on analog computation with chemical reaction networks (CRNs) has focused on deterministic mass-action systems. In DNA- and protein-based circuits, however, low copy numbers can make intrinsic fluctuations significant, motivating the use of stochastic models. In this paper, we develop a framework for computation with stochastic CRNs at the level of stationary means. Specifically, we construct elementary arithmetic modules for identification, addition, and multiplication, and analyze their mean-level correctness and convergence rates. We focus on these three modules because they are simple enough to analyze explicitly while already exhibiting the new issues raised by stochastic mean-level computation. Unlike in deterministic systems, the computed value cannot be read from a single output measurement. Instead, readout requires Monte Carlo estimation, with error arising from transient bias as the system approaches stationarity and intrinsic sampling noise that persists even at stationarity. We therefore study the convergence rates of output means, variances, and autocovariances to their stationary values, as well as the stationary fluctuations governing sampling error. We also show that this readout cost can depend strongly, and sometimes unexpectedly, on the architecture of the computation. In particular, comparing linear-chain and binary-tree implementations reveals that binary trees can greatly reduce stationary variance for addition, but can instead produce exponentially larger variance for multiplication.

title: Relative Entropy Methods for Rotating Stars in the Compressible Euler-Riesz Equations
abstract: We establish finite-time relative entropy estimates for axisymmetric finite-energy entropy solutions of the three-dimensional attractive compressible Euler-Riesz equations near a prescribed compactly supported rotating star. The entropy solutions are assumed to have the same total mass as the steady state and to satisfy the prescribed angular momentum relation. For general pressure laws, the compatibility with the angular momentum constraint, together with the nonnegative rotational remainder, yields a cancellation of the centrifugal terms. For axisymmetric perturbations, the gradient of the perturbed Riesz potential has no azimuthal component and therefore couples only to those momentum components controlled by the modulated kinetic energy. The density-weighted estimates for the Riesz potential then allow us to close the relative entropy inequality. Under an additional higher-integrability assumption on the density, the result extends to the Chandrasekhar pressure law, yielding a corresponding stability estimate for rotating white dwarf stars.

title: Almost sharp global well-posedness and low-regularity blow-up for the two-dimensional periodic Zakharov system
abstract:
We study the Zakharov system on an arbitrary fixed rectangular two-dimensional torus with initial data in $H^s\times L^2\times H^{-1}$. For the Schrödinger regularity $s$, Kishimoto proved local well-posedness for $1/2\leq s\leq1$ and global well-posedness for $9/14<s<1$ below the Euclidean cubic ground-state mass. Under the same mass condition, we prove global well-posedness for every $1/2<s<1$, with polynomial bounds for the Sobolev norms.
  We add quartic and quintic corrections to Kishimoto's resonantly modified energy. The main difficulty is to cancel the interactions obstructing the global iteration without introducing singular coefficients near resonance or losing control of the higher-order terms generated by differentiation. The coefficients exploit cancellations between successive nonlinear interactions. Away from resonance, they cancel the problematic terms; near resonance, algebraic rearrangements avoid division by small phases and preserve sufficient frequency decay.
  For every $s<1/2$, we also construct solutions with arbitrarily small initial data in $H^s\times L^2\times H^{-1}$ whose wave component blows up in finite time while the Schrödinger component remains bounded in $H^s$. We combine explicit approximate solutions supported on three Fourier modes with stability at $H^{1/2}\times L^2$. Choosing successively larger frequencies controls the nonlinear interactions among infinitely many approximate solutions and makes the accumulated errors summable, while their wave amplitudes produce blow-up. These results identify $s=1/2$ as the threshold between global well-posedness and the existence of such blow-up solutions, with the endpoint unresolved.

title: Forward and pullback attraction under worst-case and ergodic exponents in a predator-prey model with bounded random refuge
abstract: We consider a predator-prey system with logistic prey, Holling type II response and a prey refuge fluctuating randomly within a band, driven by a bounded transformation of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. Bounded noise yields a deterministic compact set attracting forward uniformly in the realisation, alongside the random pullback attractor, and we compare the two. The smallest such deterministic set, the minimal uniform attracting set, is the kernel of the control system in which the accessible fraction is any measurable band-valued function, and it meets the coexistence region exactly when the upper worst-case invasion exponent of the predator is positive, whereas the pullback attractor is governed by the ergodic invasion exponent, which decides the predator's fate pathwise. When the predator becomes extinct, the closure of the union of the fibres of the pullback attractor equals the minimal uniform attracting set if and only if the upper worst-case exponent is nonpositive, and otherwise the inclusion is strict and the latter is invariant under no realisation. When the predator persists, the essential closure of the union of the fibres contains, for every frozen environment in which the predator invades, the equilibrium or a periodic orbit of the frozen system, and every state the control system can reach from them. The predator is uniformly persistent when the lower worst-case exponent is positive and almost surely not when it is negative. The ergodic exponent lies below its deterministic counterpart by an amount comparable to the curvature of the response times the variance of the accessible fraction.

title: Higher-order Sobolev stability and temporal decay estimate for the tropical climate model with small $H^1$ data
abstract: We study the stability and temporal decay of solutions to the two-dimensional tropical climate model with Laplacian dissipation in both velocity equations and no thermal diffusion. For initial data in $H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ ($s \geq 1$) with sufficiently small $H^1$ norm, we establish a unique global solution satisfying uniform $H^s$ bounds and time-integrated estimates for the velocity and temperature. The smallness is independent of $s$, and the higher Sobolev norms of the initial data need not be small. Furthermore, without additional spatial integrability or negative-order regularity of the initial data, we prove that the $\dot H^s (\mathbb{R}^2)$ norms of the solutions are $o(t^{- s / 2})$ as $t \to \infty$. We also show that this decay rate is sharp: no additional decay factor tending to zero works for all such initial data.

title: The geometry of anisotropic propagation for multidimensional reaction-diffusion equations in shifting habitats: A zero-sum stopping game approach
abstract: We study the propagation geometry of multidimensional reaction-diffusion equations in shifting habitats. Using geometric optics techniques and viscosity solution theory, we prove that the associated rate functions converge locally uniformly to the unique viscosity solution of a variational inequality with singular initial data. We identify this limit as the value of a zero-sum stopping game whose zero set determines the Wulff shape. This zero set coincides with that of the positive part of the value function of an unconstrained optimal control problem if and only if Freidlin's condition holds. When Freidlin's condition fails, we derive a pointwise characterization of the stopping-game zero set, yielding a convex hull representation. These results then yield explicit Wulff shapes and directional spreading speeds for all habitat speed. As the habitat speed increases, the Wulff shape evolves from a large ball to a truncated ball. It then develops conical, cylindrical, and paraboloidal boundary components attached to spherical parts, before eventually becoming a smaller ball. Some of these geometric transitions occur while both axial spreading speeds remain unchanged. Moreover, by characterizing the optimal trajectories, we distinguish two mechanisms of nonlocal speed selection and show that such selection can occur in oblique directions even when it is absent in both axial directions.

title: A Discrete de Rham method for linear and nonlinear fourth-order plate models
abstract: We develop and analyze a Discrete de Rham (DDR) method for the Kirchhoff--Love plate problem on general polygonal meshes and demonstrate its extension to geometrically nonlinear plates. The construction uses local degrees of freedom and polynomial reconstructions, avoiding the implementation difficulties associated with globally $C^1$-conforming approximation spaces. A new deflection reconstruction obtained from the discrete Hessian permits a uniform treatment of the load term at all polynomial degrees. The use of this reconstruction improves the convergence rates of previous DDR methods and enables the formulation of a lowest-order scheme with only vertex unknowns. We provide a stability and convergence analysis of the method and validate the theoretical results through a comprehensive set of numerical tests. The method is then extended to the coupled von Kármán equations, for which we demonstrate convergence numerically. We also study the flat-branch spectrum of a compressed perforated plate and its small-amplitude forced nonlinear response near the first critical load.

title: Continuity of solutions to nonlocal nonlinear diffusion equations
abstract: We establish an explicit modulus of continuity for locally bounded weak solutions to nonlocal porous medium type equations with measurable kernels. The nonlocal tail is only assumed to be integrable in time. The result lays a solid foundation for the intrinsic Harnack estimates of these equations.

title: A Characterization of $q$-Ary $2$-Designs and a $3$-Design Obstruction for Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}_k$ be the doubly extended Reed--Solomon code with parameters $[q+1,k,q-k+2]_q$, where $q\ge3$ is a prime power and $2\le k\le q$. We prove a conjecture of Wu and Zhou by showing that the minimum-weight codewords of $\mathcal{C}_k$ do not form a $q$-ary $3$-design when $2\le k\le q-1$. Using shortening, we extend this obstruction to every nonempty weight class with $3\le w<q+1$. We also establish that each individual nonempty positive-weight class of $\mathcal{C}_k$ forms a $q$-ary $2$-design if and only if $\gcd(k-1,q-1)=1$. Consequently, every nonempty positive-weight class below full support has exact $q$-ary design strength $2$ when this coprimality condition holds, and $1$ otherwise.The three-design obstruction follows by applying a classical subset-product character identity to a marginal covering count for three prescribed nonzero symbols. The comparison between weights rests on a covering-count formulation of the classical MDS coset-weight relations. For every linear $[n,k,d]_q$ MDS code with $2\le k\le n-1$, this formulation shows that the $q$-ary $2$-design property at any one nonempty positive weight is equivalent to the same property at every nonempty positive weight.More generally, for $2\le t\le\min\{k,d\}$, we prove that the $q$-ary $t$-design property at any $t-1$ distinct nonempty positive weights forces it at all nonempty positive weights.

title: Independence number and odd dominating models
abstract:
A dominating $K_t$-model, introduced by Illingworth and Wood [J. Graph Theory, 2025], is a sequence $(T_1,\dots,T_t)$ of pairwise vertex-disjoint subtrees of $G$ such that every vertex of $T_j$ has a neighbour in $T_i$ for $1\leq i<j\leq t$. Let $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)$ denote the maximum order of such a model. We prove two dominating-model analogues of improvements to the classical Duchet-Meyniel bound [Ann. Discrete Math., 1982]. The first extends a result of Kawarabayashi, Plummer, and Toft [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 2005]. Every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $α(G)\geq2$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)\geq(n+ω(G))/(2α(G)-1)$. Second, we prove a constant-factor improvement of the Duchet-Meyniel bound for dominating models: every graph $G$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{d}}(G)>0.51075n/α(G)$. This qualitatively extends the results of Fox [SIAM J. Discrete Math., 2010] and Balogh and Kostochka [Discrete Math., 2011].
  An odd dominating $K_t$-model is a dominating $K_t$-model with an assignment of one of two colours to each vertex of $V(T_1)\cup\dots\cup V(T_t)$, such that every edge of each $T_i$ is bichromatic and, for $1\leq i<j\leq t$, some edge between $T_i$ and $T_j$ is monochromatic. Let $\text{had}_{\text{od}}(G)$ denote the maximum order of such a model. Our constant-factor improvement of the Duchet-Meyniel bound relies on our next result: every claw-free graph $G$ satisfies $\text{had}_{\text{od}}(G)\geq 2χ(G)/3$, generalising a result of Chudnovsky and Fradkin [J. Graph Theory, 2010]. The factor 2/3 is asymptotically best possible.
  For $t\geq2$, we prove that every $n$-vertex graph with no odd dominating $K_t$-model has independence number at least $(n+t-1)/(2t-2)$. For the stronger notion in which every vertex of $T_j$ has a neighbour of the same colour in $T_i$, we prove the analogous results with $(n+t-1)/(2t-2)$ replaced by $(n+t-1)/(3t-3)$.

title: On the sharpness of a Liouville exponent in a competitive elliptic Schrödinger system
abstract: We identify $p_*(n)=(n-1)/(n-3)$, $n\geq 5$, as the sharp exponent for Liouville theorems concerning a two-component elliptic Schrödinger system with self-focusing interactions and repulsive intercomponent coupling. We consider the strictly copositive regime, in which the repulsion strength is smaller than the geometric mean of the two self-interaction strengths. Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) established a Liouville-type nonexistence result in the range $1<p<p_*(n)$. For every $p_*(n)<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, we construct bounded, nontrivial, nonnegative entire solutions whenever the repulsion strength approaches the copositivity threshold from below. The construction combines a compact variational functional, a periodic spectral gap, and uniform exterior estimates that remove a truncation. Our result gives a negative answer to the open question posed by Quittner and Souplet (Comm. Math. Phys. 2012: 1--19) of whether strict copositivity implies nonexistence of nontrivial nonnegative entire solutions throughout the Sobolev subcritical range when $n\geq 5$.

title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
abstract: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact Kähler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely generated must factor through a hyperbolic Riemann orbifold. As applications, we derive several new restrictions on the structure of quasi-projective groups.

title: Infinite dimensional Gaussian limits for the giant component of inhomogeneous random graphs
abstract: We prove Gaussian limits for the type measure of the giant component in sparse inhomogeneous random graphs. Countable types yield convergence in a weighted Hilbert space under boundedness, irreducibility, supercriticality, and a uniform tail condition on the empirical type weights. For types on a finite dimensional closed Riemannian manifold, smooth kernels yield convergence in a negative Sobolev space for any Borel type distribution. We allow deterministic types and first order kernel perturbations; independent type sampling adds an independent Gaussian term. The proof combines a seeded exploration identity, Hilbert space martingale limits, tail estimates, and inversion of the branching operator outside the giant. Finite types with random parameters are covered. A heat kernel example gives explicit variances for all spectral modes.

title: Token graphs of stars
abstract: The $k$-token graph $F_k(G)$ of a graph $G$ has as vertices the $k$-subsets of $V(G)$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. Let $S_n$ be the star with $n$ leaves. Since every edge of $S_n$ is incident with the center, $F_k(S_n)$ is the inclusion graph of the $(k-1)$- and the $k$-subsets of the leaves. We use this identification to determine its diameter, radius, girth, Wiener index and number of spanning trees, and to decompose $F_k(S_{n+1})$ into $F_k(S_n)$ and $F_{k-1}(S_n)$ joined by a matching; the parameters of $F_k(S_n)$ that are already known, such as its connectivity, independence number, automorphism group and spectrum, are collected in an appendix. The two parameters that the identification does not settle are the domination and the packing numbers. For the domination number we prove, for fixed $k \ge 3$, that $(1-\frac{k-2}{k-1}π_k-o(1))\binom{n}{k-1} \le γ(F_k(S_n)) \le (1-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{k-2}{k-1})^{k-2}+o(1))\binom{n}{k-1}$, where $π_k$ is the Turan density of the complete $(k-1)$-uniform hypergraph on $k$ vertices; for $k=3$ both constants are equal to $\frac{3}{4}$, so that $γ(F_3(S_n))=(\frac{3}{4}+o(1))\binom{n}{2}$, and the upper bound takes the exact form $γ(F_3(S_n)) \le \binom{n}{2}-\lfloor (n+1)^2/8 \rfloor$, which is attained for all $3 \le n \le 10$. For $k=4$ we improve the upper bound to $(\frac{17}{27}+o(1))\binom{n}{3}$, which matches the lower bound if Turan's conjecture $π_4=\frac{5}{9}$ holds. We show that the packing number of $F_k(S_n)$ equals the maximum size $A(n+1,4,k)$ of a binary constant-weight code, and we characterize when the packing and the domination numbers coincide, namely, for $2 \le k \le n-1$, exactly when $n=2k-1$ and a Steiner system $S(k-2,k-1,2k-1)$ exists; in that case both parameters equal the Catalan number $C_k$.

title: The Dirichlet problem for complex Monge--Ampère equations with Hölder continuous right-hand sides
abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem for the complex Monge--Ampère equation on bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains with $C^3$ boundary and $C^3$ boundary values. For every $n\ge2$ and $0<α<1$, each continuous Bedford--Taylor solution with a strictly positive $C^α$ right-hand side satisfies a global $C^{2,α}$ estimate. There is a unique such solution, which is strictly plurisubharmonic up to the boundary. Combining new boundary estimates with weighted integral estimates for the trace of the complex Hessian along an auxiliary parabolic flow, we obtain global $C^{1,β}$ bounds for every fixed $0<β<1$ in every dimension. Green function estimates and comparison arguments near the boundary give the boundary Hessian bound. Solutions of auxiliary Dirichlet problems with locally constant right-hand sides have uniform $W^{2,2n^2}$ bounds. Rescaling and interpolation then reduce the global Hessian estimate to interior regularity.

title: Local study of generic dynamical systems on the b-symplectic plane
abstract: Let $\Gb$ be the group of germs of planar diffeomorphisms, fixing the origin, which preserve the standard b-symplectic form. The group acts on itself, under the usual left-right action and we identify, in the generic case, a simple representative of each orbit, depending on a non-vanishing, univariate, function. We then study the action of $\Gb$ on b-symplectic vector fields. For those fields that do not vanish at the origin, we establish a flow-box type theorem, while, for those that do vanish there, we show that the study of their conjugacy classes reduces to a classification of functions. We present this classification, when the origin is a regular point for these functions, while if it is a critical point, we present the orbits of their 2-jets. Finally, we address the problem of whether an element of $\Gb$ can be realised as the time-1 map of a b-symplectic vector field.

title: An Arbitrary-Order Distributional Finite Element Method for the Curl--Dev Grad Stokes System
abstract: We develop an arbitrary-order distributional finite element method for the three-dimensional curl--dev grad Stokes system governed by the Hessian complex. On tetrahedral meshes, the method couples degree-$(k+1)$ nonconforming symmetric-tensor virtual elements, degree-$k$ tangential-normal continuous traceless tensor elements, and Raviart--Thomas elements of index $k$, without additional virtual-element stabilization. Building on zero-extension curl--div theory, we derive a well-posed distributional saddle-point formulation with an $H(\operatorname{div})$ vector multiplier. A divergence-augmented discrete norm equivalence controls the full Raviart--Thomas space modulo translations and underpins mesh-uniform stability for each fixed $k\ge0$. We establish optimal $O(h^{k+1})$ energy error estimates and an optimal $O(h^{k+2})$ $L^2$ error estimate for the full symmetric-tensor approximation, under suitable regularity and load approximation assumptions. As an application, the method supplies the Stokes block of a decoupled triharmonic scheme with optimal Hessian error estimates. Numerical experiments support the predicted convergence rates for computable quantities.

title: Inhomogeneous deformations of $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$: triviality for any number of odd parameters
abstract: We treat a symmetrized mixed-oscillator deformation family of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$, $N,n\geq1$, with even mixed coefficients $β_{u,i}$ and one odd square-zero parameter. We derive the deformed bracket from an oscillator realization, show that its coefficient is determined by the realization, and exhibit an explicit odd primitive, normalized by its vanishing on $\mathfrak{sp}(2n)$. Every odd primitive differs from it by a unique inner derivation. For $N=1$ this is the case $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$ treated earlier. With multiple odd parameters the deformed bracket is the sum of the single-parameter deformations and is again trivial. The trivialization, however, is not additive: it is the product of the single-parameter trivializations followed by a nonsymplectic change of the bosonic generators. The main results are formalized in Lean~4, with the algebras constructed by generators and relations; what is not formalized is stated in the appendix.

title: On mod p Hecke algebras of abstract p-adic automorphic forms
abstract: We study completed local shallow Hecke algebras acting on residual automorphic forms attached to projective augmented modules for $\GL_2(\Q_p)$. For odd primes $p$, we prove that the maximal ideal has nilpotence exponent $O(p^{r/2})$ on the level-$r$ generalized eigenspace. For $p\ge5$, if the corresponding Hecke eigenspace in the residual smooth dual has finite length as a $\GL_2(\Q_p)$-representation, then the completed local algebra is noetherian of Krull dimension at least two. If, in addition, its cotangent space has dimension at most two, then it is a formal power series ring in two variables. The nilpotence bound follows by conjugating level subgroups. To deduce the dimension bound, we replace the Fourier pairing in the classical nilpotence method with an inequality comparing the dimension of each finite-level generalized eigenspace with that of its Hecke eigenspace. We apply these results to modular curves and definite quaternion algebras.

title: Stochastic Parallel Transport along Markov Processes: I. General Theory
abstract: We give a framework for transporting vectors along Markov processes that may have jumps, without assuming a manifold or other specific geometric structure. We prove existence and uniqueness of the resulting transport. In doing so, we develop a theory of vector bundles defined quasi-everywhere, in which the vectors live, and an axiomatic framework for energy forms that determine the bundle and the transport.

title: On-the-Fly Reduced Bases Through the Lens of Augmented Krylov Methods
abstract: On-the-fly reduced order models (ROMs) are widely used in applications where multiple queries of large-scale models are required in an iterative method, like PDE-constrained optimization or fluid-structure interaction. When compared to classical offline--online ROMs, they have the advantage of being agnostic to any precomputed training data, mesh or geometry, which makes them more general linear/nonlinear solver accelerators. The main goal of this work is to study the effect of using a reduced basis constructed on-the-fly to accelerate a restarted Krylov algorithm, and to formally bridge this category of data-driven methods with classical augmented Krylov methods. The guiding principles of on-the-fly reduced basis will be translated into the framework of Krylov subspace methods, for a Petrov-Galerkin projection method. Previous corrections generated by the algorithm are stored in a snapshot matrix, and a singular value decomposition (SVD) is used to determine a reduced subspace containing the most significant directions. It will be shown that this approach can be embedded in the framework of Krylov methods with augmented or deflated restart, but with a different, data-driven recycling strategy. An analytical study will be presented to determine the consequences of augmentation by ROM-based vectors. Numerical experiments on a convection-diffusion problem with various degrees of convection will show that the proposed methodology yields results comparable to classical iterative linear solvers in some regimes, especially for nearly symmetric or skew-symmetric operators. At equal sizes of the augmentation basis, the convergence was sometimes faster with the proposed framework than with deflation methods.

title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
abstract: We study which groups arise as fundamental groups of complements of affine Hurwitz curves. In every such group the product of the meridians is central and maps to the vector of component degrees in homology; this rules out, for instance, the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(p,q)$ with $\lvert p\rvert\neq\lvert q\rvert$, and the groups of links with at least two components and vanishing linking numbers. O. V. Kulikova circumvented this obstruction for $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)$ by passing to the non-Hopfian group $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)\times\mathbb{Z}$, which Vik. S. Kulikov's doubling algorithm realizes in degree $768$. We give an explicit braid monodromy factorization of degree 12 with this group. The corresponding curve is not isotopic to an algebraic curve, yet it is obtained from a union of three quartics in a pencil by a single twist along a circle. More generally, for every closed braid $\hatβ$ we realize $π_1(S^3\setminus\hatβ)\times\mathbb{Z}$ by an explicit Hurwitz curve, again a twist of a union of quartics in a pencil. In the other direction, a Hurwitz curve with group $\operatorname{BS}(k,k+1)\times\mathbb{Z}$ has degree at least $4$, as every Hurwitz curve consisting of a conic and a line is H-isotopic to an algebraic one, after separation of its critical points. Finally, we show that certain semiholomorphic germs, among them those realizing the generalized Borromean rings, are braided surfaces but not Hurwitz curve germs.

title: Dual Model Predictive Control through Sampling-Based Belief Propagation
abstract: We propose a sampling-based dual model predictive control (MPC) approach that combines belief propagation with parameterized feedback policy optimization. By sampling uncertain dynamics and process noise, we approximate the evolution of the hyperstate over the prediction horizon, allowing future control decisions to adapt to anticipated observations and belief updates. This enables the controller to account for the future value of information without explicit exploration incentives. We establish almost-sure uniform convergence of the sample-average objective to the finite-horizon expected objective over a compact policy class. The approach is specialized to Bayesian linear regression and evaluated on stochastic systems with constant and time-varying uncertain dynamics. We compare our approach to certainty equivalent control, and an MPC that optimizes over open-loop control sequences rather than feedback policies, demonstrating the benefits of our method in terms of both control performance and information gain.

title: Non-log-concave $τ$-polynomials of regular graphs
abstract: For any simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, write its chromatic polynomial in the rising factorial basis as $P(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}(-1)^{n-j}c_j x^{\langle j\rangle}$, where $x^{\langle j\rangle}=\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}(x+i)$ for any $j\ge 1$ and $x^{\langle0\rangle}=1$. Brenti (1992) introduced the $τ$-polynomial and its augmented version, defined by $$τ(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}c_jx^j, \qquad \overlineτ(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}j!c_jx^j.$$ He asked whether $τ(G,x)$ always has only real roots and whether $\overlineτ(G,x)$ always has a log-concave coefficient sequence. In this paper, we show that for any integer $d\ge 4$, there exists an integer $h_d$ such that, for every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ of girth at least $h_d$, the coefficient sequence of $τ(G,x)$ fails to be log-concave. This failure also occurs for $\overlineτ(G,x)$, and Newton's inequalities imply that $τ(G,x)$ has nonreal roots. Thus both questions have counterexamples among regular graphs of arbitrarily large girth.

title: CVaR Deep Optimal Stopping
abstract: Risk-sensitive optimal stopping is useful when poor stopping outcomes carry substantial costs, as in option exercise, sequential medical treatment, and safety-critical control. A natural objective is Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) of the stopped reward. We develop a theoretical framework and algorithm for CVaR deep optimal stopping. The framework and algorithm address four difficulties in applying risk-sensitive reinforcement learning to optimal stopping: state augmentation, score-function pathology, blindness to success, and dependence on auxiliary networks. We isolate three structural properties of optimal stopping: single-point reward, action-independent dynamics, and sum-zero gradient. We exploit these properties to establish Markov optimality without state augmentation and derive a pathwise gradient estimator. Under bounded policy derivatives, the pathwise estimator has bounded second moments near deterministic policies, avoiding the divergence that can occur with score-function estimators. Building on this framework, we propose DIOS (Distribution-Informed Optimal Stopping) to address the remaining two difficulties. A per-time-step soft penalty combined with tail-level annealing mitigates blindness to success. Estimating the reward quantile directly from each batch removes the need for an auxiliary critic. For a fixed tail level, we establish a finite-time stationarity guarantee under regularity assumptions along the training iterates. Across the 24 main Bermudan max-call configurations, DIOS achieves the highest mean CVaR and the shortest recorded training time among the tested CVaR baselines.

title: Fractal solutions to the two-dimensional floating body problem
abstract: In this paper, the first construction of an entire class of two-dimensional fractal bodies that float in water in equilibrium is explicitly given. Their boundaries are described by planar fractal Zindler curves which are constructed using fractal projective hedgehogs. The areas of these bodies are seen to be well-defined and their expression is explicitly computed. To this end, a result concerning the continuity of the Lebesgue measure with respect to the Hausdorff metric for compact sets is given. Furthermore, the Hausdorff dimension $w$ of these fractal curves is shown to coincide with the Hausdorff dimension of the graph of a Weierstrass function associated to the corresponding fractal projective hedgehog. The fractal Zindler curves are proved to have halving chords of constant length that split both the area and the $w$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the curve into exact halves.

title: New families of maximal curves not covered by the Hermitian curve and their cyclic automorphism groups
abstract: For every prime power $q>2$, integer $n\ge2$ and $1\le r\le 2n-1$, we construct an $\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $T_{q,n,r}$ with Kummer equation \[ z^{q^n+1}=η^{-R}y(1-y^{q-1})^R, \qquad \frac{q^r-1}{q-1},\] where $η\in\mathbb F_{q^{2n}}^*$ satisfies $η^{q^n}=-η$. For fixed $q,n$, these are cyclic covers of the projective line over a single field, indexed by the integer $r$. Writing $δ=\gcd(q^n+1,R)$, we prove that the genus is $(q-1)(q^n+1-δ)/2$ and that $T_{q,n,r}$ is covered by the Hermitian curve $\mathcal H_{q^n}$ over an algebraic closure if and only if $\min(r,2n-r)$ divides $n$. For $1<r<n$ and $δ=1$, the full automorphism group is cyclic of order $(q-1)(q^n+1)$, and distinct values of $r$ give curves that are nonisomorphic over an algebraic closure despite having the same genus and full automorphism group. We also give explicit equations and genera for all their Galois subfields. When $n\ge 4$ is a power of two, this produces families over a fixed field whose members are not covered by $\mathcal H_{q^n}$.

title: Critical radial Green potential heat flow: A tension-controlled residue and a two-bubble example
abstract: We compare two heat flows for the same corotational map of a disk into a warped product of two spheres, with the same fixed boundary values. The ordinary harmonic map heat flow develops a singularity in finite time. When the domain metric is instead determined by the critically normalized Green potential of the current energy distribution, the solution exists for all time. Two harmonic spheres of energy $4π$ form at separated scales, in addition to a nonconstant harmonic root. The energy and the image diameter of the necks tend to zero without restriction to a sequence of times. The main estimate controls the difference between the inner source mass and its critical value by the weighted tension. This is necessary because that difference is integrated over a neck of unbounded logarithmic length. Along a sequence of times the Green metric on the middle neck is asymptotically cylindrical after a spatially constant normalization.

title: Optimal Batching with Abandonment: Threshold Policies Under Risk-Neutral and Risk-Sensitive Criteria
abstract: We study optimal batching in a discrete-time Markovian system with Bernoulli arrivals and independent item abandonment. Each batch earns a per-item processing reward and incurs holding, abandonment, and fixed stopping costs. We formulate the batching decision as an optimal stopping problem and characterize optimal threshold policies under risk-neutral, risk-seeking, and risk-averse criteria. Under risk neutrality and the entropic risk-seeking criterion, the value function admits a forward-recursion representation, and the resulting reduced objectives are strictly unimodal. In the risk-seeking case, the objective is strictly discretely concave, yielding an explicit marginal-cost condition. For risk aversion, the unregularized entropic continuation branch may diverge, precluding standard fixed-point arguments. We therefore study a regularized robust surrogate formulated as a minimax problem with a relative-entropy penalty and capped likelihood ratio. We establish the existence of an optimal threshold policy and derive an explicit truncated-Gibbs worst-case distribution. We also study repeated batch clearing under both the long-run average and discounted criteria, for which the threshold objectives remain strictly unimodal. Numerical experiments examine threshold sensitivity to system parameters, costs, and risk preferences.

title: Variance-Reduced Stochastic Hessian-Driven Nesterov Acceleration with Adam-Style Preconditioning
abstract: Stochastic first-order methods use sampled gradients to reduce per-iteration costs, but estimation errors can slow convergence and, in some settings, cause divergence. To improve gradient accuracy while retaining acceleration, we develop scalar and diagonal versions of VR-Adam-SHANG for smooth stochastic convex optimization. The methods combine STORM-type recursive estimation, Adam-style preconditioning, and SHANG's accelerated interpolation and correction, using at most two stochastic gradient evaluations per iteration without full-gradient refreshes. Under unbiased sampling, bounded variance, and mean-square smoothness of gradient noise, polynomial steps with prescribed initialization yield $O(1/K)$ mean-square gradient-estimation error and expected objective-gap bounds combining $O(1/K^2)$ initial-energy decay with an $O(1/\sqrt K)$ stochastic term after $K$ iterations. These guarantees require neither monotonicity of the preconditioner nor a uniform positive lower bound on its eigenvalues. The analysis also establishes polynomial-step convergence of projected nonrecursive Adam-SHANG-s, filling a gap in its original theory. Experiments compare the methods at matched sample-gradient budgets. In every tested setting, at least one of the two versions achieves the lowest mean terminal objective gap among all compared methods.

title: The Escobar Constant for Two-dimensional Disks
abstract: Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian surface homeomorphic to a closed disk, with boundary length $L$. We establish sharp upper bounds for its Escobar constant under upper bounds on the Gaussian curvature. If $K_g\leq 0$, then $I(M,g)\leq 2/π$, with equality if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to a Euclidean disk. If $K_g\leqκ$ for some $κ>0$, $L<2π/\sqrtκ$, and $\operatorname{Area}_g(M)<2π/κ$, then $I(M,g)\leq\frac{4}{\sqrtκL}\arcsin(\frac{\sqrtκL}{2π})$, with equality if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to the geodesic disk of the same perimeter contained in an open hemisphere of the sphere of constant curvature $κ$. We also discuss the higher order Escobar constant for planar domains. In particular, we construct counterexamples to Hassannezhad and Siffert's conjecture.

title: Persistence landscape velocity: Closed formulas and a topological probe of quantum criticality
abstract:
We introduce the landscape velocity $ξ$, a scalar measure of variation of a parameter-dependent persistence landscape. For families of finite barcodes whose bars are all born at the fixed filtration value $0$, we show that $ξ$ is the $L^2$ speed of the landscape curve where the sorted death times are differentiable and derive an exact closed formula that requires no persistence landscape at all: the death times of the barcodes, as functions of the parameter, suffice. For the velocity of the empirical mean of several landscapes we also prove a closed formula which, again, strikingly requires neither the empirical mean landscape nor any of the individual landscapes, only the individual barcodes.
  As an application, we revisit Olsthoorn's persistent homology analysis of the transverse-field Ising chain. Whereas his approach uses different homology degrees and summaries depending on the boundary conditions, ours uses $H_0$ only and a single rule: the position of the maximum of $ξ$. This rule locates the quantum critical point for both periodic and open boundary conditions, and for both mutual-information and correlator-based dissimilarities. The position of the maximum converges to the critical point faster than all the estimators we can extract from Olsthoorn's work. In the 4 scenarios considered (different boundary conditions and different dissimilarity matrices), the peak of the normalized velocity becomes increasingly pronounced with system size, with observed logarithmic growth. This logarithmic growth is proved for periodic boundaries with correlator dissimilarity under stated hypotheses, identifying landscape velocity as a singular topological response to quantum criticality.

title: Harmonic and Monogenic Representations of White Noise and its weighted harmonic Bergman estimates
abstract: Continuing Feichtinger's generalized stochastic process theory, we analyze harmonic and monogenic representations of white noise in Euclidean spaces. We define its convolution with square-integrable functions. Using the weighted Sobolev regularity of the white noise, we establish a high-dimensional Sokhotski-Plemelj formula for the white noise density. Furthermore, we embed these representations into new weighted Bergman spaces, proving that the weighted Bergman norms of the harmonic representations are bounded by the white noise's weighted Sobolev norms.

title: On the Kőnig-Egerváry theorem for $k$-trees
abstract: The famous Kőnig-Egerváry theorem is equivalent to the statement that a graph is bipartite if and only if the matching number equals the vertex cover number for every induced subgraph. Bessy, Ochem, and Rautenbach (J. Graph Theory 91 (2019) 73-87) generalized this theorem to $k$-paths by introducing the class $\mathcal{G}_k$ of graphs where, for every induced subgraph, the maximum number of disjoint paths of order $k$ equals the minimum number of vertices intersecting all such paths. They provided complete structural characterizations of graphs in $\mathcal{G}_k$ for $k \in \{3, 4\}$, and for odd $k$ when no cycle of order less than $k$ is present. Inspired by this nice work, we extend the Kőnig-Egerváry theorem to $k$-trees (i.e., trees with exactly $k$ vertices). We define the class $\mathcal{J}_k$ of graphs where, for every induced subgraph, the maximum number of disjoint trees of order $k$ equals the minimum number of vertices intersecting all such trees, and provide complete structural descriptions of graphs in $\mathcal{J}_k$ for all $k \ge 3$.

title: Weak Dissolution of Groups for Rearrangement
abstract: Suppose that $k$ of $n$ classrooms are to be dissolved and their students moved to the other classrooms so that the numbers of students in any two remaining classrooms differ by at most $d$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition on the numbers of students for this to be possible whichever $k$ classrooms are dissolved. Moreover, we determine how small the largest classroom can be when this is possible. In particular, when all classrooms have different sizes, the smallest possible size of the largest classroom is $d+\lceil (n-d-1)(n-d)/(2k)\rceil$ if $k<(n-d-1)/2$, and it is $n$ or $n+1$ otherwise. This extends the results of Siriseriwan and Sripatak, who studied the case $d=0$.

title: Monotonicity of Wang's recursive sequence and logarithmically complete monotonicity of the reciprocal of the inverse tangent
abstract: In this paper, we study a sequence $b_n$, posed by Fei Wang, which is defined by $b_1=\frac13$ and a convolution-type recursive relation. We derive the generating functions of $nb_n$ and of $b_n$, the latter of which is $\ln\frac{\operatorname{arctanh}x}{x}$, and represent $b_n$ as a moment integral over $[0,1]$ with a positive density. From this representation we prove that the sequence $b_n$ is positive and logarithmically convex, that the sequence $nb_n$ is strictly decreasing, and that the ratio $\frac{b_{n+1}}{b_n}$ is strictly increasing in $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with limit $1$, which answers Wang's problem. We also give a determinantal expression and closed-form formulas for $b_n$ involving Stirling numbers of the first kind and partial Bell polynomials. Finally, we prove that the function $\frac1{\arctan x}$ is logarithmically completely monotonic on $(0,\infty)$.

title: On Rankin Invariants of Ideal Lattices
abstract: The Rankin constant $γ_{n,k}$ measures the largest discriminant of a densest rank $k$ sublattice of a lattice in $\R^n$ over all such lattices of rank $n$ and their exact values are mostly open. For a general lattice $L\subset \R^n$ of rank $n$, the problem of determining its Rankin invariant $γ_{n,k}(L)$ is to find the discriminant of such a densest sublattice. There are no general formulas to compute the discriminant of any arbitrary rank $k$ sublattice. This paper specializes to the case of ideal lattices arising from ideals of number fields, and provides two approaches to study Rankin constants: first, we propose a systematic approach to approximate the minimum discriminant by introducing subideal lattices and proving a closed-form formula to compute $γ^{ideal}_{n,k}(L)$, the ideal Rankin invariant of the ideal lattice. Subsequently, we establish necessary conditions on the underlying number field for the existence of an ideal lattice admitting an optimal subideal lattice with a prescribed minimum discriminant. Secondly, we consider ideal lattices with arbitrary sublattices. We compute $γ_{9,2}$ and improve the current known bounds of the Rankin constants $γ_{5,2}$, $γ_{7,2}$ and $γ_{9,3},γ_{9,4}$, and provide an algebraic construction of the lattice that was used in dimensions $5$ and $7$.

title: Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
abstract: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.

title: Data Center Power Flexibility Characterization: A DeepSets Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract: Data centers can provide power flexibility through the scheduling of computing workloads, cooling systems, and batteries. Characterizing this flexibility online is useful but challenging because of the complex coupling among these resources. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a role-conditioned cross-head DeepSets reinforcement learning approach to characterize the power flexibility interval of a data center at each time step. First, we formulate the flexibility characterization problem as a Markov decision process that jointly models the three resources under a carbon budget, with actions specifying the upper and lower endpoints of the power flexibility interval. We then design DeepSets actor and critic that represent delay-tolerant workloads as an unordered set, enabling the proposed approach to accommodate varying numbers of workloads with a fixed number of trainable parameters. Finally, because maximizing the width of the flexibility interval requires moving its endpoints in opposite directions, we develop a role-conditioned cross-head decoder that distinguishes their respective roles while keeping them coordinated. Case studies on the Google Cluster Data show that the proposed approach provides more than twice the daily flexibility of the standard soft actor-critic method with nearly zero carbon overshoot while using 87.7% fewer trainable parameters.

title: Local exact boundary controllability for the full compressible magnetohydrodynamic equations
abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with the local exact boundary controllability for the full compressible magnetohydrodynamic equations in a bounded domain in two and three space dimensions. We establish the local exact controllability around a constant equilibrium state. Our proof relies on the observability and controllability analysis of a suitably reformulated linearized system, together with a fixed point argument in weighted Sobolev spaces. The main novelty of this paper is to overcome the structural difficulties arising from the divergence free constraint and the strong coupling between the fluid and magnetic variables. To accommodate the solenoidal constraint, we introduce a magnetic potential formulation and develop a mixed coordinate approach.

title: A Globally Convergent Line-Search Quasi-Newton Method for Discounted Markov Decision Processes
abstract: In this paper, we develop a line-search quasi-Newton (LSQN) method for discounted Markov decision processes (MDPs). The method maintains an inverse model to approximate the inverse of the current policy Jacobian and refines it through an inner learning procedure that preserves existing secant conditions and achieves the prescribed accuracy in at most $n$ queries in exact arithmetic for an MDP with $n$ states, even when the initial inverse model is singular. A sign-based direction correction combined with an Armijo line search ensures monotonic decrease of the Bellman residual norm across policy changes without requiring a value-iteration fallback. We prove global Q-linear residual convergence and local Q-superlinear convergence of the value iterates from arbitrary finite initial value vectors and inverse models, without requiring a unique optimal policy. Numerical experiments show competitive performance against nine baselines, while public benchmarks demonstrate that the inner learning procedure typically requires far fewer than $n$ learning queries.

title: The sharp Fourier extension estimate for the sphere
abstract: The full strong Fourier extension estimate for the unit sphere is established in every ambient dimension at least three. The finite Knapp boundary is obtained by combining a uniform diagonal estimate on rescaled spherical graphs with a transverse product bound. A Whitney decomposition and a dyadic dual pairing yield strong type at the exact scaling exponents. The critical local estimate and the strict mixed range come from the recent work on Euclidean local smoothing.

title: Parametrize Integer Programming by Packing Imbalanced Circuits
abstract: We study the standard form Integer Programming problem (IP) parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number. This number is $0$ if and only if $A$ can be transformed to a totally unimodular matrix by row operations, in which case (IP) is solvable in polynomial time. We show that if the constraint matrix represents a graphic matroid, (IP) is fixed-parameter tractable when parametrized by the imbalanced circuit packing number of the matrix. The proof combines an Erdős-Pósa property for edge-colored non-monochromatic cycles with a reduction to mixed-integer programming using few integer variables. In contrast, by a reduction from the parity potential problem, we show NP-completeness of feasibility of (IP) when the constraint matrix represents a cographic matroid, even if kernel of the constraint matrix is $2$-regular and imbalanced circuits pairwise intersect.

title: Jacobi fields and Jacobi sections for semisprays on Lie algebroids: transverse variations and equivalences
abstract: We study the relationship between Jacobi sections and Jacobi fields associated with semisprays on Lie algebroids. First, we characterize compatible transverse variations in terms of Lie algebroid morphisms. This characterization leads to a variational description of Jacobi sections: a section along an integral curve of a semispray is a Jacobi section if and only if it arises as the infinitesimal variation of a compatible transverse variation of a dynamical variation satisfying a suitable condition on its image in the base. We also investigate the relationship between Jacobi sections and Jacobi fields through the anchor map. We prove that every Jacobi section projects to a Jacobi field, and establish a converse when the corresponding base variation is contained in a single leaf of the characteristic foliation.

title: Iterative Interference Cancellation for Near-Field XL-MIMO Networks with LoS Channels
abstract: In extra-large multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems, near-field users experience spherical wavefront propagation, offering higher spatial resolution than far-field plane-wave models, but complicating signal detection and interference cancellation. Under line-of-sight conditions, we propose a weighted-rate successive interference cancellation (WR-SIC) scheme whose ordering metric exploits the enhanced spatial degrees of freedom of near-field propagation to prioritize users with stronger channels. An iterative detection and decoding (IDD) scheme with LDPC coding is then developed. Simulations in hybrid near- and far-field deployments show that the proposed WR-SIC and IDD schemes improve bit-error and sum rates over existing schemes

title: Weak $λ$-sets and almost-normal Isbell-Mrówka spaces
abstract: We determine the least cardinality of a set of reals that is not a weak $λ$-set, proving that it is $\max\{\mathfrak b,\mathfrak s\}$, where $\mathfrak b$ and $\mathfrak s$ are the bounding and splitting numbers. We prove that if $\mathfrak s<\mathfrak b$, then every first countable weak $λ$-space is a $λ$-space. We also show, relative to the consistency of $\mathsf{ZFC}$, that the existence of a weak $λ$-set that is not a $λ$-set is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}+\mathfrak b=\mathfrak s$. In particular, we show that in the model obtained by adding $ω_2$ Cohen reals over a model of $\mathsf{CH}$, every weak $λ$-set is a $λ$-set. Finally, we construct an almost-normal MAD family under $\mathsf{CH}$ and show that no such family exists under $\mathsf{OCA}_{\mathrm T}+\mathfrak{ap}>ω_1$. Thus, the existence of an almost-normal MAD family is independent of $\mathsf{ZFC}$.

title: A divisorial domain with non-Prüfer normalization
abstract: We answer a 1968 question of Heinzer by constructing a two-dimensional local divisorial domain whose normalization is not Prüfer.

title: An Adaptive Short-Step Variant of BroxGD with Linear Convergence under Quadratic Growth
abstract: Broximal Gradient Descent (BroxGD), recently analyzed by Richtárik et al. (arXiv:2605.08850v1), is a projection-free sister method to Projected Gradient Descent (ProjGD) for solving $\min_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)$, where $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ and $\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ is nonempty, closed and convex. The method performs local linear minimization over the feasible set intersected with a Euclidean ball and carefully prescribed radius. Like ProjGD, BroxGD enjoys linear convergence in the smooth strongly convex setting, with the same condition-number dependence. However, the known radius rule leading to linear convergence requires unavailable information and is therefore impractical. We develop an adaptive short-step variant of BroxGD which converges linearly for smooth convex functions under quadratic growth (generalizing strong convexity), without requiring unavailable information. We use $$z_k\in\arg\min_{z\in\mathcal X\cap\mathbb B(x_k,t_k)}\langle\nabla f(x_k),z\rangle,\quad x_{k+1}=\mathrm{Proj}_{S_k}(x_k-\nabla f(x_k)/L),$$ where $L$ is the smoothness constant of $f$, $\mathbb B(x,t)$ is the Euclidean ball centered at $x$ of radius $t$, and $S_k$ is the line segment connecting $x_k$ and $z_k$. The radius is updated by $t_{k+1}=\max\{\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|,t_k/2\}$. Projection onto $S_k$ requires only scalar clipping. Assuming an exact local linear minimization oracle, each update uses one oracle call. For any positive initial radius, we bound all oracle calls to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ and obtain $O((L/α)\log(1/\varepsilon))$ for fixed initialization, where $α=\min\{α_0,L\}$ and $α_0>0$ is the quadratic-growth constant.

title: On quantitative aspects of ideal membership certificate and GCD inequality for polynomials evaluated at almost units
abstract: In this paper, we obtain an effective bounds for the ideal membership certificate in polynomial rings over almost all rings of S-integers, thereby generalizing results of Aschenbrenner and Evertse and Gyory. We also establish an effective refinement of a result of Xiao, building on earlier work of Levin and Corvaja and Zannier. In particular, we provide explicit bounds for both the number and the total degrees of the exceptional hypersurfaces arising in an inequality that bounds the greatest common divisor of multivariable polynomials evaluated at almost S-units under consideration. As an application of our results, we obtain an effective refinement of a theorem of Corvaja and Zannier: Let $(F_n)_n$ and $(G_n)_n$ be two linear recurrence sequences and $\mathcal{N}$ be the set of positive integers $n$ such that $F_n/G_n$ is an integer. Hadamard quotient theorem, conjectured by Pisot and proven by Van der Poorten states that if the set $\mathcal{N}$ coincides with $\mathbb{N}$ then $\left(F_n/G_n\right)_n$ is itself linear recurrence sequence. Corvaja-Zannier proved that if $\mathcal{N}$ is infinite set, then there exists a nonzero polynomial $P(X)$ such that $\left( P(n)F_n/G_n\right)_n$ agrees with a linear recurrence sequence for all $n$ in a suitable arithmetic progression. We give an explicit bound $C$, depending explicitly on the parameters of the recurrence sequences such that, the conclusion holds if $\mathcal{N}$ contains at least $C$ elements.

title: Gamma classes, central connection matrices, and tt* geometry
abstract: We review the gamma class of complex projective space, but from the point of view of topological-antitopological fusion. We deconstruct the central connection matrix which appears in the work of Dubrovin, Galkin-Golyshev-Iritani, and Cotti-Dubrovin-Guzzetti.

title: Ricci pseudo symmetric Anisotropic Fluid Spacetime admitting Hyperbolic solitons with Ricci vector field
abstract: This work focuses on an anisotropic fluid spacetime with these unique forms of the stress-energy tensor associated with radial pressure and a transverse pressure p. In an anisotropic fluid spacetime , we mani- fest curvatures symmetry such as Ricci pseudo-symmetric and prove that Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime is generalized quasi- Einstein spacetime. We deduce the Einstein gravitational field equation of Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime. In the framework of pseudo-Riemannian geometry, specifically, we study the quasi-conformal Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime, which exhibit the dark matter era. Moreover, we discuss the hyperbolic Ricci soliton and Hyperbolic Yamabe soliton on Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime with a time-like Ricci vector field. Finally, we turn up the char- acteristics of hyperbolic Ricci soliton and hyperbolic Yamabe soliton on Ricci pseudo-symmetric anisotropic fluid spacetime with a time-like Ricci vector field.

title: Property $R_\infty$ for Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson Groups
abstract: We prove that every Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson group $G_{n,r}$, with $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, has property $R_\infty$. In particular, every automorphism of Thompson's group $V = G_{2,1}$ has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes. These results answer questions of Olukoya and of Lins de Araujo, de Oliveira-Tosti and Santos Rego. We also prove that a homeomorphism under which no eventually periodic sequence has a finite orbit has a locally finite centralizer in $G_{n,r}$.

title: Tail behaviour of infimum of Gaussian processes
abstract: We investigate the upper tail of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$, where $X$ is a centred Gaussian process (GP) with continuous sample paths on a nonempty compact metric space $\mathcal T$. As suggested by the findings of [1], the exponential rate is governed by an optimal-measure problem, while the exact prefactor depends on the local geometry of the corresponding contact set. In the full-contact regime, we strengthen the known Gumbel max-domain of attraction property of the distribution of $\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)$ by establishing the von Mises condition. For fractional Brownian motion on $[a,b]$, $0<a<b$, with Hurst index $H\in(0,1/2)$, we also determine the order of the logarithmic correction to the leading Gaussian exponential. For finite contact sets, we distinguish dominated, smooth-critical, and rough-critical regimes and derive exact asymptotics of $P\{\inf_{t\in\mathcal T}X(t)>u\}$ as $u\to\infty$ under suitable local assumptions. We illustrate our findings with examples including fractional Brownian motion and the fractional Brownian sheet.

title: Three-Dimensional Stability of Weakly Asymmetric Burgers Vortices: A Circulation-Independent Asymmetry Threshold and Optimal Decay
abstract: Burgers vortices are stationary solutions of the Navier--Stokes equations in a background straining flow and serve as a model for vortex tubes in three-dimensional turbulence. In this paper, we consider weakly asymmetric strains and establish the local nonlinear asymptotic stability of the corresponding Burgers vortices against small three-dimensional perturbations for arbitrary circulation. Our proof exploits the specific axial structure of the linearized operator, combining a two-dimensional resolvent analysis with decay estimates for axial derivatives to control the full three-dimensional evolution. A first-moment decomposition isolates the slow modes, and Gaussian resolvent bounds are transferred to polynomially weighted spaces. This yields nonlinear stability with the endpoint exponential decay rate $(1-λ)/2$, where $λ$ denotes the strain asymmetry, without any additional polynomial factor in time. An exact nonlinear first-moment law demonstrates that this rate is optimal over the full admissible perturbation class, including at zero circulation.

title: Learning calibrated probabilistic forecasts using Koopman mode decomposition and the continuous ranked probability score
abstract: Well-calibrated forecasting for non-linear dynamical systems is essential in science and engineering applications such as fluid dynamics and weather prediction. We present a forecasting method combining probabilistic machine learning with the structured linear dynamics of Koopman mode decomposition. Within this framework, the observation, linear dynamics, and state reconstruction operators are constructed using standard machine learning architectures, producing predictive distributions via the pushforward of injected noise samples. The model is trained using a proper scoring rule, the continuous ranked probability score, to directly target calibrated, accurate forecasts. The approach is validated on two non-linear ordinary differential equation examples and two partial differential equation examples, vortex shedding and cavity flow, using both large and small, noisy datasets. Results demonstrate that known Koopman eigenfunctions and spectra can be identified and used for accurate forecasting. The model can also produce multi-modal predictive distributions, demonstrated for a trajectory initialised on the boundary between two basins of attraction. Uncertainty is captured by the sample ensemble spread, with spread--skill ratios close to one over the training horizon in several experiments, although for extended rollouts and noisy datasets, the ensemble may become under- or over-dispersed. In low-noise experiments, temporal rollout is generally accurate for at least twice the training horizon, and up to twenty times in some cases. Approximation quality is comparable to a deep ensemble approximation over the training horizon, but at a reduced computational cost and with better robustness in identifying Koopman eigenvalues.

title: Statistics of centralizers of integer matrices
abstract: With recent interests on the statistics of commuting integer matrices, we study the related problem on the statistics of the set of centralizer of a matrix. We provide asymptotics and bounds on the size of such set when restricted to integer matrices of bounded height.

title: On the monotonicity of amenable category for geometric 4-manifolds and their connected sums
abstract: We show that the amenable category is monotone with respect to the domination relation for geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums.

title: A DG method for the pseudostress-velocity formulation of the Stokes-Brinkman eigenvalue problem
abstract: We introduce a discontinuous Galerkin method for the approximation of the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the Stokes-Brinkman eigenvalue problem. The method is based on a mixed formulation in which the pseudostress tensor and the fluid velocity are the main unknowns, while the pressure can be recovered through a post-processing procedure applied to the pseudostress tensor. Using discontinuous polynomial spaces of degree $k\geq 1$, we propose a consistent symmetric interior penalty discretization for the approximation of the spectrum. Relying on the spectral theory for non-compact operators, we establish convergence of the discrete spectral approximation and derive error estimates for the method. A series of numerical experiments is presented to assess its computational performance. On the one hand, we investigate the convergence rates for different polynomial degrees, computational domains, and values of the permeability. Furthermore, we study the influence of the stabilization parameter on the discrete spectrum by comparing different choices of this parameter and examining their impact on the occurrence of spurious eigenvalues.

title: Equivalence of finite and infinite survival and sharpness of the phase transition for additive particle systems
abstract: Krone's two-stage contact process is an interacting particle system in which each site on a grid can be in one of three possible states: 0 (empty), 1 (young individual), and 2 (adult individual). Only adults can multiply, and their offspring is initially young, before growing up after an exponential time. There are two death rates, one for adult trees, and a higher one for young trees. The process is additive and has an additive dual, but unlike the contact process it is not self-dual. Answering a question of Krone, for the process on the $d$-dimensional integer grid, Foxall proved that survival of finite populations is equivalent to nontriviality of the upper invariant law. Using a completely different method, we generalise this result to processes on countable groups and along the way also establish sharpness of the phase transition for a general class of additive interacting particle systems.

title: Ranks of fibers in random elliptic surfaces
abstract: For random integer polynomials $P$ of arbitrary degree we prove that for $100\%$ of elliptic surfaces $y^2=x^3-P(t)^2x$ the average 2-Selmer rank of the fibers is 3. Consequently, for $100\%$ these random elliptic surfaces we establish a lower bound for the proportion of fibers attaining algebraic rank $0$ and $1$.

title: Smooth approximations to character sums and zeta sums
abstract: We study smooth approximations to Dirichlet character sums and zeta sums. The uniform upper-bound consequence of the Granville--Soundararajan conjecture, when imposed on all nonprincipal characters including imprimitive ones, implies the Riemann hypothesis for every primitive nonprincipal Dirichlet \(L\)-function. The proof uses characters induced to moduli divisible by all small primes. In the other direction, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,χ)\), we establish the conjectured approximation uniformly for \(q^a\le x\le q\), where \(0<a\le1\) is fixed, with \(y=(\log q+(\log x)^2)(\log\log q)^C\) for every fixed \(C>6\). In this range both the character sum and its smooth restriction, and hence their difference, are exponentially small relative to the number of \(y\)-smooth integers coprime to \(q\). We establish the corresponding approximation for \(\sum_{n\le x}n^{-it}\) under the Riemann hypothesis for the zeta function, uniformly for \(T^a\le x\le T\) and \(2T\le t\le5T\). We also show that the full zeta-sum smooth-approximation conjecture implies the Lindelöf hypothesis.

title: Hausdorff Dimension of Escaping Sets of Transcendental Entire Functions in the Speiser Class
abstract: For every $d\in[1,2]$, we construct a transcendental entire function $f$ whose finite singular value is contained in $\{-1,0,1\}$ and whose escaping set has Hausdorff dimension $d$. For $d<2$, the construction combines spiral corridors with quasiconformal folding. A narrowing Archimedean spiral gives dimension one, while a logarithmic spiral with adjustable width gives intermediate dimensions. The endpoint $d=2$ is realized by the exponential map. This gives an affirmative answer to a question of Bishop posed in 2018.

title: The topology of end-periodic smoothing operators
abstract: We develop an algebra of smoothing operators adapted to the geometry of end-periodic manifolds. We extend the renormalized trace and trace defect formula of Mrowka-Ruberman-Saveliev to this algebra, and establish a Fredholm criterion and winding-number index formula for smoothing perturbations of the identity. Our main result computes the homotopy groups of the associated end-periodic smoothing group. This provides a foundation for future work on relative index theory for families of end-periodic differential operators.
