For an acute contact angle and an arbitrary positive smooth prescribed function, we prove that a suitable initial dilation yields a global solution which converges smoothly after a horizontal translation with a uniquely determined constant velocity. As an application, we provide a logarithmic flow proof of the capillary Minkowski problem, previously established by Mei-Wang-Weng [Adv. Math. 469, 110230 (2025)].

title: Total variation error bounds for Schrödinger-Föllmer samplers
abstract: Sampling from high-dimensional, multimodal target distributions plays a fundamental role in scientific computing, statistics and machine learning. Recently, the Schrödinger-Föllmer sampler (SFS) has been proposed by Huang et al. (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, 2025) as an efficient sampling algorithm that transports the degenerate distribution at $t=0$ to the target distribution at $t=1$, without relying on long-time ergodicity. In this paper, we establish non-asymptotic error bounds for SFS in the total variation distance by deriving regularization estimates for the associated Kolmogorov equation via the Bismut-Elworthy-Li formula. When the drift can be computed exactly, a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|)$ was obtained under certain smoothness conditions on the drift with a uniform time step-size $h>0$. When the drift is approximated by Monte Carlo methods, we obtain a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|+ 1/M)$, where $M$ is the number of samples used in the Monte Carlo approximation. This yields a sharper dependence on $M$ than the existing bound $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{M})$ in the $L^2$-Wasserstein distance in the aforementioned paper, by turning the total variation error to the weak error analysis in the setting of non-smooth test functions. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the convergence rate with respect to the time step-size $h$ and the Monte Carlo sample size $M$ and the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: Lipschitz inner rates of normal surface singularities
abstract: In this article, we connect the local Lipschitz geometry of a normal surface singularity with a rational homology sphere link to the analytic semigroup $S_{an}(\tilde{X})$ associated with a convenient resolution. Under certain restriction, we provide an explicit computational characterization of the Lipschitz rate $q_v$ associated with an irreducible exceptional curve $E_v$ in terms of the semigroup. We also show that removing the restriction we get examples when $q_v$ cannot be determined from the semigroup. Interestingly enough, this phenomenon already happens for rational singularities. Indeed, we exemplify that the inner rates of rational singularities are not topological.

title: Completions of vector metric spaces and the diagonal property of order convergence
abstract: A vector metric space carries a distance with values in an ordered vector space $E$; a sequence converges if its distances to the limit are dominated by a sequence decreasing to zero in $E$. We show that, for Archimedean $E$, every $E$-valued vector metric space has a completion if and only if order Cauchy sequences in $E$ converge and $E$ has the diagonal property of order convergence (SDP): for every double sequence $(a^k_n)$ with $a^k_n\downarrow_n0$ there are indices $n_k$ and $e_k\downarrow 0$ with $a^k_{n_k}\le e_k$. In vector lattices this is the classical diagonal property of Kantorovich, equivalently the strong Egoroff property. We show that its standard characterisations remain valid in Archimedean ordered vector spaces, and that it holds if and only if convergence in every $E$-valued vector metric space satisfies the iterated limit axiom. For an ordered Banach space with a closed normal cone, all completions exist if and only if the norm is $σ$-order continuous; if the cone has an interior point, all vector metrics are then scalar. By a theorem of Veksler and of Hager and van Mill, for compact Hausdorff $K$ either $K$ is an almost $P$-space and $C(K)$-valued vector metrics are scalar, or there are countable $C(K)$-valued vector metric spaces without completion. A product of ordered vector spaces with (SDP) and nonzero cones has (SDP) if and only if there are fewer than $\mathfrak b$ factors, extending a result of Hager and van Mill for $\mathbb{R}^A$. We also prove permanence results for direct summands and uniformly dense vector lattice covers of pre-Riesz spaces.

title: Singular bifurcations in implicit discrete dynamical systems
abstract: A periodic orbit of an implicit discrete system can persist when the implicit function theorem no longer guarantees a smooth successor. We develop a joint Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction of the periodic equations and the determinants marking singular transitions. In unrestricted smooth one-parameter families, the generic event is a single evolution fold on a continued orbit. Simultaneous normal forms describe its interactions with saddle-node and period-doubling bifurcations, locating the singular transitions and, under backward regularity, determining the diverging multipliers. The results cover arbitrary periods and periodically non-autonomous systems. Exact realisations and applications to labour-market equilibrium, machining and implicit integration illustrate the theory.

title: Upper bounds on all-terminal reliability polynomials in terms of cycle basis lengths
abstract: Let $G=(V(G),E(G))$ be a connected multigraph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. The all-terminal reliability polynomial of $G$ can be written as $R_G(q)=(1-q)^{n-1}\sum\limits_{i=0}^{d}H_iq^i$ where $d=m-n+1$ is the cycle rank, each edge fails independently with probability $q\in[0,1]$, and $H_0,\ldots,H_d$ are the associated coefficients. A cycle basis, which consists of cycles that form a basis of the cycle space of a graph, is an important tool for characterizing its cycle structure. The structural properties of cycle bases, together with the associated length optimization problems and construction algorithms, have been extensively studied. In this context, Colbourn posed the following open problem, which concerns upper bounds on the reliability coefficients in terms of cycle-basis lengths: For all-terminal reliability, is it true that if $G$ has a cycle basis containing cycles of lengths $c_1,\ldots,\allowbreak c_{m-n+1}$, then $H_i \le\sum\limits_{\substack{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m-n+1\},|I|=i}}\prod\limits_{j\in I}(c_j-1)$? In this paper, we establish a result that resolves this open problem.

title: Rigidity does not imply substitution rigidity
abstract: We obtain a negative answer to a question of Freudenburg concerning rigidity conditions for a polynomial. We construct a polynomial that does not lie in the kernel of any nonzero locally nilpotent derivation on the polynomial ring, but there exist an affine domain, algebraically independent elements and a locally nilpotent derivation such that the result of substituting elements into the polynomial lies in the kernel of that locally nilpotent derivation, but at least one of the substituted elements does not lie in that kernel.

title: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
abstract: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$. They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for fine meshes with at least 512 elements has a proof checked by Lean 4. Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.

title: Investigating parameter dependence for counterexamples to Payne's nodal line conjecture using HPC
abstract: The behavior of the nodal line of the second eigenfunction of the negative Laplacian has been widely studied. Dahne could show numerically for one domain with six holes in two dimensions that it is possible to reject Payne's nodal line conjecture. We investigate the behavior of the nodal line if it does not touch the boundary, specifically the general shape, its prediction, its dependence on the parameters, and the numbers of holes. In this paper, we could address these issues numerically with a very efficient parallelized algorithm showing the rejection for various domains with six and five holes.

title: On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
abstract: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.

title: On the Abels--Garcke--Grün Model for Incompressible Two-Phase Flows with Unmatched Densities: Phase Separation and Rayleigh--Taylor Instability
abstract: Instability phenomena are ubiquitous in multi-fluid flows. For binary fluid mixtures, phase separation may occur under specific conditions, in which a homogeneous state becomes unstable and spontaneously segregates into different phases, leading to the formation of distinct patterns. Furthermore, when a heavier fluid is superposed over a lighter one in a gravitational field, the fluid interface can be sensitive to perturbations that trigger the Rayleigh--Taylor (RT) instability, i.e., the lighter fluid penetrates upward into the heavier fluid against gravity. We investigate such instability phenomena and the inhibiting conditions for incompressible, immiscible two-phase flows with unmatched densities, within the framework of a diffuse-interface model, which is called the Abels--Garcke--Grün (AGG) model. More precisely, we adopt energy methods to establish several stability/instability conditions for the perturbed system of the AGG model, which is obtained by slightly perturbing the equilibrium profile $(\mathbf{0},\overline{\varphi})$, where $\overline{\varphi}=\overline{\varphi}(x_3)$ depends solely on the vertical coordinate $x_3$. Notably, for a constant equilibrium profile $\overline{\varphi}=α\in(-1,1)$ satisfying $Ψ''(α)<0$, we establish a threshold for stability and instability of the phase-separation problem.Similar stability results are also established for the perturbed system with $\overline{\varphi}$ satisfying the RT instability condition in the presence of gravity. In particular, if the phase-separation condition fails and $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$ is a constant, a larger value of $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$, a greater interfacial thickness and a higher surface energy density contribute to inhibiting RT instability.

title: Large deviations, optimal trajectories and conservation of momenta in generalised Jackson networks
abstract:
We study properties of optimal trajectories for
  the quasipotential that governs large deviations of queue lengths in generalised Jackson networks (GJN). The trajectories are shown to satisfy Hamilton equations. The Hamiltonian is identified. Optimal trajectories and associated costs are found for networks with two and three stations. A conservation law for adjoint variables
  is discovered to the effect that certain components are maintained along an optimal trajectory. A process is proposed for finding optimal trajectories and computing their costs
  in general GJN.

title: Translation continuity for the local bilinear circular maximal operator
abstract: We prove a positive power translation-continuity estimate for the local bilinear circular maximal operator on the real line. More precisely, there is $η>0$ such that the operator applied to a translation difference in either input maps $L^8(\mathbb{R})\times L^8(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^4(\mathbb{R})$ with norm $O(|h|^η)$. This answers Question 6.3 in Borges's survey on bilinear spherical averages. The main step is a frequency-localized estimate for arbitrary bounded inputs. A $TT^*$ argument converts it into a linear maximal problem on the plane, associated with pairs of circles. We verify the corrected multi-parameter cinematic curvature condition of Chen, Guo, and Yang by proving an irreducibility and infinitesimal independence statement for the resulting quartic curves. Uniform algebraic sublevel estimates control the degeneracies. Interpolation also gives continuity for all finite exponents $2<p,q<\infty$, with output exponent $pq/(p+q)$.

title: Fundamental Outage and Diversity Limits of Fluid Antenna Multiple Access Under Correlated Nakagami-$m$ Fading
abstract:
Existing analytical studies of fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA) are largely confined to Rayleigh fading, independent-port assumptions, or asymptotic selection metrics, leaving the fundamental outage behavior under realistic fading and spatial correlation conditions uncharacterized.
  This paper fills this gap by presenting the first exact and asymptotically tight outage analysis of interference-limited FAMA systems under spatially correlated Nakagami-$m$ fading. By explicitly modeling the joint statistics of the desired and interference powers across fluid-antenna ports, \textcolor{black}{we first formulate the outage probability in terms of the joint
  desired-signal and interference distributions and then derive an explicit
  integral expression under a tractable single-reference-port spatial
  correlation model.} Building on this result, we establish a rigorous diversity-order characterization
  revealing that the achievable diversity is jointly dictated by the fading severity and the spatial correlation rank imposed by the finite antenna aperture, rather than by the nominal number of ports. 
  To enable accurate and tractable performance evaluation beyond the asymptotic regime, we further introduce a Gamma-matched outage approximation that preserves both the exact diversity order and the array-gain constant. The resulting closed-form expression provides an accurate characterization over a wide range of signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) thresholds and offers clear physical insight into the role of spatial correlation in FAMA systems. Extensive Monte Carlo (MC) simulations confirm the tightness of the exact analysis, the sharpness of the asymptotic results, and the accuracy of the proposed approximation.

title: Completely monotone memory systems
abstract: Linear time-invariant (LTI) relaxation systems are characterized by a completely monotone impulse response. This paper proposes an extension of this property to nonlinear systems: a system is said to have completely monotone memory if a positive increment in the past input leads to a completely monotone increment in the future output. We show that this property constitutes a strong form of monotonicity, while also imposing stability constraints that closely resemble fading memory, contraction, and incremental stability. We also show that completely monotone memory is equivalent to classical relaxation for LTI systems and to a combination of monotonicity and stability for a class of scalar state-affine systems. Finally, we illustrate the relevance of our framework to the gating dynamics of conductance-based models.

title: A Strict Upper Bound for Three-Point Weighted Selection in Planar Vector-Valued Regression
abstract: We prove $F_{\mathrm{weighted}}(2,2,3)<11/6$ for minimum-Frobenius-norm least-squares regression with two input and two output coordinates, improving the upper bound $15/8$. More precisely, a universal $\varepsilon_0>0$ satisfies $\mathcal T_3\le(5/6-\varepsilon_0)E$ for every finite residual frame. The proof combines an exact scalar certificate, rigidity of equality in planar selection, and a compactness argument that controls disappearing weights. Together with the known lower bound, this gives $13/8\le F_{\mathrm{weighted}}(2,2,3)<11/6$. No numerical value of $\varepsilon_0$ is claimed.

title: Ternary quadratic genera and generalized Hurwitz class numbers via quaternion orders
abstract: We classify the genera of primitive positive definite ternary quadratic forms in the extremal cases of Lehman's level and discriminant conditions. The genera are parametrized by their level, discriminant, and genus conductor, which also distinguishes local forms having the same isotropy. Using the correspondence with quaternion orders of level $(N_1,N_2)$, we express their weighted representation numbers and class numbers in terms of generalized modified Hurwitz class numbers. The formulas allow arbitrary admissible prime power exponents and include the additional genera obtained by Watson's transformation. As an application, we determine all $255$ one-class genera in these families and give an explicit representation formula for each. Of these formulas, $110$ concern nonsquarefree $N_1N_2$.

title: Non-connected minimal clusters of small volume in a compact Finsler manifold
abstract: We prove that isoperimetric clusters in general Finsler manifolds can be disconnected even when the volume constraint is small. This is in contrast with the Riemannian case and the ``fixed-norm'' case, where connectedness for arbitrarily small volume has recently been proved.

title: Horizontal estimates for Kloosterman sums under Hecke eigenvalue constraints
abstract: We prove weighted cancellation under small-value conditions on Hecke eigenvalues of finitely many non-CM holomorphic newforms. We also obtain many squarefree integers of each sign with fixed normalized amplitude, simultaneously small Hecke eigenvalues, and a fixed bound on the number of prime factors, uniformly in growing reduced residue classes. Our questions are motivated by Xi's noncorrelation conjectures and the mixed-moment estimates of Jiang and Lau. Their estimates imply that small Hecke eigenvalues can occur together with non-small Kloosterman values. Our result retains this property with a fixed prime-factor bound, both signs, and the residue conditions. Using OpenAI's zero-free half-plane theorem for Dirichlet $L$-functions, we give an example with at most $83$ prime factors, normalized amplitude at least $10^{-21}$, and moduli $M\le C^{11/200}$.

title: Fixed-occurrence cases of the shuffle-word-embedding conjecture
abstract: For self-adjoint contractions in a finite tracial von Neumann algebra, binary shuffle traces with $m=1,2,4$ occurrences of the second variable admit simultaneous finite-dimensional approximation by commuting diagonal contractions. For every odd $m$, a commuting diagonal self-adjoint pair reproduces any prescribed finite set of shuffle traces exactly. When the first operator has finite spectrum and $m\geq3$ is odd, a weighted symmetric cycle reproduces all degrees simultaneously. We prove fourth-order trace-derivative positivity in finite tracial von Neumann algebras and obtain a positive measure representing the four-occurrence coefficients. For each even $m$, we characterize the contraction model property by positivity of an associated trace-derivative functional.

title: The full length of short pants
abstract: Bers proved that any genus $g$ hyperbolic surface admits a pants decomposition of length bounded above by a function of its genus. The goal here is to provide an explicit upper bound for the sums of lengths which is on the order of $(g \log(g)) ^{3/2}$.

title: VEM-bubble discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for a fluid induced seismicity model with rate-and-state friction
abstract: This work addresses the discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for an induced seismicity model accounting for fault reactivation and slip driven by subsurface fluid injection. The model couples single-phase Darcy flow in both the porous matrix and the fault network with a quasi-static poroelastic mechanical response in the bulk and fault slip governed by a rate-and-state friction law with radiation damping stabilisation leading to a quas-dynamic formulation. The contact mechanics problem is discretised using the Virtual Element Method with bubble stabilisation of the facewise constant Lagrange multiplier. It is combined with a Hybrid Finite Volume scheme for the mixed-dimensional Darcy flow model. The time discretisation is implicit and the nonlinear system is solved at each time step using an iterative coupling algorithm which iterates between the Darcy flow, the frictional contact-mechanics, and the state differential equation. The contraction of this iterative coupling algorithm is established with a smallness assumption on the time step independent on the mesh size. This proves convergence of the fixed-point as well as well-posedness of the system. The frictional contact-mechanical model is solved using a semi-smooth Newton algorithm based on a local nonlinear inversion of the friction rate-and-state law and a block Gauss--Seidel preconditioner exploiting the structure of the VEM-bubble-$\mathbb{P}^0$ mixed discretisation.

title: Unique continuation property for $\bar\partial$ with $L^{2n}$ potentials
abstract:
We establish the sharp unique continuation property for the Cauchy--Riemann operator $\bar{\partial}$ in higher dimensions. Let $0\inΩ\subset \C^n$ be a domain. Suppose $u \in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}(Ω; \C^N)$ satisfies the differential inequality
  \[
  |\bar{\partial} u| \leq V |u| \quad \text{a.e.~on } Ω
  \]
  with $V \in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2n}(Ω)$. If $u$ is $L^2$ flat at the origin, then $u \equiv 0$ on $Ω$.

title: Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
abstract: The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $ζ(s)$ and its derivative $ζ'(s)$ are deeply intertwined: the horizontal distribution of $ζ'$-zeros near the critical line encodes information about the spacing of consecutive $ζ$-zeros. This paper establishes some results concerning the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

title: Derivations tangent to polar discriminants
abstract: We describe the module of logarithmic derivations along the discriminant of a stable polar representation of a reductive algebraic group. It splits into derivations along the fibres of the quotient map and a free summand lifted from logarithmic derivations along the associated branch divisor. This gives a uniform extension of previous results on full adjoint discriminants. We prove that, for visible stable polar actions of semisimple groups with finite generic stabilizer, the discriminant is a free divisor. For stable periodic gradings of arbitrary order with semisimple degree-zero group, we construct explicit Saito matrices from the infinitesimal action and the gradients of basic invariants, which yields determinantal equations for several exceptional discriminants. In particular, starting with exceptional Lie algebras, we provide examples of free discriminants of degrees 60, 120, 126 and 240 for inner gradings and a degree-72 example for an outer one.

title: Linear disjointness and values of Mahler M-functions
abstract: We prove that the algebra generated by the values of Mahler M-functions at algebraic points admits a decomposition as the tensor product, over Q, of a countable family of linearly disjoint algebras. Consequently, the study of linear and algebraic relations among such values reduces to the corresponding problem within each of these smaller algebras. Our proof relies on recent advances of the authors on Mahler's method in several variables. As an application, we obtain a complete description of the algebraic relations among the values of the Fredholm series and their derivatives at nonzero algebraic points. This fully resolves an old problem originating in Mahler's work.

title: Gorenstein modules over Thompson's group
abstract: Let $k$ be any commutative ring of characteristic $0$. We construct an example of a countably presented Gorenstein projective module over the algebra of Thompson's group $F$ with coefficients in $k$, that is not Benson cofibrant. In particular, we provide a negative answer to a conjecture proposed by Dembegioti and Talelli. The construction uses a general method that produces totally acyclic complexes of flat modules and is based on the computation of the (co-)cohomology of $F$ by Brown and Geoghegan.

title: Cylindricity of log del Pezzo surfaces in characteristic five
abstract: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic five, we prove that a log del Pezzo surface of Picard rank one contains no cylinder if it is not log liftable. We also characterize Du Val del Pezzo surfaces that contain no cylinder in positive characteristic.

title: Piercing a Chessboard with Restricted Slopes
abstract: Is it true that for $n\geq 3$, $n-1$ lines are needed to pierce every cell of an $n\times n$ board? This problem was independently rediscovered several times: Alkauskas (1998), Harel-Ackerman-Pinchasi (2012, without claiming the $n-1$ bound), Bárány-Frankl (2021). However, apparently the first to pose it was T. Keller (Honolulu, Hawaii), in 1980, in the problem section of The American Mathematical Monthly. In this note, we give an affirmative answer to Keller's problem when all lines have slopes in $(-\infty,-1]\cup(0,1]$.

title: Lower intermediate dimensions of classical Denjoy minimal sets
abstract: We study the $θ$-intermediate dimension of the minimal set of the classical $C^{1+δ}$ Denjoy map, an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle not conjugate to a rigid rotation. This follows on from work of Kra and Schmeling, who showed how the box and Hausdorff dimensions may differ, depending on the Diophantine properties of the rotation number. The $θ$-intermediate dimension interpolates between these two dimensions. We use the well-understood gap structure of the irrational rotation map to develop a covering strategy to get upper bounds on the lower $θ$-intermediate dimension, and use results of Banaji to show that these upper bounds are sharp for $θ$ in an interval.

title: Monetisation and Cost Function Scalarisation Cannot Guarantee Valid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making
abstract:
Monetary quantities are not preferences. Cost is an object-related system performance; value-for-money is an actor's subjective evaluation of it. Monetisation embeds trade-off information: its conversion coefficients express valuations and determine how heterogeneous performances compensate one another. Cost-benefit analysis, even net present value, yields quantities of money, not the preference value actors attribute to them.
  This creates a monetisation paradox. Cost enters a multi-criteria problem as one performance among several, but money is then elevated into the universal representation of all others, creating representational dominance. The problem collapses into a single-criterion one in which every performance acts only through its imposed monetary equivalent. Cost-function scalarisation does not resolve this by substituting points, normalised scores, losses, or penalties: these transformations and their weights fix preference directions, intensities, and trade-offs, so they are implicit preference models, yet are treated as technical constructs rather than measured and validated.
  A well-defined scalar optimum is therefore not necessarily a decision-valid multi-criteria outcome. Numerical commensurability does not establish preference commensurability. Decision validity requires heterogeneous performances to be transformed into actor preferences in a unified preference domain. Preference is relational and contextual, yet can be represented on an affine scale. Preference Function Modelling and the Linear Preference Space provide the commensurability required for valid aggregation. The decision criterion should thus maximise aggregated actor preference over the feasible and acceptable design-decision space, not monetised quantities or scalarised scores.

title: Global-dimension spectra of gentle algebras
abstract:
We classify the connected finite-dimensional gentle algebras of finite global dimension whose global-dimension spectra under derived equivalence are not intervals of integers. These are precisely the algebras with AAG invariant $[(2,4g)]$, where $g\geq2$, whose canonical line field is induced by a nowhere-vanishing vector field. Their spectrum is $\{2g,2g+2,\ldots,4g\}$. For each $g\geq2$, there are exactly two such derived-equivalence classes, distinguished by their Arf invariant.
  The geometric foundation is a realisation theorem for prescribed polygon weights in arbitrary genus. For an AAG invariant $[(m_i,n_i)]_{i=1}^b$ arising from such an algebra, the global dimensions attained in its AAG fibre form the integer interval $[\max_i\lceil n_i/m_i\rceil,\max_i n_i]$. By controlling the complete line-field invariant through local ribbon-graph constructions, we determine the spectrum in every derived-equivalence class.

title: Generation of semigroups for vector-valued pseudodifferential operators on the torus with space-dependent symbols
abstract: We consider toroidal pseudodifferential operators with spatially dependent, operator-valued symbols of positive order and finite regularity. For an arbitrary complex Banach space $E$, we prove that the negative of the closure of a parabolic operator on $C^\infty(\mathbb T^n,E)$ generates an analytic semigroup on $W_p^k(\mathbb T^n,E)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $k\in\mathbb N_0$, provided the symbol has sufficiently many spatial derivatives and discrete differences. The proof combines uniform estimates for parameter-dependent kernels with right and left parametrices. It does not require the UMD property of $E$. Real interpolation gives corresponding resolvent estimates on $B_{pq}^s(\mathbb T^n,E)$ for $0<s<k$ and $1\le q\le\infty$. The induced semigroups are strongly continuous for $q<\infty$ and on the little Besov spaces when $q=\infty$.

title: Asymptotic spreading of Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments with time-periodic limits
abstract: In this paper, we study the rightward spreading speed of solutions for Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments. The linear growth rate has time periodic limits at the two ends of the moving frame. Each limit has a positive average and may be negative during a period. When the growth rate lies between the two limits at each time, we show that the spreading speed depends only on their averages and the asymptotic shift speed. For intermediate shift speeds, the formulas give nonlocal pulling if the right end has the larger average and speed locking if the left end has the larger average. The interior growth profile may be nonmonotone in space and aperiodic in time. We prove the formulas by constructing upper and lower solutions for a stepwise profile and then comparing with shifted stepwise problems.

title: Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator
abstract: We study the subellipticity of the analytically deformed Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and give two definitions of resonances, one based on analytic dilation and the other on analytic distortion in the $x$-variables. Due to the failure of global subellipticity of the distorted operator in dimensions $n \geq 2$, the second method can only be used in dimension one. We show that, whenever both methods are applicable, they give rise to the same set of resonances. We also prove that, when $|\na V(x)| = O(\w x^{-ρ})$ with $ρ>1$, positive resonances are embedded eigenvalues and/or scattering resonances whose resonant states belong to weighted $L^2$-spaces and satisfy an outgoing radiation condition.

title: Asymptotics of matrix orthogonal polynomials with non-scalar varying weights
abstract: We study the $2\times 2$ matrix orthogonal polynomials $\mathbf{P}_N$ on the real line with respect to the varying weights $\mathrm{e}^{-N\mathbf{Q}(z)}\mathbf{B}(z)$, where $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are real symmetric matrix polynomials that commute with a Hermite-type matrix weight, $\mathbf{Q}$ is not scalar and $\mathbf{B}$ is positive definite. We are motivated by the non-Abelian Toda deformation of the Hermite-type weight, in the sense of Deaño, Morey and Román. The weight depends on $N$ through a matrix exponential that is not scalar, so that its two eigenvalues have different exponential rates. The matrix orthogonality reduces to two scalar orthogonality problems on the real line, with a varying weight that has an essential singularity at the origin. Assuming that the associated equilibrium measure is one-cut regular, we obtain the strong asymptotics of $\mathbf{P}_N$ and of $\det\mathbf{P}_N$ by the Deift-Zhou steepest descent method. Our main result is the limiting zero distribution of the entries of $\mathbf{P}_N$. These zeros are complex in general, and they accumulate on a curve where the contributions of the two eigenvalues of the weight have the same size. When this curve crosses the real segment that attracts the zeros of $\det\mathbf{P}_N$, the zeros of the entries display a critical behavior, and a positive fraction of them accumulates on this segment.

title: Real quadratic fields and finite quantum dilogarithms II: traces of quantum modular cocycles
abstract: We study traces of quantum modular cocycles at fixed points of hyperbolic elements $γ\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, formulate an algebraicity conjecture for these traces, and prove it for the cocycles associated to 1-dimensional state-integrals. In addition, we analyse a finite TQFT associated with $γ$ and conjecture that its invariants for 3-manifolds agree with the traces of their $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ quantum modular cocycles. The finite TQFTs predict a yet-to-be-defined motive with cohomology equipped with a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-degree grading and a $\mathbb{Z}$-weight grading coming from a version of the Riemann hypothesis, which suggests a similar grading should exist for an extension of the Kauffman bracket skein module, for the framed $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Floer cohomology of Abouzaid--Manolescu, and for the quantum modular cocycle. This leads to surprising additive identities among algebraic units, which we confirm for the complement of the simplest hyperbolic knot $4_1$, as well as for $S^1 \times Σ_g$ for a closed genus $g$ surface.

title: Certified finite-precision readout for $p$-adic kernel aggregation
abstract: In non-archimedean numerical analysis, a verified $p$-adic approximation can determine an absolute value, and hence downstream probabilistic rankings and classification decisions, with mathematical exactness long before the underlying number is fully resolved. We turn this observation into rigorous finite-precision certificates for norm-based readouts of amplitude families. For a common error radius, a nonempty resolved set already fixes every exact maximizer, ties included, at the sharp integer absolute precision $v_*+1$, and conditioning on that set yields an exact total-variation identity separating unresolved $p$-adic mass from real rounding error. For aggregates of $p$-adic exponentials, we give a centered-moment certificate with an explicit remainder bound: on rational data it runs in exact rational arithmetic without individual exponential evaluations, attains its minimal bound at an active phase, and resolves every nonzero aggregate at high order; we also obtain an aggregate perturbation bound free of summand-count factors. For multiclass $p$-adic classifiers that decode by minimizing the norm of a class discriminant, we prove a necessary and sufficient certification condition and show that the sharp common precision threshold is $v^{(2)}+1$, governed by the second-largest discriminant valuation, so the winning discriminant need not itself be resolved. We apply these certificates to discrete $p$-adic path-integral actions on uniform affine chains, deriving explicit action centers and proving exact output-independence at zero effective quadratic coupling. Pseudocode and a reproducible reference implementation accompany the theory.

title: Single-point determination of a potential and a nonlinearity in a semilinear biharmonic equation
abstract: In this paper, we study the inverse problem of determining the coefficient $q$ and the nonlinearity $F$ in the semilinear biharmonic equation $Δ^2 u+q(x)u=F(x,u)$ with Navier boundary data. The measurement consists of $\partial_νu(x_0)$ at a fixed boundary point $x_0$. We apply the mixed variation approach to linearize the nonlinear problem and construct semiclassical boundary-localized solutions for the linearized equation. Under suitable analyticity, nonresonance, and nondegeneracy assumptions on $q$ and $F$, we prove that this boundary point measurement uniquely determines both $q$ and $F$. We also establish boundary determination of all normal derivatives of $q$ and of the first nonzero Taylor coefficient of $F$ on a nonempty relatively open subset of the boundary. When the linear potential $q$ is known, we prove that either component of the Navier boundary input alone suffices to determine $F$, and that the polynomial nonlinearity can be uniquely determined without requiring any analyticity conditions. For suitable finite-dimensional classes of nonanalytic potentials, we also obtain, for fixed $F$, the stable determination of $q$ from finitely many boundary inputs and the associated point measurements. In addition, as an important supplement, we provide nontrivial examples verifying the main assumptions, as well as counterexamples concerning the recovery of the linear coefficient. Finally, we present numerical experiments that demonstrate the theoretical results.

title: Exponential mixing for the randomized two-vortex model
abstract: This paper investigates the mixing of passive scalars advected by a randomized two-vortex model on $\mathbb{T}^2$, in which the vortices interact through a regularized Biot--Savart kernel and are driven by independent Brownian motions. We establish quenched exponential mixing for the Lagrangian flow, characterized by the exponential correlation decay of mean-zero $H^s$ observables. The proof proceeds by establishing ergodicity of the associated two-point Markov process. We combine a uniform contraction estimate with controllability arguments to verify the Lyapunov drift and minorization conditions, allowing us to apply Harris-type theorem.

title: Rationally Null-homologous Floer Simple Knot
abstract: We prove that every rationally null-homologous Floer simple knot in a closed, oriented, irreducible three-manifold with nonzero Thurston norm is unknotted. The proof combines a cut-and-reglue comparison for extremal Floer groups with Binns's theorem on Floer-minimal knots in balanced sutured manifolds.

title: The space of Dimension functions on a $C^*$-algebra
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the space of normalized dimension functions on a unital $C^*$-algebra is either empty or a Choquet simplex. As a byproduct, we show that $W(A)$ is hereditary in $\operatorname{Cu}(A)$ for every $C^*$-algebra $A$. The argument combines an exact factorization for Cuntz comparison with Birkhoff's decomposition of lattice valuations. Moreover, we show that the space of normalized rank functions on a unital ring is either empty or a Choquet simplex.

title: Linear Functional Estimation under Multiplicative Measurement Error with Unknown Error Distribution
abstract: In this work we consider i.i.d. observations from a multiplicative deconvolution model, i.e. generated by $Y= X\varepsilon$, where $X$ and $\varepsilon$ are independent strictly positive random variables. The goal is to statistically infer the unknown signal $X$. Starting from the scenario where the probability density $f_\varepsilon$ of the error is known, we revisit local estimation strategies for several quantities of interest including the probability density function f and the survival function $S^X$ of the signal $X$. We use these results to propose a thresholded plug-in estimation technique for linear functionals in situations where the distribution of the error $\varepsilon$ is unknown, while having some additional data at our disposal. This estimation procedure combines the reconstruction of the unknown Mellin transform of $f$ as well as its regularized inversion by a spectral cut-off. We establish oracle-type upper bounds and discuss rates of convergence in explicit scenarios including estimating $f$ and $S^X$ pointwise. In addition, we develop a fully data-driven choice of the cut-off parameter via model selection, which is able to obtain the oracle risk up to a constant without any previous knowledge of the error distribution. The results are illustrated in a simulation experiment, where we compare different classes of distributions in settings with known and unknown $f_\varepsilon$.

title: An approximation for solutions to Helmholtz equation in polygons and its application in learning based numerical method
abstract: A learning based method for Helmholtz equations was proposed in [J. Comput. Phys. 520:113478,2025]. Based on Runge's approximation, it can be proved that when the solution can be continued outside the computational domain, using fundamental solutions as learning samples is sufficient to obtain the solution mapping with spectral accuracy. However, for complex geometries, such as domains with corners, approximation by fundamental solutions may only have logarithmic convergence due to the regularity issue, which is computationally impracticable. Moreover, approximation of a solution to the elliptic equation with those on larger domains is an ill-posed problem. In this work, we investigate how to feed additional learning samples to essentially get a practicable convergence rate and a stable algorithm, so as to ensure the generalizability of the learning based method. Error analysis and numerical examples illustrate flexibility and high-accuracy features.

title: On definable closure in closed $H$-fields
abstract: The definable closure of a real closed $H$-field $H$ in an ambient closed $H$-field extension $M$ is shown to be an immediate extension of $H$, except in two very special cases, where this is only true after adjunction to $H$ of a particular $H$-definable element of $M$ and then taking the real closure in $M$.

title: An almost sharp tomas-stein restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
abstract: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} for each $1\leq p\leq 2$, whenever $(\frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}-\frac{1}{m_{j}}+1)\frac{2}{p^{\prime}}\geq 1$, for every $j\in Γ$, and \begin{equation*} \mathcal{E}:=\min{\left\{\min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}> \frac{2}{p^{\prime}}. \end{equation*} We also give counterexamples that show that the condition $\mathcal{E}\geq 2/p^{\prime}$ is necessary for this restriction inequality.

title: Branch Obstructions for Area-Minimizing Currents and Flat Critical Points of Weakly-Conformal Maps
abstract:
We study two problems motivated by the local geometry of conformal $φ$-curves. First, let $T$ be a $k$-dimensional locally area-minimizing integral current in Euclidean space, with $k\geq3$, codimension at least two, no boundary, and a locally conformally flat induced metric on $\operatorname{reg} T$. We prove the following branch obstruction: at any rapid-decay branch point whose planar frequency differs from $2$, every nonzero cyclic component of every cylindrical normalized tangent function has repetition multiplicity at least two. Consequently, the nonintegral-frequency points of densities $2$ and $3$ in the rapid-decay branch set have Hausdorff dimension at most $k-3$. On the full branch set, they have zero $\mathcal H^{k-2}$ measure. These conclusions apply to Euclidean image currents of conformal $φ$-curves with locally conformally flat domains, provided the image currents satisfy the stated hypotheses.
  Second, for $C^j$ weakly-conformal maps between smooth Riemannian manifolds, with domain dimension $k\geq3$ and $j\geq2$, we prove that all derivatives of orders $1$ through $j$ vanish at every critical point. As a consequence, for smooth weakly-conformal maps with connected domain, we establish a curvature condition under which the map is constant or has no critical points. The flatness and continuation results apply in particular to conformal $φ$-curves with the corresponding regularity and curvature assumptions. Finally, we examine the Borůvka cone, which illustrates the role of regularity and the distinction between critical points and branch points.

title: The symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric problem in the plane
abstract: We resolve the symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric conjecture in the plane: every minimizer of Gaussian perimeter among centrally symmetric sets of prescribed Gaussian measure is a centered ball, a symmetric strip, or the complement of one of these sets. A quadrant-reflection argument reduces the problem to unconditional sets. The planar structural results of Barchiesi, Cagnetti and Julin then leave only a noncircular strictly convex stationary oval. We exclude this oval by an explicit volume-preserving and perimeter-decreasing linear deformation, which geometrically corresponds to an "unconditional squeezing". More generally, without requiring any symmetry assumptions, we show that any noncircular closed embedded $λ$-self-shrinker is always unstable via linear deformations. We also record a reduction to the unconditional case in dimension three, using an orthogonal equipartition theorem of Musin.

title: $λ_g$-Integrals on triple, one-part admissible covers
abstract: We effectively compute all intersection numbers of the form $λ_gψ^d$ on moduli spaces of genus $g$ admissible covers with one point of full ramification and two additional branch points with arbitrary profile. We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.

title: Positive solutions of power equations in planar corner domains
abstract: We study positive solutions of $Δu=λu^k$ on bounded planar corner domains with zero boundary values away from the vertex. For negative-power absorption we identify the admissible interval of Martin masses and prove uniqueness at the minimum mass. Along the ordinary boundary, we identify the weak Hessian endpoint and its sharp tail when the set of zero inward derivative has positive length. For superlinear sources we prove attainment of the largest positive Martin mass in the subcritical range. At criticality we construct a family of singular solutions with zero Martin mass and distinguish its members by their second logarithmic coefficient and the endpoint integrability of their Hessian differences. Above criticality an angular eigenvalue governs the Morse index away from its zero threshold. We also give sharp physical-Hessian asymptotics for finite-mass remainders and joint corner and side estimates for negative-power sources.

title: Orbits along primes in totally minimal systems
abstract: In this paper, we show that every totally minimal system admits a point whose orbit along the primes is dense. Moreover, assuming the Dickson-Hardy-Littlewood conjecture, we show that in any totally minimal distal system, the orbit along the primes of every point is dense.

title: Reconstructing Flash-Evoked Potentials in the Human Brain and Tracking Cortical Activity Using Spatiotemporal Filtering: Numerical Simulation Study
abstract: Electroencephalographic source reconstruction of visual evoked activity is challenging because distributed, temporally evolving, and overlapping cortical sources generate scalp potentials. We present a controlled simulation framework for flash visual evoked potentials (FVEPs) based on a coupled Jansen--Rit neural mass network and a realistic finite-element EEG forward model. The framework generates a sequential activation pattern across early visual, parietal, and frontal regions and enables direct comparison of reconstructed activity with known ground truth. Standardized Kalman filtering (SKF), change-rate SKF (CrSKF), conventional Kalman filtering (KF), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV) beamforming are compared using parcel-wise time courses, temporal lags, and assessments of spatial focality and Earth Mover's Distance. In the inverse comparison, SKF and CrSKF preserve the principal temporal progression more consistently than KF and LCMV, while CrSKF produces smoother temporal estimates. The results also demonstrate parcel-wise leakage and reduced separation of closely spaced components, emphasizing the need to interpret temporal ordering together with spatial reconstruction quality. The proposed framework provides a reproducible test environment for evaluating dynamic EEG inverse methods under controlled noise conditions.

title: Induced packing treewidth III. Branch decompositions
abstract:
The notion of induced packing treewidth aims to unify classes defined by forbidden induced subgraphs or induced minors with classes defined by the existence of certain structured tree decompositions.
  In this paper, we introduce induced packing branchwidth, a branch-decomposition analogue of induced packing treewidth. For a graph $H$, the induced $H$-packing branchwidth of a graph $G$, denoted by $\branchpi_H(G)$, is the minimum, over all branch decompositions of $G$, of the largest number of pairwise anticomplete induced copies of $H$ that cross one displayed cut. For $H=P_2$, it equals sim-width. We prove several structural properties of graphs of bounded $\branchpi_H$, for various choices of $H$, including $χ$-boundedness, polynomial degree-boundedness, and metric properties.

title: Edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles in the McKay--Miller--Širáň graphs $H_q$ for every prime power $q\geq 3$
abstract: Motivated by Hamilton cycle problems and applications to collective communication, we study edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles in the McKay--Miller--Širáň (MMS) graphs. The MMS graph $H_q$ (indexed by a prime power $q$) is a highly symmetric graph arising from finite fields. For every prime power $q\geq 3$, we prove that the MMS graph $H_q$ contains $\big\lceil\frac{q-1}{2}\big\rceil$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles. This resolves a problem of Li, Wang and Zheng, who established the result for prime $q$ and for $q=4$. Our construction uses graph lifts over finite fields and joins the components of lifted Hamilton cycles by adding edges within vertex fibres. The resulting cycles can be constructed using $O(|E(H_q)|)$ finite field operations, comparisons, and elementary list operations. As an application, these cycles provide edge-disjoint spanning rings for parallel ring-all-reduce algorithms on MMS networks.

title: A Silverman-Meadows-type criterion for the null controllability of time-dependent coupled heat equations with non-diagonalizable diffusion matrices
abstract: This paper is devoted to a uniform spectral Silverman-Meadows rank condition for the nullcontrollability of coupled systems of heat equations with time-dependent diffusion, coupling and control matrices. The proof relies on an adaptation of the Lebeau-Robbiano strategy combined with uniform finite-dimensional observability estimates associated with each Laplace eigenmode.

title: On the entire solutions of Schröder iteration functions of first and second kind
abstract: Let $S_{f,n}$ and $K_{f,n}$ denote Schröder's methods of the first and second kind with given order $ n $ ($\geq 2 $) applied to an entire function $ f $. This article investigates the existence of the entire solutions $f$ whenever $ S_{f,n} $ and $ K_{f,n} $ are rational. Utilizing the Nevanlinna theory, we obtain the general form of entire solutions for such equations. It is proved that either of $ S_{f,n} $ and $ K_{f,n} $ is a non-identity rational map if and only if $f = p e^{q}$, for some polynomials $p$ and $q$. Additionally, we provide one recurrence relation of $K_{f,n}$ depending only upon $K_{f,n-1}$.

title: Interface-Preserving ${H}_\infty$ Model Reduction of Network Systems
abstract: We study projection-based reduced-order models that exactly retain specified input and output interfaces. Admissible projections are characterized geometrically: the retained subspace must contain every input and output direction, which fixes the minimum order. The reduction error factors into input-coupling, internal-dynamics, and output-coupling systems, giving a submultiplicative ${H}_\infty$ bound; for positively dominated factors the ${H}_\infty$ error equals a dc gain computable from linear solves. Strict dissipativity certifies the stability of every orthogonal reduction, and a Hankel singular value bounds the optimum a posteriori. These results motivate sequential graph-coarsening heuristics for networks. On a 65,566-state chip thermal network, interface-preserving coarsening yields sparse, positive lumped models that are more accurate than Kron reduction of the same interface at every order, with far fewer edges; balanced truncation is more accurate but destroys the network structure.

title: Odd realisation numbers of rigid graphs
abstract: Determining the number of realisations of a rigid graph for a specific choice of edge lengths is a fundamental problem in discrete geometry. Gortler, Healy and Thurston showed that the number of real realisations of a generic framework is always even or equal to one. Despite being rare, there do exist graphs whose number of complex realisations is odd and not equal to one. In this article, we exhibit two necessary conditions for a rigid graph to have an odd realisation number other than one. We also provide an infinite family of rigid graphs with an odd realisation number other than one.

title: Property F implies weak integrality for non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion categories
abstract: We prove that every non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion category with property F is pseudo-unitary and weakly integral. In particular, every modular category with property F is weakly integral. Neither sphericality nor pseudo-unitarity is assumed. Passing to the Drinfeld centre extends the result to degenerate categories whose dimensions are positive on the intersection of the Müger centre with the adjoint subcategory; these include every braided fusion category with a pseudo-unitary Galois conjugate. Physically, the result connects the arithmetic of topological orders to the computational power of anyon braiding: non-integer squared total quantum dimension guarantees infinite braid group images, a necessary condition for universal quantum computation.

title: Extensions from Positive and Full Unit Spheres of $C^\infty([0,1])$ with a Compatible Fréchet Metric
abstract:
We study isometric extensions from positive and full unit spheres of $C^\infty([0,1],\mathbb F)$, where $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. We equip these spaces with a translation-invariant metric that induces the usual Fréchet topology, is unbounded, has convex balls, and has strictly increasing distances from zero along nonzero rays.
  Every surjective isometry of the pointwise positive unit sphere extends uniquely to a complex-linear surjective isometry of the complex-valued space. Restriction gives the unique real-linear isometric extension on the real-valued space. On the full unit sphere, every surjective isometry extends uniquely to a real-linear surjective isometry. The positive-sphere maps are compositions with the identity or an admissible reflection. The full-sphere maps also allow constant unimodular factors and, over the complex field, conjugation. We also classify the surjective ambient isometries.
  A counterexample shows that these metric properties alone do not guarantee positive-sphere extension. Under an explicit anchor condition, we classify surjective isometries of finite-order jet-positive spheres for maximum-type anchored metrics and prove that they extend uniquely to complex-linear surjective isometries. The classification allows any permutation of the anchored coordinates, combined with the identity or reflection on the highest-derivative component. The condition holds for every anchor when $m=1$ or $m=2$.

title: Fourteenth-canonical birationality of threefolds with positive geometric genus
abstract: We prove that the pluricanonical map of a complex projective threefold of general type with canonical singularities and positive geometric genus is birational in every degree at least fourteen. The bound is sharp.

title: On Symmetric Chain Decompositions for Bruhat--Chevalley Posets
abstract: We consider Stanley's problem on describing symmetric chain decompositions for the Bruhat--Chevalley posets of partial flag varieties and, more generally, Schubert varieties. These posets describe the containment relations of cell closures in the partial flag variety $G/P$ of a connected complex reductive algebraic group $G$. A famous instance of this problem asks whether the poset of partitions that fit inside a rectangle ordered by containment admits a symmetric chain decomposition (SCD), corresponding to the case of Grassmannian Schubert varieties in type $A$. Our first main result applies the ``complete BP decomposition" of Richmond--Slofstra to show that the SCD problem for any rationally smooth Schubert variety reduces to the (generalized) Grassmannian case, in any semisimple type. We further study the SCDs provided by codes for Bruhat--Chevalley posets in type $A$. These SCDs can be viewed as a consequence of a particular form of complete BP decomposition. In particular, we show that a poset of permutation-labeled partitions in a rectangle corresponding to the quotient $\mathcal{S}_n/\mathcal{S}_{n-k}$ admits an SCD. Further, posets of weak compositions inside a rectangle are realized as Bruhat--Chevalley intervals with associated codes and SCDs.

title: Global zero distribution and pluripolar exceptional cones for complex linear differential equations
abstract: We study the zeros of solutions of complex linear differential equations of arbitrary order $n\ge2$ with exponential-sum coefficients. Using the initial-value space $\mathbb{C}^n$ to parametrize the solutions, we show that solutions with initial vectors outside a complete pluripolar cone of Lebesgue measure zero share an explicit common leading term for the global zero count and a common joint limit in radius and angle. The rescaled radial distance from the disk boundary has an exponential limiting distribution, while the rescaled angular deviations from each main ray are Gaussian. Inspired by logarithmic tracts in the Eremenko-Lyubich class $\mathcal{B}$, we pull exterior sectors back conformally to countably many curvilinear strips extending in finitely many directions and obtain zero-counting asymptotics in each strip, although the coefficients may lie outside this class. Moreover, the asymptotic formula for the global zero count and the joint limit in radius and angle persist under arbitrary entire perturbations of strictly smaller weighted exponential type.

title: Multi-objective Markov Decision Process: Set-valued Bellman's principle and fixed point perspective
abstract: We study infinite-horizon discounted Markov decision processes with multiple cost objectives and finite state and action spaces. We consider the set of value functions generated by randomized Markov policies, where each function describes the expected discounted costs from all initial states under a single policy. We establish a set-valued Bellman equation and characterize this set as the greatest fixed point of the associated Bellman operator. We also show that choosing an attainable cost vector separately for each initial state can produce a function that no single Markov policy realizes. Nevertheless, the attainable costs at individual states satisfy their own Bellman recursion. These results provide a dynamic programming and fixed point framework for multi-objective Markov decision processes.

title: On Continuum Theories in a Locally Conformal Setting
abstract:
We study continuum and kinetic dynamics on locally conformally symplectic (LCS) and locally conformally cosymplectic (LCCos) manifolds. The main geometric tool is the Lichnerowicz-de Rham differential, which allows local geometric data that are compatible only up to conformal rescaling to glue into global structures.
  In the LCS setting, we analyze the locally conformal Vlasov equation from the viewpoint of continuity. Its source term does not represent particle creation or annihilation: it measures the mismatch between the ordinary phase-space volume and the conformally weighted volume determined by the Lee form. Absorbing this weight into the density yields a source-free continuity equation. We also compute the entropy production of the transported density, and illustrate the framework through a thermostatted ensemble, an LCS-driven Vlasov model with a momentum-dependent gyroscopic force, and their combination.
  We then propose a new definition of LCCos manifolds in which the defining one-form and two-form carry the same conformal weight. Unlike the usual convention, this allows local cosymplectic Hamiltonian systems to glue directly into global LCCos Hamiltonian dynamics, and it normalizes the evolution vector field by the conformal unit rather than by the ordinary unit. We develop the corresponding Hamiltonian, evolution and continuum dynamics, and illustrate them with a time-dependent mass example exhibiting transport in the distinguished time direction, momentum-space drift, and conformal source terms.

title: Classification of quasi-lisse simple affine vertex algebras
abstract: We classify all noncritical levels $k$ for which the simple affine vertex algebra $L_k(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse, for every finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. We prove that Fiebig's equivalence between the corresponding noncritical blocks of category $\mathcal{O}$ identifies the relevant parabolic Wakimoto modules and the homomorphisms from the corresponding universal affine vertex algebras. Combining this compatibility with a characterization of semisimple points in associated varieties, we establish that for coprime positive integers $p,q$, $L_{-h^\vee+p/q}(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse if and only if $L_{-h^\vee+p/\gcd(q,r)}(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse, where $r$ is the lacing number of $\mathfrak{g}$. The classification at the resulting levels is obtained using Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction, singular vectors and relations in the reductions of the maximal ideals of $V^k(\mathfrak{g})$. We also determine the associated varieties at the quasi-lisse levels for all $\mathfrak{g}$ of rank at most six and for $E_7$ and $E_8$.

title: Converse Lyapunov theorem for input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems
abstract:
We prove converse Lyapunov theorems for input-to-state stability (ISS) of a broad class of infinite-dimensional systems applicable to evolution equations in Banach spaces, boundary control systems, and delay systems. To this end, we employ a novel method that does not require constructing auxiliary closed-loop systems. We start by showing that ISS of a control system implies uniform global asymptotic stability of the same system with respect to trajectory-dominated inputs. Then, under an additional regularity requirement, we prove that an ISS Lyapunov function can be constructed.
  Based on our general result, we prove that for linear systems with unbounded $\infty$-admissible operators, ISS is equivalent to the existence of a Lipschitz continuous coercive ISS Lyapunov function.

title: Coarse Embeddings Beyond Doubling: Persistence Diagrams and Multiparameter Modules
abstract: We study coarse embeddings into Hilbert space and the asymptotic dimension of spaces of persistence diagrams and multiparameter persistence modules. We replace doubling, the usual hypothesis for landmark embeddings, by admissible tent covers of bounded multiplicity at every scale: stacking them across dyadic scales gives an explicit $1$-Lipschitz coarse embedding, with lower gauge $c\sqrt{τt}$, or nearly linear for slowly decaying weights, and the same covers bound the asymptotic dimension by the multiplicity. The spaces of persistence diagrams are not doubling but carry such covers, and for diagrams with $n$ points our covers improve the constant of the known landmark embedding by a factor exponential in $n$. Slice by slice, the construction embeds multiparameter modules with boundedly many bars per slice under the matching distance on any finite net of slices, a class that contains the modules with at most $n$ generators. Bounding bars or persistent Betti numbers instead of generators fails: two-parameter modules with one bar on every slice have infinite asymptotic dimension, and neither they nor the modules of bounded support and bounded rank admit a coarse embedding into Hilbert space, under the matching or the interleaving distance.

title: Distributional Limits of Empirical Codegree Processes in Sampled Networks
abstract: We study fluctuations of empirical distributions of normalized codegrees under independent vertex sampling from deterministic or random weighted parent networks. We establish a quantitative multivariate normal approximation for sampled biclique counts. Under additional graph-limit and sparsity assumptions, we establish convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the empirical codegree process indexed by smooth test functions. We further establish functional convergence on Hölder balls, with a smoothness threshold depending on network sparsity and vertex sampling probabilities. We verify our assumptions for classes of graphon-generated random graphs and give counterexamples showing that the smoothness conditions cannot in general be weakened.

title: Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity, Part II: Regular Pattern Packings and Moment Sequences
abstract:
We prove that broad families of regular pattern packings are enumerated by moments of probability measures on $[0,\infty)$. A packing prescribes occurrences of a consecutive permutation pattern at equally spaced positions, with successive occurrences overlapping and together covering the permutation. This regularity underlies the structure theory for the associated pattern-packing posets that we developed in Part I (arXiv:2610.29846).
  We obtain moment representations for all two-level shifted-grid families of Part I and all overlap-one patterns whose first and last letters differ by one or two. For families whose posets are trees with a unique minimum or maximum and overlap at most half the pattern length, positivity instead holds after finitely many initial terms of the enumerating sequence have been discarded. Our proofs develop further enumeration formulas and combine probabilistic constructions with total nonnegativity and weighted paths, yielding explicit laws or continued fractions in several cases.
  Although a previously conjectured universal moment property fails, our results establish positivity for all packing sequences associated with patterns of length at most four and all but one of the distinct sequences arising from patterns of length five. Extensive numerical evidence suggests that the remaining sequence is also a moment sequence. These results lead us to formulate refined conjectures for all overlap-one patterns and for the shifted-grid families of Part I with arbitrarily many levels.

title: Stability of patterns in variational systems with continuous symmetries: a computer-assisted approach
abstract: In variational models of pattern formation, periodic solutions are never isolated: since the energy does not change under translations, every shifted copy of a pattern is again a solution. This is an obstacle for computer-assisted proofs, which need isolated solutions. Imposing discrete symmetries removes the obstacle, but restricts the patterns that can be studied and only gives stability against symmetric perturbations. We develop a computer-assisted method that deals with the translations directly. We fix the position of the pattern with phase conditions and add unfolding parameters. They act as Lagrange multipliers, and translation invariance of the energy ensures that they vanish at a solution, under a condition that is verified rigorously by the computer. We then derive the stability of the pattern from the computer-assisted proof. We obtain the number of unstable directions and show that the only neutral directions are the translations. We apply the method to the Swift-Hohenberg equation in two dimensions and prove the existence of stable and unstable patterns without imposed symmetry. Since the linear algebra does not depend on the number of translation directions, the approach extends to higher dimensions.

title: Brown Measures and Spectral Convergence for Arbitrary GUE Polynomials
abstract:
For arbitrary noncommutative polynomials in independent GUE matrices, we prove that the empirical eigenvalue measure converges weakly in probability to the Brown measure of the corresponding polynomial in free semicircular variables. We also prove convergence of the entire eigenvalue set in Hausdorff distance and convergence of the spectral radius, both in probability. Equivalently, these matrix conclusions hold for arbitrary $*$-polynomials in independent complex Ginibre matrices. Independently, we prove that the support of the Brown measure of every polynomial in free semicircular variables equals its operator spectrum. The proof of weak convergence combines a criterion based on the second moment of the Brown measure with complex Gaussian rotation and convexity. The support theorem uses linearization and rigidity of matrix Dyson equations.
  We also prove absolute continuity for nonconstant polynomials without adjoints in free circular variables. A matrix Dyson equation recovers Brown measures of arbitrary semicircular polynomials through regularized logarithmic potentials. For drift-corrected nondegenerate elliptic free random walks, it yields quantitative convergence of potentials in the interior of the limiting domain and weak convergence of Brown measures to that of free multiplicative Brownian motion.

title: Average distance and maximum induced linear forest
abstract: Let G be a connected graph of order n, let μ(G) denote its average distance, and let L(G) denote the maximum order of an induced linear forest of G, that is, of an induced subgraph whose components are chains. Hansen, Hertz, Kilani, Marcotte and Schindl conjectured that μ(G) {\le} L(G)/2, which can be written as 4W(G) {\le} L(G)n(n-1), where W(G) is the Wiener index of G. This inequality strengthens their bound μ(G) {\le} F(G)/2, where F(G) is the maximum order of an induced forest, as well as Chung's classical bound μ(G) {\le} α(G). In this paper we prove the conjecture for all connected graphs.

title: Transport, Entropy, and the Cost of Dependence: Maximum Conditional Entropy under Transport Constraints
abstract: Maximum-entropy inference under Wasserstein constraints can be computationally challenging due to the underlying optimization over transport couplings. We investigate a tractable alternative based on maximizing conditional entropy under an average transport constraint. On Euclidean spaces, this formulation admits an explicit generalized-Gaussian additive-noise solution, providing a feasible approximation to the Wasserstein-constrained problem without solving an optimal transport problem. We establish quantitative bounds on the resulting optimality gap by showing that the two formulations admit a common feasible-marginal representation, with their discrepancy characterized by the mutual information retained between the nominal and perturbed variables. For discretely supported nominal distributions, we further obtain an exact decomposition of the gap into a marginal-entropy gain and a weighted Jensen-Shannon divergence.

title: Global Asymptotics of a Toda Soliton Condensate with Random Scattering Data
abstract: We study a dense $N$-soliton condensate for the infinite Toda lattice in the limit $N \to \infty$. In contrast to previous mathematical studies of soliton gases where the norming constants are assumed to be deterministic or infinitesimal, we consider initial scattering data where both the discrete eigenvalues and the norming constants are independent random variables. The norming constants $γ_j$ are allowed to be arbitrarily large under a mild moment condition $\mathbb{E}[γ_j^ν] < \infty$ ($ν> 1$). Our main result is divided into two parts. First, we develop a probabilistic Riemann--Hilbert framework to show that the system self-averages: despite large, independent fluctuations in the initial data, the random Toda lattice variables converge deterministically to an effective continuum model at a polynomial rate $\mathcal{O}(N^{-δ})$ for $0 < δ< 1/2$. Second, by performing the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest descent analysis of the continuum problem, we obtain the complete leading-order macroscopic description of the lattice across the entire space-time plane. The solution decomposes into five distinct finite-gap regimes, characterized explicitly by modulated elliptic and genus-2 waves with an error of order $\mathcal{O}(1/\ln N)$. In contrast to the straight characteristic rays typical of standard soliton gas limits, the interfaces separating these five macroscopic regimes in the space-time plane are genuinely non-linear curves; in particular, the boundary of the modulated genus-2 region is completely non-linear. Finally, under our assumptions, we establish the Nonlinear Dispersion Relations for the Toda soliton condensate and prove that the macroscopic ensemble averages are determined by the soliton gas density of states.

title: On Solvability of Irregular Infinite-Dimensional Differential-Algebraic Equations
abstract: This paper investigates the solvability of infinite-dimensional differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) on Hilbert spaces. We focus on irregular systems for which the operator pencil is not surjective onto the full state space, but only onto a subspace determined by the algebraic constraints. We establish a Lumer-Phillips-type generation result for this class of systems, showing that dissipativity together with a partial surjectivity condition yields a contraction semigroup on the dynamic subspace. The resulting wellposedness conditions are compared with existing solvability results. We further extend the analysis to systems in which hidden algebraic constraints restrict the dynamics to a proper closed subspace of the dynamical subspace. Under an additional structural condition, we show that the resulting constrained system is $E$-radial on suitably chosen spaces. We also demonstrate that semigroup generation does not, in general, imply $E$-radiality on the original state spaces. This provides a Weierstraß-type decomposition useful for controller design. The framework is illustrated by some examples.

title: The Szegő log-term and local rigidity of Kähler--Einstein polarizations of compact Hermitian symmetric spaces
abstract: We prove local rigidity of the vanishing Szegő log-term for integral Kähler--Einstein polarizations of a product of irreducible compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Near the invariant metric, vanishing of the log-term forces the Kähler form to lie in its biholomorphic orbit. The argument combines the first variation of the Kempf distortion function with a central-positioning procedure, reducing rigidity to polynomiality of spectral multipliers of the Laplace operator and the Berezin transform. For integral Kähler--Einstein polarizations, a common-pole obstruction then rules out all infinitesimal deformations transverse to the automorphism orbit.

title: Perdomo's index conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces in spheres
abstract: Let $x:M^n\to\sphere^{n+1}(1)$, $n\ge2$, be a full minimal immersion of a closed, connected, oriented manifold. We prove that its Morse index is at least $n+3$, with equality precisely for the standard Clifford embeddings. For a non-Clifford image, the constant function and the position and normal coordinates span a space containing an $(n+4)$-dimensional subspace on which the Jacobi quadratic form is negative definite.

title: Budan--Fourier theorem for circuit polynomial systems
abstract: We prove a Budan--Fourier theorem for linear combinations of analytic functions whose successive Wronskians are positive: the number of zeros of $g=\sum_{k=1}^s c_kh_k$ in an interval $(a,b]$, counted with multiplicities, is bounded by the drop of the number of sign changes of the sequence of Wronskians $W(h_1,\ldots,h_{k-1},g)$ between $a$ and $b$, and the difference is even. This refines the bound $s-1$ of Koiran, Portier and Tavenas, and we show that it applies, after a suitable renumbering, to any sequence of functions satisfying Descartes' rule of signs. We then study the functions arising from polynomial systems supported on circuits, that is, systems of $n$ equations in $n$ variables with $n+2$ monomials. For these functions, we show that the Budan--Fourier bound never exceeds Descartes' bound, and we compute it at the endpoints of the interval of definition.
