As an application, we obtain a refinement of the optimal Descartes' rule of signs for circuits of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård: we bound the number of positive solutions whose logarithm lies in explicit polytopes, these bounds add up to at most the bound of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård, and they determine the parity of the number of positive solutions.

title: Second-Order Linear $q$-Difference Equations
abstract: Second order $q$ difference equations arise in various areas such as basic hypergeometric series, orthogonal polynomials and the analytic theory of special functions. When the independent variable is scaled by powers of $q$ ($0<q<1$), such equations display asymptotic behaviour that differs markedly from their differential or classical difference counterparts. Our purpose is to give a complete, self contained treatment of linear, second order $q$ difference equations with divergent formal solutions, including explicit error bounds, exact resummations and Stokes phenomena.

title: Sharpness of the Martin-O'Bryant autoconvolution inequality
abstract: We show that there does not exist a constant $c<1$ such that ${\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{2}}^2\le c\,{\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{1}}{\lVert f\ast f\rVert}_{L^{\infty}}$ holds for every nonnegative $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R})\cap L^2(\mathbb{R})$.

title: Eigenvector Occupation Statistics and Extremes in the Rosenzweig-Porter Model
abstract: We study the occupation probabilities $p_i=|u_i|^2$ of a normalized bulk eigenvector in the GUE Rosenzweig-Porter model $A_N=B_N+τ_NG_N$, with $τ_N^2=N^{1-γ}$ and $1<γ<2$. Conditioning on an eigenvalue at a regular bulk energy $E$ through the normalized one-eigenpair Kac-Rice law, we derive an exact finite-$N$ projective density and reduce its asymptotic analysis to a Hubbard-Stratonovich integral over $2\times2$ Hermitian matrices, which we evaluate by the saddle-point method. The resulting occupation field is governed by a self-consistent Lorentzian profile with effective resonant size $K_N(E)\asymp N^{2-γ}$ and local exponential fluctuations. We prove the asymptotics of all generalized inverse participation sums and identify a transition at $q=1/2$. We also obtain a two-branch thickened amplitude-counting spectrum. At the two ends of the occupation field we prove marked Poisson point-process limits: the largest components have Gumbel fluctuations, whereas the smallest component has an exponential limit on the scale $N^{-1-γ}$. Finally, for every fixed $q>0$ the largest component contributes an asymptotically vanishing fraction of the inverse participation sum, showing that these fixed-$q$ statistics do not freeze. The statements are quenched, uniformly on a high-probability regularity event for the diagonal disorder, and hence also hold in the annealed setting.

title: Adding unbounded and not bounded sets to a singular cardinal
abstract: This paper solves a problem (SP) attributed to Solovay in the 1960s, which is to add an unbounded sequence to a singular cardinal $κ$ without adding bounded subsets to $κ$, while preserving $κ^+$. The solution applies to any cofinality of the singular cardinal, with the assumption that $κ$ is a strong limit needed for the case of uncountable cofinality. Unsuccessful attempts to solve (SP), mostly for the countable cofinality, have appeared in published papers by various authors.

title: Discrete Configuration Spaces of Simplex Skeleta: a Middle-Dimensional Manifold Phenomenon
abstract: For a simple graph $Γ$ without loops and an integer $n\geq2$, Abrams showed in his Ph.D. thesis that the discrete configuration space $DConf(Γ,n)$ is homeomorphic to a closed $n$-manifold if and only if $n=2$ and $Γ$ is $K_5$ or $K_{3,3}$, the two minimal obstructions to graph planarity. We show that this manifold property persists for the infinite family of discrete configuration spaces obtained by replacing the Kuratowski graphs with the $d$-skeleton of the simplex of dimension $2d+2$, thus recovering Abrams' $K_5$ case when $d=1$. Our manifold recognition argument relies on a recursive application of Whitehead's theorem that collapsible PL manifolds are PL balls, combined with Forman's discrete Morse theory. The resulting construction produces an infinite family of combinatorial spheres that contains the Legendre polytope boundaries and is closed under taking vertex links.

title: Strong pseudo Frobenius numbers
abstract: By Sylow's theorem, the number of Sylow $p$-subgroups of a finite group is congruent to $1$ modulo $p$, but not every such integer occurs. Frobenius extended the congruence to the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ for every $a\ge0$. Kulakoff and Hall showed that this number is congruent to $1$ or $1+p$ modulo $p^2$ whenever $p^{a+1}$ divides the group order. A positive integer is a Frobenius $p$-number if it is the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ of some finite group for some $a$. There are integers congruent to $1$ modulo $p^2$ which are not Frobenius $p$-numbers, and it remained open whether there are also such integers congruent to $1+p$ modulo $p^2$. We show that no finite group has exactly $106$ subgroups of order $5^a$ for any $a\ge0$.

title: The dimension of multi-index assignment polytopes and Latin-square transversal polytopes, via association schemes
abstract: We determine the dimensions, and the implicit equations, of several polytopes from integer programming whose vertices are the largest stable sets of highly symmetric graphs. Our main tools are two new dimension formulae within Lee's spectral method, which reads the dimension off of an association scheme: for amorphic schemes it becomes a threshold formula, and for point sets in $GF(q)^d$ invariant under the maps $z\mapsto az+b$ it is $q-1$ times the number of hyperplane directions along which some point is not equidistributed. A single integer point, a witness, then certifies a whole eigenspace. For the multi-index assignment polytopes of Appa, Magos, and Mourtos at prime-power orders, the dimension equals that of the linear relaxation except in two infinite families, which are, to our knowledge, the first counterexamples to their expectation that the two always coincide. The missing equations are explicit clique equations that the standard integer-programming formulation omits. For every abelian group with a transversal, the Latin-square transversal polytope of its Cayley table, equivalently the polytope of rainbow perfect matchings of the corresponding edge-colored $K_{n,n}$ , has the maximal dimension ${(n-1)(n-2)}$; the witnesses come from new constructions of complete mappings. We also treat transversals of Desarguesian nets and the largest sets of symmetric $3\times3$ and $4\times4$ matrices over $GF(q)$ whose differences have rank at least $3$, of sizes $q^3$ and $q^5$.

title: Riemannian Real-Time Optimization for Robotics: Active Set SQP Parametric Pathfollowing
abstract: Robot optimal control often combines Euclidean states with configurations on Lie groups and other smooth manifolds. This paper develops a parametric Riemannian Newton pathfollowing method based on homotopy quadratic programs and parallel strict-working-set tasks. It specifies the event handling, working-set exchanges, matrix factor updates, synchronization, and residual checks used by the algorithm. Tracking guarantees are given under mildly degenerate regularity conditions and the Riemannian strong second-order sufficient condition. Drone navigation and arm manipulation are formulated as geometric optimal-control problems, including finite-force grasp acquisition, transport and supported release. Numerical examples illustrate drone navigation and arm pick-and-place through KKT-residual histories and MuJoCo simulations, together with preliminary initialization results for the full-horizon optimal-control problems.

title: Separable $\mathcal L_{\infty}$-spaces with Kalton's property $Q$
abstract: We construct separable $\mathcal L_\infty$-spaces with Kalton's property $Q$, which, to the best of our knowledge, are the first known examples of this kind. Our technique employs the Bourgain--Pisier construction and a quantitative analysis of metric types in limits of finite-dimensional $η$-admissible embeddings. The argument rests on two complementary estimates: approximate radial centres yield asymptotic separation of tree increments, while an admissibility inequality yields asymptotic gain, leading to concentration on Kalton's interlacing graphs. This leads to an abstract criterion for property $Q$ in terms of asymptotic separation $AS_θ$ and asymptotic gain $AG_α$. We illustrate the limitations of this criterion with Johnson--Lindenstrauss spaces. Our examples exclude uniform embeddings of the unit ball of $c_0$, strengthening in a nonlinear direction the classical Bourgain--Delbaen phenomenon. As an application, every separable Banach space embeds isometrically into a separable $\mathcal L_\infty$-space whose unit ball is not a uniform retract of the unit ball of its bidual.

title: The Cheng--Yau gradient estimate for Jacobi fields
abstract: We prove a pointwise gradient estimate for positive Jacobi fields on minimal hypersurfaces of dimension two and three, inspired by the Cheng--Yau estimate for harmonic functions. The estimate also controls the second fundamental form, and so provides yet another proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in dimensions two and three.

title: Semiampleness of Hodge line bundles and b-semiampleness of the moduli part
abstract:
We give proofs of Hodge semiampleness and b-semiampleness without using o-minimality. We establish a geometric semiampleness criterion for line bundles on proper algebraic spaces. Let $(X,D)$ be a log smooth pair with $X$ a proper algebraic space. For an integral polarizable pure variation of Calabi--Yau type on $X\setminus D$ with unipotent local monodromy, let $L$ be its extended highest Hodge line. If $L$ is numerically integrable and has torsion combinatorial monodromy, then $L$ is semiample. We also prove semiampleness of extended Griffiths lines. We construct normal projective period compactifications on which a positive power of the Griffiths line extends to an ample line bundle.
  As an application, we prove that the moduli b-divisor $\mathbf{M}$ of a projective lc-trivial fibration over a normal algebraic variety is b-semiample, provided that the generic boundary is effective. Suppose further that the geometric generic pair is klt and its boundary is big, with nonzero coefficients in a fixed finite set $I\subset(0,1)\cap\mathbb{Q}$. Then $c\mathbf{M}$ is b-Cartier and b-free for an integer $c>0$ depending only on the relative dimension and $I$. We extend b-semiampleness to analogous projective fibrations over normal complex analytic bases, assuming a global relative polarization and an invertible log pluricanonical sheaf pulled back from the base.

title: Periodic vortex dipoles near closed geodesics on Riemannian surfaces
abstract: We study the motion of a pair $(p_1,p_2)\inΣ\timesΣ$ of point vortices with equal magnitude and opposite signs on a closed oriented Riemannian surface $(Σ,g)$. Given a closed geodesic that satisfies a non-degeneracy condition we construct a one-parameter family of periodic solutions $(p_1^\varepsilon,p_2^\varepsilon)$, $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, of the Hamiltonian dynamical system for point vortex pairs whose trajectories converge towards the geodesic curve. The two vortices lie on opposite sides of the geodesic, are separated of order $\varepsilon$ and have period $2π\varepsilon$. The proof is based on a differentiated expansion of the Riemannian distance in Fermi coordinates, an augmented Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction, and an intricate contraction argument in scaled variables. The reduced normal equation is governed by the Jacobi operator of the closed geodesic, and the first order correction to the normal center of the dipole is characterized by an inhomogeneous Jacobi equation involving the curvature and the regular part of the Green function of the Laplace-Beltrami operator.

title: Residual-Based Spectral Submanifold Reduction of Constrained Multibody Systems on Matrix Lie Groups
abstract: The parameterization method yields efficient and accurate reduced-order models for nonlinear dynamical systems, but existing procedures that compute them assume polynomial vector fields on vector spaces. Constrained multibody systems instead obey differential-algebraic equations on matrix Lie groups such as $\mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$ and $SE(3)$. Minimal parameterizations of these groups lead to non-polynomial equations that must be approximated or recast before reduction, and current implementations require the nonlinearities as explicit multilinear maps, which are cumbersome to construct for assembled multibody systems. This work develops a parameterization framework for constrained multibody systems on matrix Lie groups. Rigid and floating frame of reference bodies use rotation-matrix components or Euler parameters, while geometrically exact beam elements use an Euler-Rodrigues representation that eliminates the logarithmic map and expresses the exponential map polynomially, retaining screw-motion interpolation. The reduced-order models satisfy linear joint constraints exactly, and a rotation-preserving parameterization keeps the configuration on the Lie group to machine precision. The parameterization method is formulated directly in terms of the assembled residual, so that only residual evaluations and their derivatives are required. Truncated Taylor arithmetic delivers all Taylor coefficients of a given order from a single residual evaluation, and a non-intrusive coupling to codes with real-valued residuals is demonstrated with the multibody code Exudyn. Numerical examples show accurate prediction of backbone curves, forced response curves, and internal resonances at substantially reduced computational cost.

title: Finiteness of fundamental groups for manifolds with sign-changing Ricci curvature
abstract: Let $M$ be a complete open $κ$ noncollapsed Riemannian manifold and have Ricci curvature bounded from below. If the negative part of its Ricci curvature goes to zero sufficiently rapidly at infinity in terms of the volume noncollapse constant and dimension $n$, then the fundamental group of $M$ is finite. When the Ricci curvature is nonnegative, the result agrees with the classical conclusion of [Peter Li, 1986].

title: On the Cohomological Amplitude of the Locally Analytic Jacquet--Langlands Functor
abstract: We prove a local cohomological bound $RΓ_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)\in D^{[0,\dim X]}$ for a pro-étale sheaf with a derived $p$-complete integral lattice whose modulo $p^m$ reductions are filtered colimits of finite local systems on an affinoid topologically of finite type over $C$. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $n\geq2$ and $F/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, we apply these local bounds to variants of Scholze's Jacquet--Langlands functor $\mathrm{JL}_\mathscr{B}(Π):= RΓ_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(\mathbb{P}^{n-1}_C,\mathcal{F}_Π\otimes^{L, \square}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}\mathscr{B})$ for $\mathscr{B}\in\{\mathbb{Q}_p, \widehat{\mathscr{O}}, \mathbb{B}_J\}$ and Banach or compact-type LB representations $Π$ of $G$, obtaining $\mathrm{JL}_{\mathscr{B}}(Π)\in D^{[0,2(n-1)]}$ for each choice of $\mathscr{B}$. We also prove that for arbitrary continuous principal series $I(η)=(\mathrm{Ind}_B^Gη)^{\mathrm{cont}}$, we have $\mathrm{JL}(\mathrm{Ind}_B^Gη)\in D^{[0, n]}$, while $\mathrm{JL}_{\widehat{\mathscr{O}}}(I(η)),\mathrm{JL}_{\mathbb{B}_J}(I(η))\in D^{[0, n-1]}$.

title: Permutation symmetries and characteristic polynomials
abstract: We compute certain multilinear functionals of permutation-invariant random matrices, following the work of Marcus and Geneson. As an application, we derive formulae for the average characteristic polynomial of the sum and the product of permutation-invariant random matrices.

title: The Paley--Wiener excess and a local law for the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process
abstract: The main result of this paper is the proof that the Paley--Wiener excess of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ process almost surely equals $\lfloor \sqrt{2/β}\rfloor$ for all $β>0$. We also derive the loop equations for the resolvent of the ${\rm Sine}_β$ point process and use them to obtain accurate bounds on the moments of the associated Stieltjes transform.

title: Diophantine conditions for absolute continuity of projections for self-similar measures
abstract: We prove that every projection of a planar self-similar measure $μ$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on its support if the rotations satisfy a simultaneous Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ and $μ$ has finite $s$-energy for some $1+2τ\le s<2$. Under strong separation, we prove the fibre measures have exact dimension $\dim_Hμ-1$. For self-similar sets $E$ with $\dim_H E>1+2τ$, the same rotation condition implies uniformly positive projection lengths and fibres of dimension $\dim_H E-1$ at Lebesgue-almost every point of each image without separation assumptions. The absolute continuity and fibre dimension theorems extend to non-coordinate projections of products under a joint Diophantine condition with exponent $τ$ on the logarithmic contraction ratios. These imply for all self-similar sets $K,L\subset\mathbb R$ satisfying this condition and $\dim_HK+\dim_HL>1+2τ$, every sum $uK+L$, $u\ne 0$, has positive length, and $\dim_H(L\cap(y-uK))=\dim_HK+\dim_HL-1$ for Leb. a.e. $y\in uK+L$. The proof combines the $L^1$ Gaussian smoothing approach used in the higher dimensional case with averaging at random stopping scales with a Brownian martingale bound using Itô calculus.

title: Legendre manifolds generated by the Barenblatt equations
abstract: The paper is devoted to the construction of exact general solutions of the equations of oil filtration in a porous medium under the action of an active reagent injected into the reservoir. The choice of the reagent solution determines the control process of chemical oil flooding in hard-to-recover fields. The problem is described by a system of two first-order nonlinear partial differential equations (the Barenblatt model). Conditions are found on the Buckley--Leverett function, the adsorption function, and the distribution function of the reagent in oil under which the original system, by means of a nonlinear change of variables on a five-dimensional manifold endowed with a contact structure, is reduced to a linear wave system with constant coefficients. Six families of such functions are indicated. For them, contact transformations and Legendre surfaces corresponding to general solutions in implicit form are constructed.

title: A complete symmetric rank-two modularity classification, obtained through a sharp uniform degree bound
abstract:
We classify modular Nahm sums with a rational symmetric positive-definite two-by-two matrix and rational shifts. Up to coordinate exchange, every modular datum belongs to three explicit rational-point families, is a product of two modular rank-one sums, or is one of thirty-four exceptional triples on twelve matrices. The list consists of Zagier's rank-two examples, the Vlasenko--Zwegers additions and split products; no further data occur. The proof first bounds the joint degree of the distinguished Nahm point by four, using an initial degree bound of twenty-four and exact local exclusions at the prime 7. Explicit height and exponent bounds then give exhaustive arithmetic classifications in degrees one through four. Exact polynomial elimination determines all rational shifts, and published identities of q-series establish modularity of the survivors. The degree bound is sharp. The finite steps are accompanied by exact certificates, verification programs and independently implemented checks.
  Computational companion: https://github.com/johnngy44/math/releases

title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations and Closed-Form Geodesics on Non-Naturally Reductive Orbit Spheres: The Spin(9) 15-Sphere and the Cayley Plane
abstract: By the Skew-Torsion Holonomy Theorem of Olmos and Reggiani (2012), the 15-sphere $S^{15}$ admits no non-trivial naturally reductive metric under any transitive Lie group, precluding geodesic integration via canonical Ambrose-Singer connections. Simultaneously, Nikonorov (2013) established that every $Spin(9)$-invariant metric on $S^{15}$ is a geodesic orbit (GO) space. We integrate the geodesic flow on this non-naturally reductive GO manifold via the Lie Subalgebra Closure Principle: whenever the slice generators of a multi-axial reductive decomposition close into a finite-rank reductive Lie subalgebra, the geodesic vector equations decouple into an algebraic eigenvalue problem. Using the 16-dimensional spin representation and Vol'per's decomposition $\mathfrak{spin}(9) = \mathfrak{spin}(7) \oplus \mathfrak{p}_1 \oplus \mathfrak{p}_2$, we prove that the slice generators $X_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_2$ and $Y_1 \in \mathfrak{p}_1$ close into $\mathfrak{u}(2) \cong \mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1) \subset \mathfrak{so}(16)$. The generator $M = αX_1 + βY_1$ has the four-mode spectrum $Ω\in \{ |R \pm 3α|, |R \pm α| \}$ ($R = \sqrt{α^2 + β^2}$), yielding a closed-form 4-projector decomposition and Euler-Cartan factorization for $\exp(αX_1 + βY_1)$. Under the normalized Ricci flow, we prove that the Bourguignon-Karcher squashed Einstein metric at $t = 3/11$ ($λ= 64$) is an unstable repeller separating sub-Riemannian fiber collapse from the round sphere basin. Finally, on the deformed Cayley plane $\mathbb{O}P^2 = F_4/Spin(9)$, we prove universal CROSS never-Einstein rigidity, establish the 15-dimensional three-stratum Whitney stratification of the cut locus $Cut(q_0)$ at non-polar basepoints $q_0$, and prove Blaschke and Besse rigidity for all $λ> 0$.

title: The generic behavior of permutation entropy for continuous maps
abstract:
Permutation entropy, introduced by Bandt and Pompe in 2002, measures the complexity of a dynamical system through the ordinal patterns of its trajectories. Bandt, Keller and Pompe established that for measure-preserving, piecewise monotone interval maps with finitely many monotonicity intervals, the normalized order-$n$ permutation entropy $H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)/n$ converges to the Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy. Although this result has subsequently been extended to broader classes of maps, whether normalized permutation entropy always converges has remained unknown.
  We show that convergence can fail, and indeed that nonconvergence is generic. More precisely, for a generic continuous Lebesgue measure-preserving map $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$, we prove that \[ \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)}{n}=0, \qquad \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{H_n^{\mathrm{perm}}(f)}{n\log n}=1. \] Thus, despite the generic vanishing of Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy, permutation entropy exhibits oscillations between vanishing linear growth and the maximal possible asymptotic growth.
  We also construct an explicit Lebesgue measure-preserving interval map with countably many monotonicity intervals for which the normalized permutation entropy has lower limit zero and upper limit infinity. This demonstrates that nonconvergence can occur even within the countably piecewise-monotone setting, beyond the scope of the convergence theorem of Gutjahr and Keller, relying on conditions concerning the lengths of the pieces.

title: Concave shifts and the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property
abstract: Let $\mathcal H$ be a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on the unit disc, and assume $\mathcal H$ is invariant under the forward and backward shifts. We show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal H$ is concave, then $\mathcal H$ is a complete Nevanlinna--Pick space. This gives an affirmative answer to the concavity part of Shimorin's question \cite{Sh02} and extends his theorem on the complete Nevanlinna--Pick property of Dirichlet-type spaces with superharmonic weights.

title: Adaptive Output Regulation of Linear Systems with Unknown Harmonic Exosystems and Additive Noise
abstract: This paper addresses error-feedback output regulation for known multivariable linear plants subject to an unknown exosystem and additive Gaussian process and measurement noise. The exosystem generates constant and sinusoidal signals, but its dimension, frequencies, and coupling matrices are unavailable. An output-injection transformation represents the external action through known channels. A causal observer then produces a residual independent of the applied input, whose filtered output separates into a harmonic signal, stationary colored Gaussian noise, and a decaying transient. Using this observation model, a Fourier procedure consistently identifies the number and values of the active positive frequencies in the presence of noise. The identified frequencies determine a regulator through interpolation with stable residual filters. A contractive filter realization, nonexpansive state resizing, and bounded gain updates ensure closed-loop moment bounds uniformly over the selected filter orders. If the gain bound contains the ideal interpolation gain, the adaptive plant response and tracking error converge in mean square to those of the corresponding known-frequency regulator. The limiting mean-square tracking error is a linear function of the process- and measurement-noise covariances. In the absence of both noises, the tracking error converges to zero.

title: On regularity and stability results of global weak solutions to two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum
abstract:
For the initial and initial-boundary value problems of the two-dimensional (2D) incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity and vacuum, Lions' global weak solutions are shown to possess additional regularity, via establishing some key a priori decay-in-time rates for the approximate problem, under suitable
  smallness condition on the density-dependent viscosity.
  In addition, large-time decay rates of the pressure and gradient of velocity are obtained,
  which are even exponential in time for bounded domains or the periodic case. Note that these results hold without any smallness conditions on the initial data, even for initially vanishing density.

title: On the higher-order Titchmarsh divisor problem
abstract: For every fixed integer $k\geq2$ and every fixed nonzero integer $h$, we prove that, as $x\to\infty$, \begin{equation*} \sum_{x<n\leq2x}Λ(n)τ_k(n+h) \sim C_{k,h}x(\log x)^{k-1}, \end{equation*} where $τ_k$ is the $k$-fold divisor function and $C_{k,h}>0$ is a constant depending only on $k$ and $h$.

title: KL-Regularized Policy Iteration for Adaptive LQR: Gain Updates and Probing from One Policy Improvement
abstract: Policy-gradient methods for adaptive linear quadratic control improve the feedback gain of an unknown plant online by gradient-type steps computed from closed-loop data. A recent framework of such methods, policy-gradient adaptive control (PGAC), takes one gradient-type step per sample, which its indirect form computes from an estimated model and its direct form directly from the data. Because data generated by a fixed linear feedback cannot identify the plant, PGAC adds a probing perturbation to the input and leaves its covariance as a design parameter. We study the adaptive LQR problem through a KL-regularized formulation, in which the probing is the randomness of a Gaussian policy kept close to a Gaussian reference policy, so that the cost of the probing is part of the objective. One policy improvement of this formulation gives a gain update together with a probing covariance. We show that, for suitable references centred at the current gain, this gain update is exactly PGAC's Gauss-Newton or natural-gradient update with any step size below a bound. We repeat this policy improvement, each time against a tempered copy of the current policy, and refer to this scheme as KL-regularized policy iteration (KLPI). On a known plant and with tempering, the cost of KLPI's gains converges linearly to the optimal cost, and the probing covariance keeps a floor proportional to the regularization weight. On an estimated plant, under conditions like PGAC's (small updates and sufficiently informative data), the closed loop stays stable, the cost of the gains converges linearly up to a bias, and the probing covariance again keeps this floor. In simulations at equal probing cost, the shape of KLPI's probing covariance, which PGAC can adopt, lowers the extra cost caused by suboptimal gains on nearly all tested plants, whereas KLPI's use of past iterations in its gain update changes this cost little.

title: Hidden frequencies in topological dynamical systems
abstract: We show for certain skew products built over any infinite minimal nilsystem, the frequencies present in the nilsystem are not always enough to govern recurrence for the whole system. This strengthens and generalizes a theorem of Glasscock, Koutsogiannis, and Richter.

title: Perfect loops of proper schemes
abstract: We study the perfect loop space $LX$ of a proper scheme $X$ over a local field $F$. We show that if $X$ contains a rational curve, then $LX$ is not ind-representable, even in a very weak sense. We also show that if $X$ admits a proper model $\mathfrak{X}$ over the integers $\mathcal{O}$ of $F$, whose geometric special fiber does not contain rational curves, then $L^+\mathfrak{X} \stackrel{\sim}{\to} LX$ is an isomorphism via the natural map, where $L^+\mathfrak{X}$ denotes the perfect positive loop space (jet scheme) of $\mathfrak{X}$. In particular, $LX$ is a scheme in this case.

title: One-Particle Resonances and Eigenstate Thermalization in Periodic Free-Fermion Lattices
abstract: We study eigenstate fluctuations of the particle number in the nearest-neighbour free-fermion model on the periodic cubic lattice $(\mathbb{Z}/L\mathbb{Z})^d$. For every fixed dimension, every particle number, every subvolume, and every normalized energy eigenstate, we prove a bound of order $NL^{d-1}$ for the particle-number variance. The corresponding eigenstate-thermalization estimate is of order $L^{d-1}/(Nη^2)$ for fluctuations of relative size $η$. In particular, at positive particle density the bound decays as the inverse linear size. The proof decomposes the centered particle-number operator according to one-particle energy transfer and treats the zero- and nonzero-transfer components separately. The nonzero-transfer part is controlled by a sharp resonance bound, proved from Mann's theorem on relations among roots of unity, while the zero-transfer part is estimated by a Hilbert-Schmidt argument. These bounds are optimal in every dimension: the maximal nonzero-gap multiplicity has order $L^{d-1}$, and suitable many-body eigenstates realize matching variance lower bounds and show that the concentration bound cannot be improved in estimates uniform in the tolerance parameter.

title: When is Polynomial Optimization SoS-Exact? Sufficient Regularization and Strict Gram Representations
abstract: Global minimization of multivariate polynomials is computationally difficult in general, and nonnegativity does not necessarily imply a sum-of-squares (SoS) representation. We show that adding sufficiently strong Euclidean regularization to a polynomial provides a general mechanism for overcoming such challenges. Namely, for any multivariate polynomial $P$ of degree at most $p$ with a nonzero linear coefficient, and any even integer $2d>p$, we prove that $m_σ(s)=P(s)+\fracσ{2d}\|s\|_2^{2d}$ is SoS exact for all sufficiently large $σ$. Furthermore, the shifted polynomial $m_σ-\min m_σ$ admits a positive-definite Gram representation on appropriately-shifted nonconstant monomials. Consequently, the global minimum and minimizer can be recovered exactly by a single degree-$d$ semidefinite programming (SDP) representation, whose size is polynomial in the dimension for fixed $d$, without requiring higher levels of the SoS hierarchy. The proof develops a degree-independent mechanism based on the Bregman remainder of the regularizer: its strict Gram margin absorbs the lower-degree polynomial perturbations. We further establish an analogous exact SDP regime for polynomial optimization over sufficiently small Euclidean balls, connecting large regularization with small-radius trust-region problems. Finally, we investigate how the algebraic structure of the regularizer governs the existence of a strict Gram margin, extending the mechanism beyond Euclidean norms while identifying limitations of coordinate-separable regularization.

title: Counter-examples to Conjectures on NCCRs via a Reductive McKay Correspondence
abstract: We disprove three conjectures appearing in Van den Bergh's plenary ICM survey, posed by De Deyn and Van den Bergh, which concern the interplay between non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) and the stringy Euler characteristic. Our counter-examples are applications of a new McKay correspondence for reductive groups that we prove in this paper, extending the classical McKay correspondence for finite groups. We obtain explicit formulas for the stringy $E$-functions of reductive quotients in terms of the Weyl group action and stringy $E$-functions of toric varieties; we also obtain an equivalent formula expressed as an integral of the age function over Weyl-fixed loci of a compact real torus. For symmetric representations, our expressions are related to arithmetic Tutte polynomials, yielding combinatorial formulas for the stringy Euler characteristic.

title: Shape Holomorphy of the Calderón Projector on Lipschitz Surfaces: Frequency-Explicit Bounds for the Helmholtz
abstract:
We establish the holomorphic dependence of the Calderón projector for the Helmholtz operator upon shape boundary deformations of a family of bounded Lipschitz domains in two and three spatial dimensions, with bounds explicit in the wavenumber and the size of the holomorphic extension. More precisely, after transporting the four boundary integral operators contained in the Calderón projector to a fixed reference boundary, we prove that the resulting parameter-to-operator maps admit bounded holomorphic extensions in their natural fractional Sobolev spaces. Unlike approaches that require boundary regularity of class $\mathscr C^{1,1}$ or higher, our argument traces the holomorphic dependence on the shape by transferring elliptic estimates to the boundary through the fundamental solution and the Dirichlet and conormal trace operators. This construction is the key step that allows us to treat Lipschitz-regular boundary deformations.
  Furthermore, we show that the domain of holomorphy can be chosen independently of the wavenumber $κ$, while the operator bounds in the corresponding fractional Sobolev spaces contain algebraic factors in $κ$ multiplied by $\exp(Cκδ)$. In particular, for real domains, corresponding to $δ=0$, our single layer estimate recovers, to our knowledge, the best available frequency dependence on general Lipschitz boundaries. For the double layer, adjoint double layer, and hypersingular operators, we obtain novel frequency-explicit bounds.
  The results proved in this work provide the analytic foundation for frequency-explicit uncertainty quantification, model order reduction, and high-dimensional approximation of boundary integral operators, their Galerkin discretizations, and the resulting boundary densities and quantities of interest on families of parametrically varying boundaries.

title: Continuum hierarchical Cannings process: I. Construction, duality and dichotomy
abstract: We construct spatial measure-valued Cannings processes on the \emph{continuum} hierarchical group $Ω_N^\infty$ of order $N\in\N$ (an uncountable topological group with an ultrametric distance). These processes arise as the continuum-space limit of spatial Cannings processes on the \emph{discrete} hierarchical group $Ω_N$ of order $N\in\N$ (a countable topological group with an ultrametric distance) analysed in \cite{GHKK14}. On $Ω_N$, each site represents the \emph{geographic location} of a colony of individuals, each carrying a \emph{type} drawn from a compact type space $\K$, and the state in each colony is a probability measure on $\K$ describing the type distribution in that colony in the large-colony-size limit of individual-based models. The continuum-space processes on $Ω_N^\infty$ take values in the set of locally finite measures on $Ω_N^\infty \times \K$ and are to be thought of as describing a population of individuals, each equipped with a geographic location in $Ω_N^\infty$ and a type in $\K$, and each being subjected to \emph{migration} and three mechanisms of \emph{resampling}: (1) Fleming-Viot resampling at single sites; (2) Cannings resampling at single sites; (3) Cannings resampling and uniform reshuffling in balls around single sites (corresponding to consecutive hierarchical levels). The reshuffling adds to the migration, resulting in an \emph{effective migration} that is the superposition of the two relocation mechanisms.

title: FEALPy.OPT: A Multi-Backend Tensor Computing Framework for Metaheuristic Optimization on CPU and GPU Platforms
abstract: Metaheuristic algorithms (MAs) are widely used to solve complex optimization problems, but their computational costs can become substantial as population size and problem dimensionality increase. This paper presents FEALPy.OPT, an open-source Python framework for metaheuristic optimization built on the FEALPy computational infrastructure. It integrates a unified optimizer abstraction with multi-backend tensor computation, supporting NumPy and PyTorch backends on CPU and GPU platforms. To evaluate its computational performance, five metaheuristic algorithms are tested on ten benchmark functions under three problem scales, with population sizes ranging from 100 to 10,000 and dimensions from 30 to 100. The results show that NumPy/CPU achieves the shortest average runtime for small-scale problems, whereas PyTorch/GPU becomes increasingly advantageous as the problem scale grows. For large-scale problems, PyTorch/GPU is approximately 9.50 times faster than PyTorch/CPU and 32.96 times faster than NumPy/CPU. These findings demonstrate the value of multi-backend and multi-platform support for improving the computational flexibility and efficiency of metaheuristic optimization.

title: FRT presentation of the $q$-Onsager comodule algebra and refined $q$-characters
abstract: We introduce a concept of counital comodule algebra $(B,δ_B,ε_B)$ over a Hopf ${\mathbb K}$-algebra $H$, where $δ_B: B\rightarrow B \otimes H$ and $ε_B: B\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ are coaction and counit homomorphisms, respectively. This structure gives a canonical (counital) comodule algebra map $ι_B: B \rightarrow H$. In this paper, we study in details the case $B=O_q$, and $H$ is the quantum loop algebra ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$ for ${\mathbb K}={\mathbb C}$. Here, $O_q$ is the $q$-Onsager algebra with four presentations: (i) the $q$-Dolan-Grady type; (ii) the alternating type; (iii) the root vectors type; (iv) the Drinfeld type. For $(O_q,δ_{O_q},ε_{O_q})$, in fact a 3-parameter family of counital comodule algebras, we establish a Faddeev-Reshetikhin-Takhtajan (FRT) type presentation, which is written in terms of a K-operator satisfying a reflection algebra relation. The coaction $δ_{O_q}$ (resp. $ι_{O_q}$) sends the K-operator to a `dressed' K-operator (resp. K-matrix) using Ding-Frenkel type L-operators of ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$; the counit $ε_{O_q}$ sends the K-operator to the most general (non-diagonal) solution of the reflection equation. The FRT presentation allows to compute the image via $δ_{O_q}$ and $ι_{O_q}$ of the generating functions of $O_q$ for each presentation (ii)-(iv). Moreover, the images of Lu-Wang's generating functions of $O_q$ in the so-called Drinfeld second realization ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$ are obtained, as well as their images via the (ordinary) coproduct of ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$, which enhance two theorems by Przeździecki. Finally, we apply our FRT presentation to the construction of new type $q$-characters for ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$, in imaginary root vectors of $O_q$, refining those of Frenkel-Reshetikhin, and we explain representation-theoretic meaning of such refining.

title: Motivic Mirror Symmetry for Sink-recurrent Cluster Varieties
abstract: We prove motivic mirror symmetry for full-rank sink-recurrent cluster varieties. We allow skew-symmetrizable principal parts and invert all frozen variables. The rational geometric motive of such a variety is isomorphic to the additive orbifold motive of the mirror stack of Hu and Shende. This gives comparisons of cohomology, higher Chow groups, and algebraic $K$-theory with rational coefficients. The proof combines quantum deformation with the splitting of these motives into Tate summands. For really full-rank skew-symmetric seeds, a finite étale morphism realizes the comparison. We also study this geometric comparison in families over the projective line.

title: Quantitative global regularity for Navier--Stokes equations with odd viscosity on the cubic three-torus
abstract: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equation on the cubic torus with a constant odd-viscosity operator given by the vertical derivative of the curl. Arbitrary real, mean-zero, divergence-free initial data and an independent steady force, both in the second-order Sobolev space, admit a unique global strong solution when the magnitude of one fixed odd-viscosity coefficient is at least a norm-uniform sufficient threshold. In the unforced case the solution is smooth at positive times. The qualitative argument adapts the resonant-averaging framework for rapidly rotating fluids to the different odd-viscous dispersion. Weighted lattice counts and signed corrected-energy estimates yield a sufficient bound for the odd-to-ordinary viscosity ratio that is polynomial in the normalized initial-data radius at each fixed normalized force radius, together with a separate bound in a specified force-dominated regime. No optimality is claimed for the polynomial exponents or prefactors; determining the sharp viscosity threshold for the original equation remains open. Direct kinetic and weighted enstrophy barriers also give regularity for every coefficient on explicit bounded data and force regions, including the closed unforced ball of homogeneous second-order Fourier Sobolev radius ninety-seven fortieths times the viscosity and seven closed forced rectangles. We specify how finite certificates enter the analytic argument and distinguish minimization of a sufficient formula from sharpness for the original equation. All three main theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

title: On $\mathrm{HH}^1$ of blocks of finite simple group algebras
abstract: Let $G$ be a sporadic simple group, $k$ a field of positive characteristic and assume $B$ is a block of $kG$ with non-trivial defect. In this paper we prove the first Hochschild cohomology group $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is non-vanishing. Furthermore, we prove that for every wild block with abelian defect of a sporadic simple group, we have that $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is a solvable Lie algebra of derived length two, with non-zero maximal toral rank.

title: Delaunay Asymptotics for the Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
abstract: In dimensions $n\geq3$, we prove that near an isolated boundary singularity a positive solution of the Escobar--Yamabe equation for a smooth metric approaches a fixed periodic Delaunay solution or the cylindrical solution if its trace lies between positive multiples of $|\overline x|^{-(n-2)/2}$, where $\overline x$ is the tangential Fermi coordinate. The relative error decays at a positive power rate, with weighted estimates through two derivatives in Fermi coordinates. The necksize is unique, and the translation parameter is unique modulo the least positive period in the periodic case. The Hamiltonian smoothly parametrizes the periodic family modulo translation. We classify Jacobi fields of polynomial growth at both ends without assuming symmetry. Translation and energy differentiation generate these fields along periodic solutions, and two oscillatory fields generate them along the cylindrical solution. We also exhibit a first-order obstruction to improving these asymptotics by boundary-preserving conformal deformations of the flat models.

title: A proof of the Erdős-Herzog-Piranian lemniscate conjecture
abstract: Let $p:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n\geq 1$. In 1958, Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian conjectured that the length of the lemniscate $\{z\in\mathbb C:|p(z)|=1\}$ is maximized by $p(z)=z^n-1$. We prove this conjecture in every degree and show that equality holds precisely for $p(z)=(z-z_0)^n-e^{iθ}$, where $z_0\in\mathbb C$ and $θ\in\mathbb R$. The proof uses Möbius variations of the critical values and estimates for the inverse branches of $p$, supplemented by rigorous computer-assisted estimates in a finite range of degrees.

title: Hamiltonian Cotangent Deformations of Space Forms: Curvature Pinching, Soliton Rigidity, Conjugate Loci, and Superintegrability
abstract: We study the one-parameter family of Riemannian metrics $g_λ$ induced by the Hamiltonian cotangent deformation $H_λ= H_0 + \fracλ{2}\|J\|^2$ on simply connected space forms of constant curvature $κ\in \{1, 0, -1\}$, where $J$ is the momentum map of the isotropy action fixing a base point. The master reciprocal identity $1/f_λ^2 = 1/s_κ^2 + λ$ governing the warping function controls the geometry of the family and implies that radial geodesic acceleration is independent of $λ$. From this mechanism we derive three classes of results: (1) Curvature and rigidity: closed-form sectional curvatures, the sharp positivity trichotomy, pointwise and global Brendle-Schoen $1/4$-pinching windows on $\mathbb{S}^{n+1}$, never-Einstein rigidity for $λ\neq 0$, and the realization of Hamilton's steady cigar soliton on $(\mathbb{H}^2, g_1)$ as the unique gradient Ricci soliton in the family. (2) Dynamics and stability: iso-kinematic decoupling into unperturbed radial motion and uniform precession $Ω= λL$, closed-form Clairaut integration, the transcendental inward conjugate point law with Euclidean inversion $r_0 R^* = 1/λ$, and stratified $A_3$ cusp caustics. (3) Integrability and spectral theory: maximal superintegrable rational pericenter invariants on $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, transverse Killing rigidity on curved space forms, Fuchsian Heun spectral reduction with modulus $τ= 1 + λ/κ$, and essential spectrum gap collapse to $[0, \infty)$ on $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$. Extensions to anisotropic sphere families and intrinsic deformations of compact rank-one symmetric spaces ($\mathbb{C}P^n, \mathbb{H}P^n, \mathbb{O}P^2$) are also established.

title: A geometric Kähler--Ricci flow proof of the Calabi--Yau theorem
abstract: We give a geometric proof that every Kähler class on a compact Kähler manifold with vanishing real first Chern class contains a unique Ricci-flat metric, and that the Kähler--Ricci flow converges smoothly to this metric. The fixed Kähler class and the bounded logarithmic volume density control the mean pairwise distance. Chow's scalar-curvature decay makes available, at a fixed spatial scale and all sufficiently late times, the relative-volume comparison of Jian--Song, derived from Bamler's pointed Nash entropy estimates. This comparison upgrades the mean-distance bound to a diameter bound without an absolute lower bound for entropy. A restarted heat-gradient estimate then gives exponential decay of the Ricci potential. A parabolic Schwarz estimate and the interior estimates of Sherman--Weinkove yield smooth exponential convergence. The proof does not invoke the Calabi--Yau existence theorem or global estimates for a scalar complex Monge--Ampère equation.

title: The Minimum Canonical Volume of Threefolds of General Type
abstract: We prove the sharp lower bound $vol(X) \geq 1/420$ for every smooth complex projective threefold $X$ of general type.

title: Why the non-abelian Gyarmati--Matolcsi--Ruzsa inequality does not generally work: mechanisms and explicit examples
abstract:
For finite sets in a commutative semigroup, Gyarmati, Matolcsi and Ruzsa proved \[ |A_1+\dots+A_n|^{n-1}\ \le\ \prod_{i=1}^n|A_1+\dots+A_{i-1}+A_{i+1}+\dots+A_n| . \] They asked whether in an arbitrary group \[ |A_1\cdots A_n|^{n-1}\ \le\ \prod_{i=1}^n\ \max_{a\in A_i}\,|A_1\cdots A_{i-1}\,a\,A_{i+1}\cdots A_n| , \] where each omitted set is replaced by the largest slice obtained by fixing one of its elements. Nair, Namayandeh and Zhu proved that this inequality does not hold when $n=4$ and $G=D_4^{14}$, of group order $8^{14}$. We develop its double-coset mechanism and construct counterexamples in many other groups.
  For $n=4$, the smallest group found has order $518\,400$, namely $A_6^2\times C_2^2$; no absolute minimality is claimed. For $n=6$ there is a witness in a group of order $1728$, for $n=10$ a class-three $3$-group of order $243$ suffices, and for $n=4$ a single class-two $2$-group of order $2^{23}$ works. We also obtain torsion-free examples. The violation ratio $R_n=|A_1\cdots A_n|^{n-1}/\prod_iN_i$ is greater than one exactly when the inequality fails; explicit four-set constructions attain $R_4\approx1.29$ in $A_8^2$, and a larger ratio of about $1.43$ is reported for $A_{10}^2$.
  For every $n\ge4$, the inequality holds in all direct powers of $G$ precisely when $G$ is abelian. For $n\ge2$ the optimal exponent $θ_n$ is the infimum of $\log(\prod_iN_i)/\log|A_1\cdots A_n|$ over products of size at least two. We obtain $2\leθ_n\le n-1.0768$, and an infinite family in $C_3*C_3$ shows $θ_n\le n-1-δ$ for every $δ<5-2\log_25\approx0.3561$ and all sufficiently large $n$.

title: Learning Rate Decay Can Exponentially Accelerate SGD for Global Optimization of Nonconvex Functions
abstract: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is a workhorse algorithm for continuous optimization. It is a folk belief among deep learning practitioners that learning rate decay in SGD substantially improves performance. However, it has remained unclear whether learning rate decay offers an asymptotic advantage for global nonconvex optimization. We answer this question in the affirmative by demonstrating a natural class of nonconvex functions for which, we prove that SGD with learning rate decay requires exponentially fewer gradient queries for global optimization than SGD with any fixed learning rate in the small-step size regime. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first exponential advantage that has been demonstrated for learning rate decay. The class of functions we consider includes many popular benchmark nonconvex functions. Our results provide a robust explanatory theory for the empirically observed benefits of learning rate decay for global optimization. We show that annealing performs the non-logconcave sampling task associated to the optimization problem in polynomial time, via a novel application of weak Poincaré inequalities.

title: Functorial Homological Mirror Symmetry for Acyclic Cluster Varieties
abstract: We introduce the formalism of cluster models, a class of log Calabi-Yau varieties obtained from smooth quasi-affine toric varieties by iterated affine blowups along non-toric codimension 2 centers determined by a really full rank quiver. Cluster models include the truncated cluster varieties of Gross, Hacking, and Keel with respect to really full rank quivers, all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties, and all open toric subvarieties of $\mathbb{C}^n\times(\mathbb{C}^*)^m$. We then construct mirrors to cluster models via iterated Weinstein handle attachments to toric mirrors, so that the corresponding skeleta acquire compact pieces, and we prove homological mirror symmetry for all cluster models, compatibly with freezing, deleting, and contracting vertices of the quiver. This extends toric mirror symmetry and its naturalities beyond the cotangent bundle. In particular, we obtain homological mirror symmetry for all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties. We develop this package with a view towards conjectures of Marsh, Rietsch, and Williams about mirror symmetry for Grassmannians and closed positroid varieties. Motivated by these, we also conjecture that open positroid varieties are self-mirror. Assuming a natural ansatz, we prove this for a class of positroid varieties that includes nontrivial cells in every Grassmannian and all cells in finite-type Grassmannians. Towards this end we introduce a new combinatorial input, the notion of weak $k$-booleanness for permutations and braids.

title: A relative trace formula for the orthogonal Gan-Gross-Prasad model and the proof of its fundamental lemma
abstract: In this paper, we propose a comparison of relative trace formulas to study the Gan--Gross--Prasad conjecture. We unfold the relative trace formulas, match their regular orbits, and formulate the corresponding fundamental lemma and smooth transfer conjecture. Finally, we prove the fundamental lemma for the unit element of the Hecke algebra.

title: Stochastic Multilevel Sampling for Inverse Problems via Coarse-Space Identifiability
abstract: Sampling only part of the data reduces the cost of each iteration in an inverse problem, but can make reconstruction updates unreliable. We study stochastic multilevel sampling, which computes updates on a coarse-to-fine hierarchy of correction spaces. The guiding idea is that a small sample may support a reliable coarse-grid update even when it provides insufficient information for a fine-grid update. For quadratic objectives, we identify conditions under which corrections computed from sampled data decrease the full-data objective. In small-batch experiments with computed tomography and periodic deblurring, the stochastic multilevel method improves reconstruction accuracy over matched single-level methods. In an increasingly ill-conditioned CT refinement with a fixed number of projection angles, the single-level error increases as the image dimension grows, whereas a deep hierarchy maintains or improves accuracy and outperforms full-data single-level optimization at the same number of forward and adjoint applications. The gains persist across the tested local solvers and strengthen with deeper hierarchies. A separate known-probe ptychography study provides complementary evidence for the benefit of hierarchical corrections for nonlinear inverse problems.

title: The vector-valued Stein inequality and dimension-free R-sectoriality
abstract: For a complex Banach space \(X\), we characterise dimension-free \(R\)-sectoriality of the Walsh operator, the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator, the Laplacian, and the Poisson operator by the vector-valued Stein inequality. For each family, the dimension-free \(R\)-bound of the resolvents on the negative real axis equals the Stein constant. Consequently, the resolvent estimate on the negative real axis already implies uniform \(R\)-sectoriality at an angle strictly smaller than \(π/2\). We furthermore prove that the full and dyadic Stein properties are equivalent and that they are independent of the exponent \(1<p<\infty\) entering their definition.

title: Twisted convolution with conic support and the parabolic algebra
abstract: We prove that tempered distributions on \(\mathbb R^{2n}\) whose supports satisfy a common strict cone condition form a unital associative algebra without zero divisors under twisted convolution \(\star\). The supports may be noncompact, and the associated Weyl maps need not be bounded. As applications, we show that the parabolic algebra and the norm-closed algebra generated by positive translations and modulations have no zero divisors, confirming Levene's conjecture. We also obtain a zero-product theorem for Toeplitz operators on the one-dimensional Fock space with bounded symbols whose distributional Fourier transforms satisfy a common strict cone condition. The proof of the distribution theorem uses Schwartz smoothing between distributional Weyl maps to convert a hypothetical zero product of nonzero distributions into a smooth function \(h\not\equiv0\) satisfying the same cone condition and \(h\star h=0\). The cone bound implies the \(Q\)-support condition, meaning that some linear functional is bounded above on \(\operatorname{supp}h\) and has compact upper level sets there. Truncating \(h\) near the maximum of this functional and applying the support identity for compactly supported twisted squares rule out \(h\star h=0\). For the operator applications, uniformly bounded Weyl-conjugation averages identify twisted convolution with bounded operator composition under the common cone condition.

title: R-Function Representation and Composition for Flexibility Analysis and Robust Design Spaces
abstract: Explicit multiparametric solutions provide analytical feasibility and design-space descriptions after elimination of adjustable variables. R-functions convert these descriptions into fields whose nonnegative regions represent feasible or robust designs. The principal contribution is the analytical composition of independently derived design spaces through union, intersection with engineering restrictions, and exclusion of prohibited regions, without repeating the underlying multiparametric elimination. A support-function construction supplies the robust design fields used in this composition. A two-parameter example demonstrates how alternative configurations, a manufacturing restriction and an exclusion combine into one admissible field. The resulting representations also support geometric interrogation of external boundaries, internal interfaces and limiting uncertainty contact, illustrated by a four-parameter heat-exchanger network. Explicit MPC offers a potential further application.

title: Wolfe's Minimum-Norm-Point Method Generalizes the Simplex Method
abstract: Wolfe's method computes the point of minimum Euclidean norm in the convex hull of finitely many points. The method is parameterized by an insertion rule and it has been an open problem whether Wolfe's original rule guarantees a polynomial number of iterations (De Loera, Haddock, and Rademacher; STOC'18). We resolve this question by proving an exponential lower bound. In fact, we establish a tight connection to the simplex method for linear programming that allows us to transfer many lower bounds for simplex pivot rules to corresponding insertion rules of Wolfe's method. These include not only Wolfe's linopt rule via Dantzig's pivot rule, but also many other classical, randomized and history-based rules. As a corollary, we obtain the first exponential example for the Lawson-Hanson algorithm for nonnegative least squares, as well as PSPACE-hardness of deciding whether the linopt rule ever uses a given point.
